\textbf{Ch 25 (relationships at the close).} Sella still carried him at the half-pace from every open slate, gave every instruction to the bucket, the broom, the pot, the wool, the water and the fire and never to the basket, said \emph{the house}, moved her lips along a loaf row standing with two gaps, sent a woman to the pot with \emph{the house has said it}, told the fire it was the thaw and said \emph{The house will keep it}, stood a moment counting under her breath with the grey streak pale at her temple and did not look toward the bed; she heard the neighbour’s one-breath joining and did not join it to the empty place at his ear. Tarn took the broom only after its instruction and on Seed 25 his stroke went on over the flagstones without the half-check it had made the day before, the stones keeping the place where it had stopped, chest tight, the breath from Seed 16 unspent, the knife at the very edge of its sill and the loan uncalled. Jorra gave the men in the back room no name, came through with grey slate dust past the bent finger, spoke to the wheel and a pot and put that finger into the damper ahead of her unfinished sentence; \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed and the promise to the slate-burners was neither given nor withdrawn. Alda laid the date over the flower and said \emph{Warm and breathing} exact and not true with her sixth page and both tins shut; Mira’s second cord and Orra’s board stayed unread and not touching; Berr’s twice-wiped thumb, the soft hands at the Cross and the clerk’s uncalled measure stayed on separate trays. Dessa stayed dead and unnamed to him; Ulda was offstage. No bond changed hands: no name given, no knot counted, no tin or box opened, no sale or betrayal paid and no seventh hearing.

\textbf{Ch 26 (bonds).} Nothing changed hands across Seed 27–30. Sella still carried him at the half-pace from every open slate, gave every instruction to the bucket, broom, pot, fire, wool and water and never to the basket, said \emph{the house}, set him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without a look at his face and left the thread frozen; the private roll stayed unshown and his number was spoken by nobody. With Tarn the equality held at the place it had moved to: the seventh year pressed to the very edge of the sill, the breath from Seed 16 unspent, the stroke going on over the flagstones without the half-check while the stones kept the stopped place, neither man naming the other’s silence and the loan still uncalled. With Jorra the grey dust from men unnamed, the bent finger in the cold damper ahead of Sella’s sentence, \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed and the promise to the slate-burners ungiven; he did not look toward the bed or the basket. With Alda, Mira and Berr their records and hands stayed on their own trays: six pages and three tins shut, two cords twisted twice with neither knot counted, the twice-wiped thumb and the finger over a figure that did not know the missing hand. No name given, no knot counted, no tin or box opened, no sale, no seventh hearing and no ending.

\textbf{Ch 27 (bonds).} Nothing changed hands across Reed 1–3. Sella still carried him at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the bucket, broom, pot and fire their instructions before anybody and never the basket, said \emph{the house}, went around the space beneath the lowest rack and the missing hand’s place as wide as a pail of hot water set where a child might knock it, and at the going of the light set him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without looking at his face and left the thread frozen; her hand rested a half-beat longer than the setting needed and the grey streak showed pale. With Tarn the equality held at the place it had moved to: the seventh year pressed past the end of the planting and still held, the knife at the edge of its sill, the breath from Seed 16 unspent, and the unchecking stroke kept beside the earlier half-beat with no cause across them; the loan was not called. With Jorra the men in the back room were given no name, grey slate dust was ground past the bent finger, the damper’s double bite was read as an object joined to no kiln, and \emph{he’s not Vail} and the promise to the slate-burners stayed sealed. Mira’s not-looking was a keeping beside Orra’s board and knot-string, six pages and two tins stayed shut, Berr’s twice-wiped thumb stayed on its tray, and the foundling’s fifth half-beat at the market was not a sale. No name given, no knot counted, no tin opened, no seventh hearing and no ending.

\textbf{Ch 28 (bonds).} Nothing changed hands across Reed 4–6, and the one thing that moved did so without a hand on it. Under the Vail roof the sentence that would call Tarn’s loan came all the way to the threshold of the word for the first time and stopped there — an interval on the tray, not a payment, with no figure and no name — and he filed it beside the half-beat, the unchecking stroke and his own held breath from the market, writing no cause across any of them. Sella still carried him at the half-pace, gave the bucket, broom, pot, fire, wool and wind their instructions and never the basket, said \emph{the house}, went around the rack space and the missing hand’s place as wide as a pail of hot water set where a child might knock it, left the thread frozen and her hand resting a half-beat longer than the setting needed, and sent a woman asking the reeds’ cost to the pot. Tarn’s seventh year was pressed past the third tend and still held; Jorra’s bent finger stood in the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence while his stroke went on without the half-check, the two silences unjoined and \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed. At the Weir Mira’s second twist showed beneath the grey with neither knot counted and her board beside Orra’s not touching; Orra gave a date where a levy figure was asked, and the reed-cutter’s tally went back inside his coat unread, a third private record touching none of them. Berr read one in twelve from the clay road and took himself out of his own sentence with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}. No name, no figure, no knot, no tin, no box, no seventh hearing and no sale.

\textbf{Ch 29 (bonds).} Nothing changed hands across Reed 7–9, and the one thing that moved did so a second time without a hand on it. Under the Vail roof the sentence that would call Tarn’s loan came again all the way to the word that would call it and stopped there a second time, with no figure and no name; he filed it beside the first on the interval tray as a second interval and not a second payment, and the loan stayed uncalled while the seventh year was pressed further past its third tend and still held, the knife at the edge of its sill, the breath from Seed 16 unspent. Sella carried him at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool and the river wind, the bucket, the broom, the pot and the fire and never to the basket, said \emph{the house}, went around the clean dark line, the thaw, the rack space and the place where a hand went in and did not come back as wide as a pail of hot water set where a child might knock it, set him on his bed under the roof each dusk and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without a look at his face, left the thread frozen, her hand resting a half-beat longer than the setting needed; at the yard she sent a woman asking the reeds’ cost to the pot with \emph{the house has said it}, and at the Cross she set the basket in the moot-post’s shade and kept a half-pace from every slate. With Jorra men unnamed came before first grey, fine grey slate dust was ground small as meal past the bent finger, the full note of a pot was known before a High Kiln kiln-master and withheld, and the bent finger went into the cold damper ahead of an unfinished sentence; \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed and the promise of the name neither given nor withdrawn. At the market a third green sat at the corner of a silent woman’s mouth, with a pale line on the back of her hand where something had once been worn tight and long, and the boy held both on places of their own and joined neither to any cord, eel, door or box; three likenesses in a row wanted to become a cause and he refused the labour, which nobody in the square could see. At the Weir the reed-cutter’s grey cord went back inside his coat with its knots unread, Orra gave a date where a figure was asked and the man at the stern kept his hands off the oars, Mira’s second twist stayed twice beneath the grey with neither knot counted, and the soft-cuffed clerk kept his slate for a measure nobody called: four private records in materials no Court thumb would read, all visible and none enterable. Berr came up with green at one corner of his mouth, wiped his thumb twice, said a number goes into a slate and not into a bundle, read \emph{one in twelve, as the notice says}, called the levy and denied it with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}. Three doors down Alda laid her birth-slates before the fold, pressed the wool too long, crossed the flower unknowing, covered the sign with the date she gave Dessa, said \emph{Warm and breathing, that’s all I’ve set down} exact and not true, touched her tin unopened and left six pages unread. No name, no figure, no knot counted, no tin or box opened, no seventh hearing, no sixth sighting and no sale.

\textbf{Ch 30 (bonds).} On Days 129–131 nothing changed hands, and what moved moved without a hand on it. At the Cross on Reed 10 he watched Berr read \emph{one in twelve, as the notice says} over a crowd, call the levy and take himself out of his own sentence with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, while the true subtraction stayed in the locked box up the clay road and the heard bell stood beside the told bell, four, four and a gap, nobody crossing himself. Sella carried him at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind, the pot, the broom and the fire and never to the basket, went around the rack space with its broken birth-slates, set him on his bed under the roof each dusk and left the thread frozen. At the low angle beneath the Vail loaf shelf he saw short charcoal marks in clusters on the UNDERSIDE of the board, pressed hard and faded nearly into the grain, a keeping put where nobody thinks to look above a row kept badly on top with its two unnamed gaps. He did not read a stroke, count a cluster, copy a mark or lay the marks beside the fold’s one crust, Alda’s tin, Mira’s cords, Orra’s knot-string, Dessa’s pewter tin or the reed-cutter’s cord; he set the tally on a place of its own, advanced and unpaid, held for the far-off day a hand not his lays the district’s private records together (T100 planted). On Reed 11 Tarn brought the sentence about an ear worth more than the debt a \textbf{third} time to the word that would call the loan and stopped, drawing the breath he did not spend; the boy filed a third interval and not a third payment, refusing to let three stoppings stand up and call themselves a doctrine. On Reed 12 Sella put a finger beneath the board and brought it away without looking or a word; he saw the hand and made no cause of the habit. At the Weir the reed-cutter tied a knot with his teeth and put the cord back unread, Orra gave a date where a figure was asked and the man at the stern kept his hands off the oars, Mira’s second twist stayed twice beneath the grey, and the soft-cuffed clerk kept his slate for a measure nobody called: private records in materials no Court thumb will read, all visible and none entered. No name, figure, knot or loaf crossed the basket; no seventh hearing, no sixth sighting and no sale.

\textbf{Ch 31 (bonds).} Through Days 132–134 nothing changed hands. Sella carried him at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind, the pot, the broom and the fire and never to the basket, said \emph{the house}, set him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without looking at his face and left the thread frozen; twice, on Day 132 and again on Day 134, she reached a finger beneath the loaf shelf where the charcoal tally lies, without looking and without a word, and did not go back to the shelf. He did not read the marks, count them, lay them beside the two gaps above or the crust in the fold, or make a cause of the hand that goes under without looking. At the hearth on Day 133 Tarn brought the sentence about an ear worth more than the debt that holds it a \textbf{fourth} time to the word that would call the loan and stopped there with no figure and no name, drawing the breath he did not spend; Sella, within hearing, gave the end of her instruction to the pot and asked nothing, Jorra did not ask about the ear and Tarn did not ask about the room, and the two silences stayed unjoined. Jorra’s grey dust came out of the back room before first grey from men he did not name, his bent finger went into the cold damper ahead of her unfinished sentence, and the full note was known before a High Kiln kiln-master and withheld; \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed. At the Weir the reed-cutter’s cord, Orra’s date and knot-string and Mira’s two cords stood as private records in materials no Court thumb could spell, all visible and none entered. At the Cross a fourth green at a silent woman’s mouth was filed as a colour and not a name, five shapes counting Berr’s glaze, joined to no ear; Berr bought eels two marks short, said \emph{A number goes into a slate, not a bundle}, took himself out of his own sentence with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, and went off with the box locked. No name given, no knot counted, no sale, no seventh hearing and no ending.

\textbf{Ch 32 (bonds).} Through Days 135–137 nothing changed hands. Sella carried him at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket, reached a finger beneath the loaf shelf on Day 135 without looking, and set him on his bed at the going of the light on Day 137 with the fold righted without a look at his face; she still has not said whose child he is. Tarn brought the sentence about the ear under this roof a fifth time to the word that would call the loan and stopped there with no figure and no name, drew the breath and did not spend it, and Jorra did not ask about the ear while Tarn did not ask about the room. Jorra’s grey dust came out of the back room on Day 136 and his bent finger moved the damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence; Mira’s second twist stayed twice beneath the grey at the Weir and the fish-trade shade with her board beside Orra’s and not touching; Orra gave a date where a figure was asked and kept the forty-first double turn legible and unnamed; Berr took two pair of eels and paid two marks short with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, and his box stayed locked. Dessa stayed dead and unnamed, Alda’s six pages and both tins and Dessa’s pewter tin stayed shut offstage, Marra was not in Sill, Ulda and the green-mouthed woman were offstage, and no sixth sighting, no seventh hearing, no knot counted, no tin opened and no sale given.

\textbf{Ch 33 (bonds).} With Sella nothing changed hands across Reed 19–21: the half-pace from every open slate, the instruction to the wool, the river wind, the pot, the broom and the fire and never to the basket, \emph{the house} where another woman would say \emph{I}, the bed under the roof and not the Debt Loft, the fold put right without a look at his face, the thread left frozen, the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand. On Day 138 she reached a finger beneath the loaf shelf without looking or a word, and on Day 140 she gave no name to the men who went into the back room and did not say the room was cold; within hearing of Tarn’s sixth stopping she ended her instruction at the pot and asked nothing. With Tarn the equality held at the place it had moved to --- two ears, two silences, a loan that can hear and has never been called --- and the sixth stopping cost him a breath he did not spend while his stroke went on over the flagstones without the half-check. With Jorra the dust, the wheel spoken to first, the full note withheld from the High Kiln master and the bent finger in the damper ahead of her unfinished sentence went unasked about; \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed and the promise of the name was neither given nor withdrawn. With Mira and Orra nothing was counted or joined: their boards lay side by side and did not touch, Mira’s second twist twice beneath the grey, Orra’s forty-first double turn legible and unnamed. Berr read one in twelve at the second Account-day, paid two marks short and went up the road believing he had done a kindness, the true subtraction locked in his box. The green-mouthed woman of Day 139 was the fifth at a mouth and the sixth shape of the colour, a colour and not a name, never Fenna in the narration; Alda’s six pages and both tins and Dessa’s pewter tin stayed shut offstage, Marra was not in Sill, Ulda and the watcher were offstage, and no sixth sighting, no seventh hearing, no knot counted, no tin or box opened and no sale came.

\textbf{Ch 34 (bonds).} Across Reed 22–24 nothing changed hands and no hand was laid across another keeping. Sella still carried him at the half-pace, gave the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket, set him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without looking at his face, left the thread frozen and the pot handle two inches beyond his reaching hand, and let her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needed; on Days 141 and 143 she reached a finger beneath the loaf shelf without a word and the charcoal stayed unread, the widow’s mark untouched because a shelf and an afternoon and a dusk are not openings. A neighbour at the shelf on Day 141 named the row’s old gap and the empty place at his ear under one appetite in a single breath, a further shaping of T097 held on a place of its own, advanced and not paid, with no third gap and no joining. At the hearth on Day 142 Tarn told the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} and brought the ear-sentence a seventh time to the word that would call the loan, stopping there with no figure and no name; the loan stayed uncalled and the seventh year stood one tend from its end. Jorra’s grey dust, his wheel spoken to first, the pot’s full note withheld from the High Kiln kiln-master and his bent finger in the cold damper went unasked about; \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed. Berr read one in twelve at the Cross, took himself out of his own sentence with \emph{your house}, paid two marks short and went off with the box locked. At the Weir on Day 143 Orra’s readable unnamed double turn, Mira’s second twist and the reed-cutter’s knotted cord stood within a dozen paces of the basket, visible and none enterable, and below the sill the dark foot was still the cold to one woman and weather to the yard. No knot counted, no name given, no tin or box opened, no sale and no ending.

\textbf{Ch 35 (bonds).} Sella still carried him at the half-pace and gave every instruction to the wool, the wind, the pot, the broom and the fire and never to the basket, reached a finger beneath the loaf shelf on Day 144 without looking, and set the pot handle two inches beyond his reaching hand at dusk; she has still not said whose child he is. Tarn’s eighth stopping at the word on Day 145 was brought to the threshold with no figure and no name and the loan stayed uncalled; he asked nothing within hearing, as Jorra asked nothing about the ear and Tarn nothing about the room, the two silences unjoined. Jorra came through on Day 145 with grey slate dust past the bent finger, spoke to the wheel and a pot, withheld the full note from a High Kiln kiln-master and put that finger into the cold damper ahead of her sentence; \emph{he’s not Vail} and the promise to the slate-burners stayed as they were. Mira and Orra kept their cords and knots side by side at the Weir on Days 145 and 146, neither counted, neither carried to a door; the cold foot below the sill stayed the cold to one woman and weather to the yard. Three doors down Alda crossed the flower unknowing, covered it with the date she gave Dessa and said \emph{Warm and breathing} exact and not true over a death no living person can correct; her sixth page and both tins stayed shut. No bond changed hands: no name given, no knot counted, no tin or box opened, no loan called.

\textbf{Ch 37 (bonds).} No bond changed hands in the first three days of Tallow. Sella touched the widow’s mark before the kiln mouth on Day 150 and went straight back to setting pots, and the opening made no more of him than a basket set out of the draught; Tarn’s sentence came up to the threshold on Day 152 and stopped short of it, so the loan that can hear was still uncalled; Jorra’s knowing of a pot’s full note went to the near-full tray and not among the hearings; Mira’s and Orra’s boards stayed side by side and not touching; the foundling stayed offstage with his sixth glimpse gathering interest and no loaf, slate or sale. The crust two inches from his ear remained stiff, unnamed and out of reach, and nobody under any roof said how old he was.

\textbf{Ch 38 (bonds).} No bond changed hands across the seven days of Tallow 4–10. Sella still carried him at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot and the broom and never to the basket, and brought him home from the first Account-day at the going of the light saying nothing about what had been read over him; the two rooms did not touch. Tarn took the broom only after it was instructed, and his ear-sentence did not come up at all in these seven days, so no tenth stopping stood up to join the nine and the loan stayed uncalled; Jorra’s knowing of a pot’s full note went to the near-full tray and not among the hearings, and neither man asked about the other’s silence. At the Weir on Day 155 Mira’s board lay beside Orra’s and did not touch it, with the reed-cutter’s cord a third record along the same boards unread. The one new shape was Hessa Rale, a slate-runner from Slate Row who carried Berr’s narrow slate edge-on between the Cross and Greybank; her hand went to the slate before her eyes went to the yard, and the boy filed that order as an eighth record-first hand on a place of its own, not joined to Marra, the clerks, the cutter, the twice-wiped thumb or the finger beneath the shelf. No figure came off her slate and no private keeping was opened. The foundling stayed offstage with his sixth glimpse gathering interest, and no loaf, slate or sale was paid.

\textbf{Ch 39 (bonds).} No bond changed hands across the three lived days. Sella still carried him at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, sent the wet-pot neighbours’ cost to the pot without a figure, put him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, and went to her own bed in the room that does not touch his; on Day 161 she let her unfinished sentence at the damper finish instead of having Jorra’s finger finish it for her, and nobody said a word of the waiting. Jorra’s fraction is held and unspoken, not a reconciliation, not a hearing, not a payment: \emph{he’s not Vail} stays sealed and the promise of the foundling’s name stays ungiven; Tarn’s ear-sentence went to his teeth and no further, his stroke over the flagstones without the half-check, the ninth stopping still nine with no tenth and the loan uncalled, the two silences unjoined. Downriver at the Weir Mira answered a figure with a saying and did not look into the basket; Orra gave a date where a figure was asked and the boy did not decide whether her thumb’s return was a lie or the habit of counting. Hessa Rale stayed offstage, her narrow slate unread; the foundling stayed offstage with his sixth glimpse unspent, the green never Fenna in narration, and Dessa dead and unnamed to him.

\textbf{Ch 40 (bonds).} Nothing changed hands under the Vail roof or at the Cross across seven lived days. Sella still gave every instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, said \emph{the house}, kept the half-pace, left the widow’s mark where it hung at a morning, a shelf, a hearth, a dusk, a road and a square, rested her hand a half-beat longer at the setting and set the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand; on Day 166 she held a finger beneath the loaf shelf for one counted breath and gave no word, and the boy kept the held beat on its own place (T100 advanced, not paid). Jorra came through on Day 164 with slate dust ground small as meal, withheld a pot’s full note from a High Kiln kiln-master, no pot lost, and when Sella’s voice went low his bent finger waited at the damper for her sentence to finish, the Day 161 fraction held and unspoken (T062). Tarn took the broom only after it was instructed, told the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count}, kept nine stoppings as objects with no tenth and the loan uncalled, and said nothing of the waiting at the iron. Berr read the printed figure at the second Account-day, denied the levy with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, and went off with the box locked and the true subtraction inside; the figure read was still not the figure paid. Hessa carried his slate up the clay road edge-on with her figure unread and was joined to no other hand; Mira at the Weir and Orra with her date kept their records on boards that did not touch. No name given, no bond paid, no secret sold.

\textbf{Ch 41 (bonds).} Nothing changed hands under the Vail roof across the last working week. Sella still gave every instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, said \emph{the house}, kept her half-pace, left the widow’s mark where it hung at a morning, a shelf and a dusk, set the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and let her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needed; on all three days her eye went once to the clay jar cold under its glaze and her hand shut half over nothing without touching it, and her finger did not go beneath the loaf shelf. Jorra came through on Day 171 with slate dust ground small as meal past the bent finger, spoke to the wheel, told a pot \emph{You’ll do}, withheld its full note from a High Kiln kiln-master who said a pot singing early generally sings itself out early, no pot lost, and held his bent finger in the cold damper until Sella’s sentence finished. Tarn took the broom only after it was instructed, said \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late, six counted where the house can check and the seventh held where it cannot, the ear-sentence to his teeth on Day 172 and no further, no tenth standing and the loan uncalled; and while Jorra’s finger stood in the iron his broom checked half a beat behind it on the flagstones and went on without a word or a turn of the head. The boy filed that third movement on a place of its own beside the Day 161 fraction at the damper and the Day 166 held beat beneath the shelf and forbade the three to stand up as a rule. The crust stayed stiff two inches from his ear with its empty place unnamed, the two rooms did not touch, and the costs of the week went to pots, weather and rivers without a figure. \emph{He’s not Vail} stays sealed, the foundling’s name ungiven, no bond paid and no payer named.

\textbf{Ch 42 (bonds).} Nothing changed hands across the firing month’s last seven days. Sella still carried him at the half-pace, gave every instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, said the house, kept the widow’s mark untouched at every shelf, well, rack, road, basket, market, post and dusk, and on Day 179 set him in the moot-post’s shade where no slate lay without a word to the basket about the turn. Tarn kept six counted and the seventh held, nine stoppings with no tenth and the loan uncalled; Jorra kept his dust, his withheld note and his waiting finger, \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed; Berr went off with the box locked and his good reason intact; Hessa carried the slate unread to Greybank. No name given, no bond paid, no secret sold, no seventh hearing, no sale.

\textbf{Ch 43 (bonds).} Through Ember 1–3 nothing changed hands under the Vail roof and nobody said what the number counted. Sella gave every instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, said \emph{the house}, kept her half-pace, glanced once at the clay jar without touching it, set the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and let her hand rest a half-beat longer at the setting; on the morning of Day 180, before the kiln, she touched the widow’s mark, held it one breath, lifted the clay lid and tipped the carried coal under a broken pot, and did not touch the mark again at any shelf, well, rack, road, basket, afternoon or dusk, and nobody praised the opening or saw what it mended. Tarn took the broom only after it was instructed, six counted where the house can check and the seventh held where it cannot, the ear-sentence at his teeth on all three days and no further, nine stoppings still nine objects, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled; Jorra gave the men who came before first grey on Days 181 and 182 no name, kept his dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray, withheld the full note from a High Kiln kiln-master on the wrong wind, and held his bent finger in the cold damper until Sella’s sentence reached the pot, the fraction held and unspoken. The three held changes stayed on three separate places, the two shut-room tellings at two, the charcoal unread and the two rooms that do not touch untouched. No bond paid or spoken, no name given, no secret sold and no payer named.

\textbf{Ch 44 (bonds).} Through Ember 4–6 nothing changed hands under the Vail roof and nobody said what the number counted. Sella gave every instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, said \emph{the house}, kept her half-pace, glanced once at the clay jar cold under its glaze without touching it, set the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with the half-beat at setting, sent a neighbour’s cost to the pot and the weather, and left the widow’s mark where it hung, because a morning and a shelf are not openings and the one opening was before the kiln on Ember 1. Tarn took the broom only after it was instructed, six counted where the house can check and the seventh held at the lip, Garl’s unforged sentence beside the knife, the ear-sentence short of the word that would call the loan on all three days, nine stoppings still nine objects with no tenth before the seventh year was earned, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled. His one act of the week was private and unreconciled: on Day 183 he took the warm stone out of its pot in the Debt Loft, set it on the sill in the light, looked at it and put it back, still cold, not forgiven; the boy heard only the scrape of a pot’s foot from a room he cannot enter and kept it on a fourth place of its own. Jorra gave the men who came before first grey on Days 184 and 185 no name, kept his dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray, withheld the full note from a man on a wrong wind who said a pot singing early generally sings itself out early, no pot lost, and had his bent finger standing in the cold damper on both days as a remembered holding and not a new change. The three held changes stayed on three separate places, the two shut-room tellings at two, the charcoal unread and the two rooms that do not touch untouched. No bond paid or spoken, no name given, no secret sold, no payer named and no new scar, possession or change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 45 (bonds).} Through Ember 7–9 nothing changed hands under the Vail roof and nobody said what the number counted. Sella gave every instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, said \emph{the house}, kept her half-pace, glanced once at the clay jar cold under its glaze without touching it, set the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with the half-beat at setting, and left the widow’s mark where it hung, because a morning, a shelf, a rack and a dusk are not openings and the one opening was before the kiln on Ember 1. On Day 187 a neighbour with a wet pot asked what the firing cost; she sent her to the pot and the weather with \emph{Ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there. The house has said it}, and nothing was priced, refused or entered. On Day 188 she set the basket at the yard’s edge, turned his face as she would turn a pot to the light and went wide around the place the carriers crossed, giving no name for what ailed the man. Tarn kept six counted and the seventh held, brought the ear-sentence to the threshold of the word that calls the loan on all three days and stopped with no figure and no name, his stroke over the flagstones without the half-check and Garl’s unforged sentence beside the knife; the loan stayed uncalled. Jorra gave the men in the back room no name, knew the full note of a pot three turns ahead and withheld it from a man on a wrong wind, and held his bent finger in the cold damper until her unfinished sentence reached the pot, the fraction a remembered holding and not a new change; the two silences stayed unjoined. The old life stayed offstage and no bond changed hands: no name given, no tin or box opened, no figure paid, no collector called.

\textbf{Ch 46 (bonds).} Through Ember 10–12 nothing changed hands under the Vail roof and nobody said what the number counted. Sella gave every instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom, the running water and the river wind and never to the basket, said \emph{the house} and \emph{The house will keep it}, kept her half-pace and her jar-glance without a touch, set the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with the half-beat at setting, and left the mark where it hung, because a market and a reading are not openings and the one opening was before the kiln on Ember 1. On Day 189 she stood half a pace off at the moot-post shade through the reading and the bell; on Days 190 and 191 women’s cost-questions went to the pot and the weather. Berr read Ember’s first \emph{one in twelve, as the notice says} over the basket, said \emph{The levy is called. It is not called by me} and \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, and went off up the clay road with the box locked and the true subtraction inside, believing he had done a kindness; Hessa carried his slate up the road edge-on and unread. The reading did not answer the man carried out on Day 188: no figure, collector or slate knew what he cost, and the pale line stayed on a place of its own. Tarn held six counted and the seventh at the lip, the ear-sentence short of the word that calls the loan, nine stoppings with no tenth and the Seed 16 breath unspent; Jorra’s dust and withheld note, his remembered holding at the damper and the two shut-room tellings stood as they had. No name given, no tin or box opened, no collector called and no payer named.

\textbf{Ch 48 (bonds).} With Sella nothing changed hands across three days: the instruction to the wool, fire, pot, broom and running water and never the basket, \emph{the house}, the half-pace, the jar-glance without a touch, gruel from the house’s own dish with his mouth unwiped, the pot handle two inches beyond his hand with the half-beat at setting, the mark untouched, and the two rooms that do not touch. With Tarn the equality held at the place it had moved to — six counted and the seventh at the lip, the ear-sentence at the threshold of the word that would call the loan, nine stoppings with no tenth, the Seed 16 breath unspent, no collector — and the boy did not join his own held inch to Tarn’s held breath. With Jorra the dust and the withheld note and the finger waiting in the damper stood as before, \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed and the promise ungiven, and the sweet edge on the wrong wind was not made to answer the man carried out on Day 188. The old life stayed offstage: no present-tense break, no `**` tag, no name looked for. No bond paid, sold or spoken; no new scar or possession.

\textbf{Ch 51 (bonds).} With Sella nothing changed hands across Days 204–206: every instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom, the running water and the river wind and never the basket, \emph{the house}, the half-pace, the jar-glance and hand shut half over nothing without a touch, gruel from the house’s own dish with his mouth unwiped, the pot handle two inches beyond his hand with a half-beat at the setting and no look toward the bed, her lips along a two-gapped row with no figure, her finger kept from beneath the charcoal, the mark untouched, and the two rooms that do not touch. \item \textbf{Ch 79 (bonds).} Sella still carried him at the half-pace from every open slate, went to the fire before the basket on all three mornings, gave every instruction to the fire, the wool, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, said \emph{the house} and \emph{The house will keep it}, kept her finger on top of the shelf’s front edge so the charcoal stayed unread, turned the dressed grain beneath the wool with a lighter touch and no figure, set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, put the fold right without a look at his face, left the thread frozen and touched the widow’s mark at no hour, because a morning, an afternoon and a going of the light are not openings. On Frost 20 she set the basket in the moot-post’s finger’s width of thin shade where no slate lay and stood half a pace off through the twice-read figure and the bell, and carried him home at the going of the light saying nothing of what had been read over him. Tarn brought the ear-sentence to the calling word and stopped on all three mornings as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth, kept six where the house could check and the seventh at the lip, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled. Jorra parted dusty forearms from clean, spoke to the wheel and a pot before any person, put his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence, gave the unnamed back-room men no name and kept \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed and the promise of the boy’s name neither given nor withdrawn. Berr read one in twelve twice over the basket on Frost 20 — once for the moot and once for the households that came late — called the levy, denied it with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, and went off up the clay road with the box locked and Frost’s second true subtraction inside, believing he had done a kindness; the printed figure stood unchallenged and the figure read was still not the figure paid. Hessa carried his slate up toward Greybank before noon, edge-on and unread, answering the question put and not the one behind it with \emph{I don’t read it. I carry it. There’s a difference, and the road doesn’t care which}; the Frost 14 saying gathered a second shaping from an ownerless voice over the boards and well-roof on Frost 19, filed beside the first and Hessa’s eighth hand with a finger between, not a witness, not a cause, not a joining and not paid, and Hessa was not made a reader. Garl stayed in objects with his name unspoken two hundred and eighty-eight through two hundred and ninety days and his tile debt uncalled; Ilva was offstage on all three days with her ninth strip unread and her ninth hand nine. The soft-cuffed clerk stayed set at the out-of-line landing for a measure nobody called; the green-mouthed woman and the foundling stayed sightings at the market with no eighth of either. No bond changed hands, no name given, no debt paid, no secret sold; no new scar or possession and no change of voice.

\item \textbf{Ch 83 (bonds).} Through Days 300–302 nothing changed hands with anyone under the roof, in the yard or on the clay road. Sella went to the fire before the basket at every morning and going of the light, gave every instruction to the fire, the wool, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, said \emph{the house} and \emph{The house will keep it}, kept her finger above the charcoal and her lips along the two-gapped row, glanced once at the clay jar and shut her hand half over nothing, turned the dressed grain beneath the wool with a progressively lighter touch and no figure, set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and on Bone 2, before the basket, touched the widow’s mark for one breath, lifted the clay lid with the back of a hand and tipped the carried coal under a broken pot; nobody praised the opening, named what it mended, entered a slate or made a lesson of five openings in five months, and her fire still missed its fifth under the floor with its payer unnamed three hundred and two days. Tarn kept six counted in the worn thumb-mark and the seventh at the lip beside Garl’s unforged sentence, \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count}, the ear-sentence stopped at the calling word on all three days as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, the Seed 16 breath unspent, the loan uncalled, no collector on the road, the warm stone cold and unreconciled in its loft pot by not trying, which is not forgiveness. Jorra came through with meal-fine grey dust past the bent finger and under the nails, parted dusty from clean forearms as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, spoke to the wheel and a pot before any person, withheld the note known three turns ahead on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them, gave the unnamed back-room men no name and put his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence; \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed and the promise of the boy’s name neither given nor withdrawn. Garl stayed in objects with his name unspoken three hundred, one and two days. Ilva at the well on Bone 2 answered a woman with her hand toward her sleeve and the strip unread — \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account} — and the ninth hand stayed nine. A hunter come down from Cold Acre carried a hare across his shoulders at the well on Bone 1; a woman asked what the carrying cost and he told her the weather and went off toward the north gate road, so the month’s trade came and went as a direction with no figure or entry. No bond was paid, sold, named or spoken, no new scar or possession and no change of voice.

Jorra came through with meal-fine grey dust, parted dusty forearms from clean as clot from vessel, spoke to the wheel and a pot before any person, withheld the note he knows three turns ahead, and put his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence, leaving it standing while the broom checked. No name given, no promise made, no bond paid, sold, named or spoken.

\CRsheetheading{Arc So Far}
\textbf{Ch 123 (Days 420–422, Ilmen 26–28).} Three ordinary tending days are lived one dated day at a time in six full scenes, two to a day, each opened by its own `\textbackslash{}daymark`; no market, Cross, bell, Account-day, collector or runner came on any of them, and Ilmen 30 (Day 424), the third and last reading, stands two mornings off as a date and is not brought. The surgeon takes the body in its old order — crust gone into old horn two inches from the ear, fold found where put and still a finding, thread stiff and unwiped, cold stopping at cheek, temple and wrist, Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — and the infant’s three wants quarrel without verdict, the second louder, neither winning, the quarrel the work. Count \textbf{422 exact}, six months and two hundred and forty-two days told by nobody, \textbf{420 honest answers} on the sixth place, answers 415 through 420 entered two to each of the three days, each exact, complete, worth nothing at two inches of air. \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, advanced and NOT paid (T080 with T090/T102):} on the morning of Ilmen 26 a woman waiting her turn at the yard well brought a number up out of a shut fist, held it toward the light and put the fist toward the strip in Ilva’s sleeve, saying she could put a figure to the month’s firings. Ilva’s hand went flat over the fold before her eyes went to the asker and her mouth opened after both, the half-beat lying in the gap where a lesser observer would have put an intention; she answered the question put and not the one behind it — \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account} — and put the flat of her hand once more on the sleeve. The offered figure went from fist toward wood, looked at the light and went back into the sleeve, arriving nowhere; the woman shut her fist on it, said \emph{Then it’s a stick} and went back to the round, and nobody turned twice. No slate was opened within reach of the basket, no figure came off the wood, no reader was made and no name was spoken over the notches. The boy took the order apart by the place of each part — fist, eye, mouth, the half-beat in the gap — and filed the \textbf{offer and its return} on a place of its own beside Ilva’s ninth record-first hand and the fifth shaping of the well-saying, with a finger between every pair: not a sale, a reader made, a tenth hand, a payer, an account or a sixth shaping, not the calling of the loan and not joined to the well-asking, the clerk’s entered figure, the second man’s turned slate or the face at the yard’s edge, but a reaching gathering interest toward the far-off hand that will one day lay the district’s private keepings together and not that hand. Ilva’s fear is advanced and unpaid; the count stays in wood where no clerk’s thumb can take a figure off it. Through the two following days the offer was found where put and was not offered again, made a habit, spent or joined; the well-asking was not told again, the softening at the river’s skin stayed weather, and no figure came from the fist or the note that was not a price. The three counts in three places stay three, the twelve old arithmetics are not laid across the two readings of the year, the figure read is still not the figure paid, and no key came under any roof. The fire’s fifth stays unpaid and Garl’s name unspoken 420, 421 and 422 days, the two counts side by side and not one. In the small hours the towel came out as instruments do when a case is done; six hearings stood with the seventh empty and the Drawing’s knock outside, nine record-first hands and nine stoppings with no tenth, and he did not wipe the thread or lift the crust. No sixth hearing, tenth hand, eighth opening, sixth shaping, eleventh arithmetic, signature, payer, witness or reader stood; nothing was opened, joined, named, called, paid, forgiven or ended. Forward, not closed.

\textbf{Ch 122 (Days 417–419, Ilmen 23–25).} Three ordinary tending days are lived one dated day at a time in six full scenes, two to a day, each opened by its own `\textbackslash{}daymark`; no market, Cross, bell, Account-day, collector or runner came on any of them, and Ilmen 30 (Day 424), the third and last reading, stands five mornings off as a date and is not brought. The surgeon takes the body in its old order — crust gone into old horn two inches from the ear, fold found where put and still a finding, thread stiff and unwiped, cold stopping at cheek, temple and wrist, Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — and the infant’s three wants quarrel without verdict, the second louder, neither winning, the quarrel the work. Count \textbf{419 exact}, six months and two hundred and thirty-nine days told by nobody, \textbf{414 honest answers} on the sixth place, answers 409 through 414 entered two to each of the three days, each exact, complete, worth nothing at two inches of air. \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, advanced and NOT paid (T102 with T080/T090):} on the morning of Ilmen 23 word came up once at the yard well, from mouth to mouth among the bucket-round with no body standing under it — a report and not a sighting — that a man with a narrow slate under his arm had asked after a house-name under this roof and been answered with the weather. Nobody saw the asking, no voice carried, no slate was opened within reach of the basket, no figure came off any slate, no room was entered and no name was spoken. The boy took the word apart by the order of its parts — asking, house-name asked after, weather that answered, the half-beat where a name would have stood — and filed the \textbf{asking} on a place of its own beside the second man’s direction down the north bridge road and his turned slate, the first man’s face, the clerk’s entered figure and the fifth shaping, with a finger between every pair. He gave it no name, owner, answer carried, interior, witness, sale or tenth hand and joined it to none: a reaching gathering interest toward the far-off calling and the far-off hand, \textbf{not} the calling of the loan, not a second sighting, not a sixth shaping, not a rule and not a door. It was not told again and the direction was not made a custom by being remembered; Ilva, drawing at the well, was expressly not the speaker and her strip stayed unread with her ninth hand nine. The small grammar went on: a number rose out of a shut fist, looked at the light and went back into a sleeve, arriving nowhere; a woman sent to ask a pot’s cost got a note and not a price; the called-gone grey stayed beside the left-in-place ridge, a thing left in place not a thing forgiven; the softening at the river’s skin was found where put and called weather. Sella’s grammar held at both ends of every day, Tarn’s six and seventh and Jorra’s dust and damper stayed found where put, and Garl’s name and the fire’s fifth went unpaid 417, 418 and 419 days. No present-tense break, no tagged memory, no payment, witness, reader, tenth hand or ending. Forward, not closed.

\textbf{Ch 120 (Days 411–413, Ilmen 17–19).} Three ordinary tending days are lived one dated day at a time under the Vail roof, in the Clay Yard and at the yard well, each in two full scenes, nothing crossing from one day to the next as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer. The surgeon takes the body in its old order — the crust leathery and hardened into old horn through another dry night, the fold found where put, the thread stiff and unwiped, cold stopping at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint, the Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — and the infant’s three wants quarrel without verdict, the second louder, neither winning; count \textbf{413 exact}, six months and two hundred and thirty-one through two hundred and thirty-three days told by nobody, \textbf{402 honest answers} on the sixth place, answers 397 through 402 entered two to each day, each exact, complete, worth nothing at two inches of air. \textbf{The chapter’s two changes, both advanced and NOT paid:} (T036/T076/T006) on Ilmen 18 at the kindling Tarn withholds the sentence he said on the seventeenth, keeping six where the house can check, the seventh at the lip, hand over blade and sill and away with no breath held, and says it again on the nineteenth so the silence is found where put and not made a habit; the boy files the silence on a place of its own as a hand withdrawn from a field before the dressing goes on — not a tenth stopping, payment, hearing or rule, with no payer standing, and not laid across the clerk’s figure, the degree, the face at the yard’s edge or Jorra’s promise. (T083/T085/T092) on Ilmen 19 air less cold comes off the river, the sour tang of Ash thins at the Vail corner and the river’s skin softens at one edge where the low note runs nearer under it; the yard calls it weather and nobody owns the day, Sella tells the fire it is the thaw, and the boy files the softening on a place of its own beside the clean dark line and the called-gone grey, not a sign, fourth covering, sixth shaping or payment and not made again. The clerk’s entered figure, Tarn’s degree and the face stay on three places with a finger between; the fifth shaping stays on its own tray; Hessa’s eighth and Ilva’s ninth stay eight and nine with no tenth; the first arithmetic of Y.H. 814 stays up the clay road with no key under any roof and is not laid across the twelve of Y.H. 813, for paper is not a payer. Ilmen 20 (Day 414), the month’s second Account-day and market, stands one morning beyond the close as a date and is not brought. No present-tense break or tagged memory; the satisfaction in a field taken as found and left as found costs nothing, which is how he knows it is not peace. Forward, not closed.

The file lay open on the towel with every gap left gap and no number spoken to him, and Bone went on without a boundary drawn.
