\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 107: Lived Days 372–373–374, Stone 13–15, Thirdday to Fifthday, carried under the Vail kiln-house roof, down into the Clay Yard on the afternoons, to the yard well on the thirteenth, to the clay road’s edge on the fourteenth and to the kindling and wheel-shed on the afternoons, three hundred and seventy-two, seventy-three and seventy-four days old — six months and one hundred and ninety-two, ninety-three and ninety-four days — told by nobody, the count going 371 to 374 exact with \textbf{three hundred and twenty-four honest answers} standing on the sixth place (319 in the small hours of the thirteenth, 320 at its close, 321 in the small hours of the fourteenth, 322 at its close, 323 in the morning of the fifteenth and 324 in the small hours at the very end), each a small intake taken from the room whose floor does not touch his, held whole on the river’s note’s own finishing under the winter skin, let go as the note ended and the hand straight down and laid flat against the fold as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking — exact, complete, worth nothing at two inches of air, a restraint and not a payment borrowing no house count and supplying no payer. Three lived days, each in two full scenes with its own dated `\textbackslash{}daymark`, deliberately ordinary so that the evening’s keeping would register as a change: nothing from Stone 10, 11 or 12 crossed under any roof as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, the Hearth Drawing standing behind the household with its flat knock outside the six hearings and the seventh place empty, and the tenth arithmetic standing behind one unsigned figure with no doctrine out of ten. Each morning the surgeon’s register took the body in the old order — the leathery brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear with its corner a hair off the wool and its empty place unnamed and no third, the thread of drool frozen in the dry kiln heat and unwiped because nobody under any roof had ever been given an instruction about the thread, cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint as at the end of a line written out for it, the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — and he knew the order in which a body gives heat up is the reverse of the order in which it takes it back and that pink returning to a face is surface still cold and not the core, and could do nothing with the knowledge; the infant’s want of the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle quarrelled without verdict, both true, the second louder, neither winning, the quarrel the work. Sella came to the hearth before the basket at both ends of every day, told the coals it was the thaw, turned them with the back of a broken pot, said \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say I, lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack with the hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire and never to a person, turned the dressed grain under wool with no figure and no handful, kept her finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stayed unread, glanced once at the clay jar with her hand half over nothing, set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and left the widow’s mark untouched because a morning, a hearth, a shelf, a well, a yard, a road, a going of the light and a bed are not openings and no eighth opening was made due. The yard went around its seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, widest around the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out; the gone white frost, the skinned trough and the silt-clouded plate of ice stayed weather entered nowhere with a finger between every pair, and the river’s winter skin was found where put beside water over water and not spent. On the thirteenth Ilva drew at the well with the rope stiff and the clay pale in her nail crescents, her hand to her sleeve before her eyes to the asker and her mouth after both, answering \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account} with the notched birch strip unread and no figure off the wood; the boy filed her order of reaching as the \textbf{ninth} record-first hand with a finger between it and Hessa Rale’s eighth and filed no tenth, and she was expressly not the speaker of any voice. On the fourteenth Hessa came \textbf{down} the clay road out of Greybank with Berr’s narrow slate edge-on to her forearm and the writing turned toward her sleeve, the second strap let out and dried road-mud unbrushed on the shortened skirt; her hand went to the slate before her eyes to the yard and nothing pressed where the writing was, she gave no figure, read nothing aloud and did not look into the basket, and the boy filed the turning of the writing toward herself beside the Ash 6 sighting with a finger between, no reader, no witness, no fifth shaping of the Frost 14 well-saying and no payment, her eighth hand staying eight with no tenth. The four rooms with the same gap in their count — the birth room, the Vail kiln-house, the market-day slate room and the Drawing house seen two doors down — were held on a place of their own with a finger between every pair, four likenesses and not one account, an account wanting a hand to lay them together and a payer under all four and no such hand or payer standing. At the kindling on the fourteenth and fifteenth Tarn kept six in the worn thumb-mark where the house could check and the seventh at the lip beside Garl’s unforged collector sentence, the knife at the very edge of its sill, passing his hand over blade and sill and away with no breath held at the top of the reach, telling the wood \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count}, finding the Ash 14 held breath and the Bone 26 thumb’s resting where they had been put and making neither again, the pale clip-ring catching what little light there was, his chest tight since the dark and Ash worked into the knuckle creases, his stroke over the flagstones without the half-check, bringing the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stopping as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled. Jorra kept the wheel-shed edge, parted dusty forearms from clean as clot from vessel with meal-fine grey slate dust white in a fist-crease, gave no name to the men who went low into the back room before first grey, spoke to the wheel and a pot before any person, withheld the full note known three turns ahead, and let his bent finger lead into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence — one iron with two bites — taking it out without leaving the extra holding of Ash 26 a second time; \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed and the promise of the boy’s name to the men who burn slates was neither given nor withdrawn. \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, T097 with T060/T086 advanced and NOT paid:} at the going of the light on the fifteenth Sella set him on his bed at the low angle of the loaf shelf, put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and tucked the wool into the empty place beside the crust — a small keeping with no word, no third crust, no name spoken over the place, no look toward his face and no instruction to the basket, her hand resting the half-beat longer than the setting needed and the thread left frozen and unwiped. He took the interval apart by what was there and by what was not and filed it on a place of its own beside the crust’s gap, the shelf’s two gaps, the gone pan’s round ring and the field’s empty place: expressly not a joining of rooms, not a third crust, not a gift, not a payment, no payer, not a sixth held object, not a seventh or eighth, not a habit, a way, a sign, a hearing, a mending, a cause or a rule, gathered once and not made again, found where put, gathering interest toward the far-off finger that will one day lay shelf and fold together and call the joining an account — and that hand is not his and has not come. The surgeon read the movement as a hand at the edge of a wound that closes nothing, exact and worth nothing at two inches of air; the infant wanted the crust lifted and the thread wiped; both true, the second louder, neither winning. No sixth hearing, seventh opening, sixth held object, tenth hand or tenth stopping was supplied to make a row come out even, for a finding filled to make a row come out even is a finding forged. No growth in capacity, no rank, no power, no new scar or possession and no change of voice; the hand still cannot close two inches or lift his chin, and the count went on at three hundred and seventy-four exact, told by nobody. Forward, not closed.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 106: Lived Days 369–370–371, Stone 10–12, Tenthday to Secondday, carried under the Vail roof, down into the Clay Yard on all three afternoons, to the Cross on Stone 10 and to the Hearth Drawing two doors down on Stone 12, set at the edge of the light where he could see and not join; three hundred and sixty-nine, seventy and seventy-one days old — six months and one hundred and eighty-nine, ninety and ninety-one days — told by nobody, the count going 368 to 371 exact and \textbf{three hundred and eighteen honest answers} standing on the sixth place (313 in the moot-post’s shade; 314 in the small hours at the roof; 315 at the yard well’s morning; 316 at the close of Stone 11; 317 after the carry home from the Drawing; 318 in the small hours at the very end), each a small intake held whole on the river’s note’s own finishing under the ice, let go as the note ended and the hand straight down and laid flat against the fold as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking — exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, a restraint and not a payment borrowing no house count and supplying no payer, laid across none of the held objects. Stone 10 was the month’s first Account-day and market and the tenth arithmetic of the year: Berr Clay came up short off the clay road with the red cord folded, the sweet green of glaze at one mouth-corner and the smell of nothing at all, wiped his thumb twice before touching nothing, passed a finger over the figure through his sleeve, read \emph{one in twelve, as the notice says} twice over the basket — once for the moot, once for the late households — called the levy, denied it with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, said something low to the block about kindness being entered and went off with the box locked and Stone’s first true subtraction inside, believing he had done a kindness; \textbf{ten readings stand behind one unsigned figure and ten are ten and not one account}, the figure read still not the figure paid and no doctrine out of ten. Hessa took the slate up the road before noon with the writing to her sleeve and answered the question put; the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set at the out-of-line landing for an uncalled measure; the silent green-mouthed woman turned a cup a quarter and the small shape in cast-offs caught the green sliver and went dull, a seventh of each with no eighth; the bell went four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, the heard bell kept in its square beside the told. Each morning the surgeon’s register took the body in its old order — stiff brown-edged barley crust two inches off with its hair-lifted corner, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread frozen in the dry kiln heat and unwiped, nobody under any roof ever given an instruction about the thread; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint as at the end of a line written out for it; the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house will perform — and the composed face was not composure, a cold patient cannot clot and will seem better before he is worse, and rewarming must be slow and from the outside, never rubbed, never set too near the fire; the infant wanted the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle, both true, the second louder, neither winning, the quarrel the work. On Stone 11 Ilva drew at the well with the pail against her knee and answered what Stone’s firings had taken with \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account}, her hand to her sleeve before her eyes to the asker and her mouth after both, the notched birch strip unread and filed as the \textbf{ninth} record-first hand with a finger between it and Hessa’s eighth and no tenth; she was expressly not the speaker of any voice. \textbf{The chapter’s earned event, Stone 12’s Hearth Drawing, was rendered only from the basket at the edge of the light:} a cuff soft from washing and folded back twice, a flat leather satchel, a cold iron tube out of a roll of wool, fingertips grey the colour of skimmed milk gone off, a hand to the slate before the eyes to the bed, and the collector’s ordinary untroubled hand filed on a tray of its own and joined to none; the neighbour on the board-bed gave under the tube with a small flat knock and was left with a pale round place, not a wound and no blood, and the boy did \textbf{not} make the knock a seventh hearing, for a hearing wants a source standing and the room was seen from a basket, not entered. A rekindled child three days out of a thin return went worse on the third day — grey fingertips, red at the hairline, a pink face that was surface still cold and not the core — and the room called it a graft settling; the mother held a cup of warm milk she never drank, and the death-house women corrected the boy without knowing he had spoken. He knew the order in which a body takes heat back and the order in which it gives it up, and could not speak, reach, warm or say \emph{leave it} or \emph{warm it slowly}. He set the room beside the birth room, the Vail kiln-house and the Court’s room with a finger between every pair, wrote no cause across any of them and joined none to the burned slate, the Greybank saying or the Ash directions. Sella carried him home at the going of the light saying nothing of where they had been, set him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, let her hand rest the half-beat longer than the setting needed and left the thread frozen. Hessa carried the slate up toward Greybank unread, her hand to it before her eyes to the crowd; Ilva answered at the well on Ash 19 with her strip unread and her ninth hand nine and was expressly not the speaker of any voice; Tarn kept six and the seventh, checked the Ash 14 held breath on all three days and stopped the ear-sentence at the calling word as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth; Jorra parted dusty forearms from clean, spoke to the wheel and a pot before any person, withheld the note known three turns ahead and put his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence. At the close he lay on his bed at the low angle of the loaf shelf under the roof, awake, silent, cold, carried and untouched in every particular, one stiff crust two inches from his ear with its empty place unnamed and no third, the thread frozen and unwiped, the file open on the towel with every gap left gap. No wound, growth in capacity, rank, power, scar or possession; no answer became a reach, hearing, stopping, gift, habit or rule; the count closes at \textbf{350 exact}, six months and one hundred and seventy days told by nobody. Forward, not closed.

\end{itemize}

\item Ch 93: Lived Days 330–331–332, Ash 1–3, Firstday to Thirdday, carried under the Vail roof and down into the Clay Yard on all three days and to the kiln mouth on the second, three hundred and thirty, thirty-one and thirty-two days old — six months and one hundred and fifty, fifty-one and fifty-two days — nobody saying any figure. Body inventoried in the surgeon’s old order each morning: the stiff brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear, gone leathery in the dry kiln heat, its corner a hair off the wool, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread of drool frozen and unwiped because nobody under any roof has ever been given an instruction about the thread; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rode back, as at the end of a line written out for it; the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house will perform. He knew the composed face is not composure, that a cold patient cannot clot and must be warmed from outside and slowly, never rubbed, never set too near the fire; the infant wanted the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle, both true, the second louder, neither winning, the argument the work. Three counts stood in three places and did not become one — the carried fire’s four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have stood under the floor, its payer unnamed 330, 331 and 332 days; the boards’ four nails, four and a thumb-width knot; the river’s water over water through the finger’s-width door, never numbered among the hearings — because agreeing any two would want a payer put under both and none stood. Six hearings stood beside and never among with the seventh place empty, the heard bell stayed in its square beside the told, the told figure beside the paid with no signature between, and six arithmetics of the year with their true subtractions rode locked in Berr’s box up the clay road, six readings six and not one account, the finding kept on a place of its own with no payer and not laid across the house’s not-doings, the covered grain, the four held changes, the handful, the thumb’s resting, the two small objects of the hand or his own gaps, the edges coming near to touching and the finger going between. \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, advanced and not paid (T058/T079, T088):} on Ash 2 at the kiln mouth Sella set the basket level out of the draught where the heat came sideways and, before any instruction went to the basket and before any word, stood over him with her hands still, put her left hand to the widow’s mark at her throat — a thumb-length of lead-glazed clay with the Vail kiln scratched into it, the cord oiled where a working thumb had touched it ten thousand times, the little-door burn half-closing on the cord — held it one breath and let go, lifted the clay lid with the back of a hand and tipped the carried coal under the back of a broken pot. The fire took, answering four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should have stood, its payer unnamed three hundred and thirty-one days; \textbf{six openings in six months — Tallow 1, Ember 1, Smoke 1, Frost 2, Bone 2 and Ash 2 — are six and not a rule}, no seventh made due, nobody praising it, naming what it mended, entering a slate or making a lesson, sign, mending, cause or payer of it, the five behind not looked at again as signs or payments, and the mark not touched again at shelf, well, rack, road, basket, yard, morning, afternoon, dusk or going of the light. He took the opening by the small sounds — the scrape of the clay lid, the coal under the broken pot, the fire taking in fours with the gap — and filed it on a sixth place of its own with a finger’s width around it, noting only that the fifth pull was still missing and joining it to none. Sella kept the hearth grammar on all three mornings and at each going of the light: fire before basket, coals told the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot, \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say \emph{I}, small intake, hold and letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, finger on top of the loaf shelf with the charcoal unread, lips along a two-gapped row unfigured, one glance at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, twice-mended pot thumb-first at the wire with both proverbs to pot and fire and the crack showing, dressed grain turned under wool with a lighter touch and no figure and no handful, pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, the grey streak at her temple pale and coal-black hair pushed back with the burn-wrist. She carried him at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot and the river wind and never to the basket, and went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a step and no number; the three coverings stayed weather entered nowhere with a finger between every pair, and the month’s hunts and repairs stayed directions judged by the carrying arm and the weather, never figures. Tarn kept six where the house could check and the seventh at the lip beside Garl’s unforged collector sentence, the knife at the very edge of its sill, the ear-sentence brought to the word that would call the loan and stopped as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth, the Seed 16 breath unspent, his chest tight, Ash in the knuckle creases the colour of the clean dark line, the pale clip-ring holding light, his stroke over the bright patch without the half-check, the warm loft stone cold in its unmarked pot, the thumb’s resting of Bone 26 checked and not made again on any of the three days, and \emph{Yes, house} to an early and a late thaw with the late kept because it puts off the paying. Jorra parted dusty forearms from clean as clot from vessel, spoke to the wheel and a pot before any person, withheld the full note known three turns ahead from any High Kiln master who would make a song of it, set his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence, read one iron with two bites and no Grathic word for both mercies, kept \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed and the promise to the men who burn slates neither given nor withdrawn, and let the burned slate stand at five. On Ash 2 Ilva drew at the well with the rope stiff in the Ash cold, clay pale in her nail crescents and rack dust in one thumb seam, and to a woman asking what the firings of Ash had taken answered \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account}, her hand to her sleeve and the notched strip unread; the boy filed the order of reaching as the ninth record-first hand with a finger between it and Hessa Rale’s eighth, filed no tenth, made no figure of the open slate a pace away and joined her keeping to none (T080 advanced, not paid). Garl stayed in objects on all three days — salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease, hollow wheel-seat, clean dark line and finer grey called the thaw unswept, twice-mended pot with the hairline of the original break showing between staple and wire, both proverbs gone to pot and fire and never to a person — his name unspoken 330, 331 and 332 days and his tile debt uncalled. The hand answered six times, 235 in the first light of Ash 1, 236 at its close, 237 after the opening on Ash 2, 238 at that close, 239 on Ash 3’s morning and 240 at the very end, each a small intake from the room whose floor does not touch his, held whole on the river’s low note and let go on that note and straight down as a tool put away where the next hand will find it, the note having done before the hand came down so neither early again nor stayed, borrowing no house count and supplying no payer, laid across neither the six arithmetics, the bell’s gap, the covered grain, the handful, the thumb’s resting, the stayed object, the early letting-go, the sixth opening nor his own gaps. \textbf{Two hundred and forty honest answers} stood on the sixth place at the close, each an object and not a power, and neither the number nor the small hand-movings stood up and called themselves a doctrine, for a doctrine is an account that has found a payer and none stood. \textbf{Three hundred and thirty-two stood exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody} in Low Kiln, Sill and Grath; six months and one hundred and fifty-two days were told by nobody; the carried fire’s fifth was unpaid the same number with its payer unnamed; Garl’s name was unspoken the same number. Nothing on Ash 3 was opened, joined, named, called, paid or ended. Forward, not closed.

The boy read a hand laid on a place a man had decided not to open and left there unopened, and filed it on a place of its own with a finger between it and the nine stoppings, the four held changes, the handful let fall at the rack end on Bone 22 and his own gaps — not a tenth stopping, not the seventh year given, not a payment, not a fifth held change, not a hearing, not a near-full answer, not a mending and not a rule, no payer standing and not made again on Bone 27, when Tarn said \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late and kept the late because it puts off the paying. Sella kept the whole hearth grammar on all three mornings, went to the fire before the basket, told the coals it was the thaw, turned them with the back of a broken pot and said \emph{The house will keep it}, kept the charcoal unread and the two gaps unfigured, glanced once at the clay jar with her hand half over nothing, lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first at the wire with both proverbs and the crack showing, turned the dressed grain under wool with no figure and lifted no handful, set the rim two inches beyond his reach with a half-beat and no look toward his face, righted the fold without a look and left the thread, touched the widow’s mark at no hour, carried him at the half-pace from every open slate around the seven walked-around places with a look and no number, and on Bone 27 set him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, her hand resting the half-beat longer than the setting needed before it went away. Ilva came once to the well on Bone 26 with the notched birch strip unread and answered the question put; Jorra kept the wheel-shed edge, parted dusty forearms from clean, spoke to the wheel and a pot before any person, withheld the note known three turns ahead, put his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence and kept \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed; Garl stayed in objects with his name unspoken 324, 325 and 326 days. The staying at the inch of Bone 15, the early letting-go of Bone 17, the handful of Bone 22 and the thumb’s resting of Bone 26 stayed four objects on four places, each a finger from every other and none made again. No wounds, no growth in capacity; the hand still cannot close the two inches to the pot handle. No power used, no rank change, no experiment, no heresy, no new scar or possession and no change of voice.

\end{itemize}

He knew the composed face that is not composure and that a cold patient cannot clot and must be warmed from outside and slowly; the infant wanted the crust lifted two inches, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle, both true, the second louder, neither winning, the argument the work. Three counts in three places did not become one (the carried fire’s four low pulls and its silent fifth, its payer unnamed 321, 322 and 323 days; the boards’ four nails, four and a knot; the river’s water over water, not numbered among the hearings), six hearings stood beside and never among with the seventh place empty, the heard bell stayed in its square beside the told, and five arithmetics stood behind one printed figure in Berr’s locked box with the finding kept on a place of its own and no payer. Six answers were filed, the two hundred and seventeenth through the two hundred and twenty-second: 217 on Bone 22’s morning, 218 at its close, 219 on Bone 23’s morning, 220 at its close, 221 on Bone 24’s morning, 222 at the very end — each a small intake from the room whose floor does not touch his, held whole on the river’s low note and laid straight back against the fold as a tool put away where the next hand will find it without looking, the note having done before the hand came down so nothing was either early again or stayed. \textbf{Two hundred and twenty-two honest answers} stand on the sixth place, each an object and not a power. \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, advanced and not paid (T077, T060/T086, T061/T082):} on Bone 22 at the rack end Sella lifted the wool from the dressed grain, took a small handful and let it fall back through her fingers onto the heap instead of spreading it, saying nothing and giving no figure; he filed it on a place of its own as one object, not a fifth held change, sign, lesson, mending, cause, sixth arithmetic or rule, with a finger between it and the four held changes and between it and his own gaps, and did not let it join the empty fingers of Bone 23 and 24, which went beside it as a keeping and not a second. No payer stood and the keeping bought nothing. On Bone 23 at the well Ilva’s hand went toward her sleeve and stayed, the notched strip unread, and she answered the question put and not the one behind it with \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account}; the boy filed her reaching as the ninth hand and no tenth, and did not join her keeping to the handful under the wool. The staying of Bone 15, the early letting-go of Bone 17, the four held changes, the burned slate at five, the row at five askings, the well-saying at three shapings, nine stoppings with no tenth and the uncalled loan all stood as they stood. Nothing was opened, joined, named, called, paid or ended; no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

Bone came on without a boundary drawn and neither habit of naming the months was corrected; no market, Cross or bell. Body inventoried in the old order each day: one stiff brown-edged crust two inches off with its unnamed empty place and no third, the thread frozen in the dry heat and unwiped, cold at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint as at the end of a written line, the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform; a cold patient cannot clot and must be warmed slowly from the outside, and the wanting of the crust two inches off is louder than the knowing, the checking being the work and not a virtue. The round three hundred went over on Bone 1 and was kept as a threshold, not spent, not spoken over the basket; the count closed at \textbf{302 exact}. The hand filed six answers, the \textbf{one hundred and seventy-fifth} through the \textbf{one hundred and eightieth}: a small intake held against the kiln’s fourth low pull and let go whole; two intakes held apart with the nearer’s early ending kept whole as an absence; a small intake at the opening held against the first low pull and not carried into the fifth; a letting-go and the fourth pull set on two places with a finger between; a held interval beside an empty interval with the finger brought down and taken up; and a small intake at the very end let go whole on the same note. Each exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, none promoted into a reach, hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, held change, key, power, freedom, gift, doctrine or rule, no payer named. The chapter’s one meaningful change was not his: on Bone 2 Sella opened the kiln with one breath to the widow’s mark and the coal under a broken pot, the fire taking in fours with the fifth still missing; he kept the fifth opening on a place of its own with a finger between, read it as a controlled reconnection paid for by a man nobody would name, and bought nothing. A Cold Acre hunter carried a hare across his shoulders at the well; asked what the carrying cost he told the weather and went off toward the north gate road, leaving no figure. Ilva answered at the well on Bone 2 with her strip unread and her ninth hand nine. The stayed frost went off the well’s north lip while the trough kept its skin and the silt-clouded plate stood out of the path of feet, all called weather. No powers used, no rank change, no experiment, no new scar or possession, no bond changed hands, nothing opened, joined, named, called, paid or ended, and no payer stood to any of it.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 80: Lived Days 291–293, Frost 22–24, Secondday to Fourthday, three dated days in six scenes, two hundred and ninety-one through two hundred and ninety-three days old — six months and one hundred and eleven through one hundred and thirteen days — nobody saying either figure under any roof. Carried in a basket under the Vail roof, awake and silent; the surgeon’s inventory exact and useless and the infant’s want of the crust two inches off louder, the checking of satisfaction by want being the work and not a virtue. No present-tense Chicago break and no tagged remembered line. The hand filed six answers, the \textbf{one hundred and fifty-seventh} through the \textbf{one hundred and sixty-second}, each exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, the hundred and sixty-second setting the held interval beside the empty interval with a finger between and refusing to stand up as a doctrine, a gift or a rule; the count closed at \textbf{293 exact}. On Frost 23 an ownerless voice over the boards and the well-roof gave the Frost 14 well-saying a \textbf{third shaping} — the slate-runner once carried a name the district spent and did not say whose — filed beside the first saying and the second shaping with a finger between every pair, not a witness, not a cause, not a confession, not a joining and not paid, and not making Hessa Rale a reader; three shapings cannot stand up as a witness, for a witness stands somewhere and can be asked and none stood. Sella, Tarn, Jorra and Garl’s objects went on in their old grammar; the row stayed at five askings, the burned slate at four, the shut-room tellings at two, the ninth stopping ungiven and the loan uncalled; Frost 30 (Day 299) stood six mornings ahead and was not brought early. No bond changed hands, no power gained, no new scar or possession.

\end{itemize}

The stayed frost on the well lip, the skinned trough and the plate of ice clouded with silt on its flat stone were called weather and entered nowhere; the dressed grain lay covered and unfigured under wool, read over on the tenth by a number that did not know its cost; Frost’s first arithmetic stayed locked in Berr’s box up the clay road with the printed one in twelve unchallenged and the figure read still not the figure paid (T083/T085 held, T077, T015/T041/T047). He added that a figure may be carried in a slate by someone who will not read it, that a voice can arrive nowhere with no owner to be asked, that a rule is an account that has found a payer and none stands, and that a letting-go kept whole is not a freedom or a gift, because a freedom wants a taker and nobody under this roof has taken anything. \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 1: Born in the front room of House Silt on Stone 7 and lived the whole day awake. Held the count of the floorboards, read Dessa’s pulse and sieve-wire scar, matched the pause in the dark hand on the birth-slate to the hand at the flare light and did not put them together, and felt the river stone go cold with nobody else in the room noticing. Wanted the breast more than he wanted the truth. Drooled, could not hold up his head, could not turn it past a point without a small animal sound, could not reach a cup, could not keep the wool on his shoulder. The clinical ear was wide awake and wholly useless.

\item Ch 2: Lived Days 2 and 3. Heard the flat note of a cup across the birth room for the first time and could neither reach the cup nor make anyone tap it; heard Des’s laugh break through in the present tense and go out; watched Alda cross the sign over his flower again without knowing it. Was carried up the Clay Yard in Sella’s bundle, counting her steps, while Alda told Dessa he had gone in the levy and the number was never spoken. Was laid on fresh straw under the Vail roof and given a bed while Tarn was given the loft; read the hollow seat, the salt coat and the Ash ridge as a man-shaped gap, and heard a second flat note from a pot without anyone naming it. The stone was left behind in House Silt; heat came back into his hands and feet; he was warmer and more watched and could say nothing about either.

\item Ch 3: Day 4, Account-day. Carried in a basket under wool from the Vail kiln-house down to the Cross, counting a hundred and nine steps and then the market’s pigs, turnips, hoops and bell. Heard \emph{one in twelve, as the notice says} spoken twice by Berr Clay and the Sill assessor’s \emph{the figure stands as read}, and stood inside the account that priced his kind without being named in it. Heard the slate’s flat note on the second and fourth hearings of the chapter --- a third vessel after the cup and the pot --- and could not lift a knuckle toward it. Ostrowski’s voice broke through in the present tense with the two duties; for one breath the market and the trauma bay were the same room; he reached for a pocket with no phone. Saw the neat hand’s stop a third time at the Court’s table, still unread. Heard Berr confirm Sella’s widow’s mark as a kindness that is entered, and knew the debt against the tiles was being spoken around. Watched Alda touch her tin, cross the sign at his wrist and cover it with a date; watched Mira ask the eel price and answer it herself without once looking at him; watched the barrow of Ash go out toward the north gate. Counted the bell four, four, a gap. Was carried back up the Clay Yard with no word spoken to him all day. Still mute, cracked, unranked, unable to read Grathic or lift a hand to his own chin.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 4: Lived Days 5 and 6. Heard the flat note a fourth time from a Vail pot through the wall and saw Tarn’s broom stop two strokes at it without a word; kept the hearing in its own place. Watched Alda reach for the slate before the child, touch the tin, cross the sign at the red edge of his wrist and write what she turned writing-down, while the neighbour’s rekindled child went grey at the fingertips and every woman corrected his knowledge of the Afterdrop with a kinder, older, wrong answer. Was carried to the Hearth Drawing in a basket set at the edge of the light; watched the collector’s cold iron tube find the place under a dying man’s arm, the exact hand that did not press, and heard the small flat knock a fifth time --- the first from a person --- and the soft sentence \emph{the measure is banked; the account stands; the return is recorded}. Knew the figure on the slate was the one the Cross had read aloud and could not reach the tube, read the writing or lift a knuckle toward it; the collector’s hand had no pause in it and he did not join it to the three. In the Chicago break the white light took the room for two sentences --- a nurse holding pressure, a hand going past a turned note toward a signature --- and went out. Reached for a pocket-place twice, found wool, did not look at the name. Kept the death-house ridge a finger’s width thicker than Vail’s, the Vail ridge, the charred slate and the barrow of grey side by side without joining them. Fed from the house’s own dish, unentered, with the coals banked, the fold put right without a look and the count four, four and a gap. Still six days old, mute, cracked, unranked, below Thin, with no power moved and nothing gained.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 5: Lived Days 7--9. On Stone 13 turned his head toward a pot \emph{before} Jorra set it down; the pot gave nothing and he kept the interval, count still five from four sources, while Tarn saw the turning and stopped his broom at the empty set-down and said nothing. Read the house’s arithmetic again --- bed under the roof, debt in the loft, a seventh year held back, the days to Kindling gone around as a closed fist --- and extended the file to the death-house bench and to the absent note. On Stone 8 was carried to the Fishstairs, where Mira flicked eel-bones, short-weighted Berr by two eels against two marks short, called the basket \emph{warm} off the slate and touched the grey cord when a figure was spoken; a collector’s cuff crossing the bridge brought two present-tense sentences of a hospital cafeteria and a wrapper eaten to the last crumb, and he counted four steps down, four, and a landing that was not a step. On Stone 9 was set in the bridge’s shade, where Dessa called the pits’ cough weather, counted nineteen into her thumb and put him among the bits without looking in, and where Mira put a brown-edged crust into the fold that he could smell but could not lift. Sella carried him home and said nothing; at dusk she banked the coals, counted her loaves twice and came back to the same place, and he lay with the crust warm at his side and his hand going up an inch and coming down --- four, four and a gap.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 6: Lived Days 10--14, Stone 16--20, ten to fourteen days old. On Stone 16 watched Tarn measure the kindling (four, four, a space where the fifth should be) and Sella move her lips along the loaves so the days to Kindling stood as a shape; Alda came at mid-morning, reached for her slate before him, touched the tin once, pressed the fold flat too long, crossed two fingers at the red edge of his wrist without knowing it, covered the sign with an unasked-for date and wrote a second note she turned writing-down into her shawl toward a floorboard he does not know. On Stone 17 Tarn went still for two breaths at \emph{you’ve done well}; a pot turned toward on the bench gave nothing and he filed a second interval beside the first, count still five from four sources; Sella named the kiln’s breath and Tarn told of the man in Mud End called merciful. On Stone 18 the number went around the yards as a fist; at the well a neighbour reached for her slate before her child and the hospital broke through in the present tense --- ceiling light at four, a chart with its note turned down, a hand going past it to a signature, a pocket holding wool where a lit phone with a name had lain --- and he looked at no name. On Stone 19 a man come up from the Ilm held ice with a dark hair running and stopping short of the edge; a woman from High Kiln said the thaw would come early and neighbours who wanted it late contradicted her; a neighbour back from the Court’s room described bench, pot, draught and gap and he kept the room in four separate places; Sella measured the ridge near two thumbs here and a finger thicker two doors down. On Stone 20, Account-day, Sella carried him down to the moot-post’s shade; the bell went four, four and a gap and nobody crossed himself; Berr read one in twelve, called the levy for the feast and said it was not called by him, went around the uncalled debt and did not look into the basket; at the Court’s table a soft-cuffed clerk laid his hand on the slate before the woman waiting and said it was entered as it stands, and the pause in the neat dark hand came a fourth time, unread and unjoined to the other three, with the Drawing collector’s hand with no pause kept apart. At dusk the coals were banked, the fold put right without a look at his face, and the cold crust left where it was put; the Five eleven days off, the household keeping the number badly and he keeping it exactly. Still mute, cracked, unranked, below Thin, carried, unable to read Grathic or lift a hand to his own chin.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 7: Lived Days 15--24, Stone 21--30, fifteen to twenty-four days old. On Stone 21 counted fuel and bread into the last tend in loaves, glances and a space, and heard a man come back from the ice with a number in a shut fist that he would not give; Sella touched the widow’s mark before the lid and at no other hour. On Stone 22 Tarn was sent for a collector for a neighbour and came back with a man whose fingertips were the colour of skimmed milk gone off and who said \emph{the measure is taken and the account stands as entered} to a slate; on the way back a carried vessel gave its flat note past the door, Tarn’s head turned a degree, and the boy filed it on the interval tray, count still five. On Stone 23 Jorra’s grey dust returned after five clean mornings and two records went hidden in one house; on Stone 24 Alda touched her tin unopened, crossed the sign at his wrist unaware, covered it with a date and turned a further note face-down toward a floorboard. On Stone 25 a pot cracked two paces from him with the flat knock and was called a pot gone wrong; he could not turn to place it and made a third interval, no sixth hearing. On Stone 26 the number for the Five went around three, two and whatever the moot gave out, and he kept one day after tonight. On Stone 27 ice-mice and the thaw argument were filed as weather; on Stone 28 Mira put a fresh crust beside the spent one, touched her grey cord and showed the second cord twisted twice, while Dessa coughed from the pits and called it weather. On Stone 29 the brooms came out and Sella measured Vail’s ridge by thumb against the death-house ridge; Garl’s coat kept its peg and the tiles’ debt was circled without a name. On Stone 30, Account-day and the year’s last market, Berr read one in twelve for the feast and said it was not called by him, the Five were three days off, and at the Court’s table the neat dark hand’s small stop came a fifth time and lay with the four unjoined; in one present-tense beat the flare light was orange on wet snow and a hand in a grey sleeve found wool where a lit phone with a name had lain, and he did not look. At dusk Sella set him on his bed under the roof, banked the coals and did not touch the mark; the fire kept four, four and a gap and Kindling was tomorrow. Still mute, cracked, unranked, below Thin, carried everywhere, unable to read Grathic or lift a hand to his own chin.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 8: Lived Days 25--30, Kindling through Ilmen 1, Y.H. 812--813, twenty-five to thirty days old. On Kindling watched the year’s fire come up the Clay Yard in a clay dish with a coal under ash, handed from hearth to hearth, and Sella tip it into the kiln after touching the widow’s mark before the opening and at no other hour; extended the count to its light --- four, four, and a place where a fifth would be if there were a fifth --- and heard the year’s first measure taken offstage with no figure spoken in the house. On Weighing heard a clean voice in a temple’s clothes read the measures, a whole return for a person not in the room and a name the household would not repeat, counted the silence after the name among the gaps, and set the Court’s room --- bench, pot, draught and a missing line heard through a doorway --- beside the birth room, the kiln-house and the death-house without writing a cause; Berr was glimpsed wiping his thumb, passing a finger over his slate and going off with his box locked. On the Long Night listened to stories of the Return with the fire out, filed the gap between question and answer, the left-out name and the stopped story with the intervals, kept the told bell’s four, four and a gap beside the heard bell in two places, and felt cold come at cheek, temple and wrist while neither breast nor crust was given. On the Remembering heard names pass along the yard and Garl’s name not spoken under the Vail roof, watched Alda lay dates where a name should stand, touch her tin once unopened and cross two fingers at the birth-flower without knowing it, and found wool in the pocket-place where a lit rectangle with a name had lain while the boat promise came in past tense, untagged; the charred slate lay untouched in the kiln ash. On the Last Day watched no third crust enter the fold, heard Mira answer a question with a question and her own answer and show the second cord twisted twice beneath the grey with the knots uncounted, and saw Sella measure both ridges with one thumb and leave the Ash where it lay. On Ilmen 1 watched the grey burned and called dealt with, found the coals still banked so the mark stayed untouched, heard Slate Row spoken of as a direction with one in twelve printed and unchallenged, and carried the count into Y.H. 813. Still cracked, mute, unranked, below Thin, carried everywhere; five hearings from four sources and no sixth, five pauses unjoined, nothing explained; his hand outside the wool went up an inch toward the warmth and came down.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 9: Lived Days 31–37, Ilmen 2–8, Y.H. 813, thirty-one to thirty-seven days old. At the yard well heard a woman say the water tasted different and a man say the ice was honeyed under the mud, and kept the shape of a change nobody would name (T085); watched Mira answer a question with a question, touch the grey cord under her apron when a figure was spoken and show the second cord twisted twice beneath it, knots uncounted (T025, T059). On Ilmen 3 watched Tarn set the small knife on its sill and announce it to the empty yard, six years counted and the seventh held back, Ash in his knuckles, wanting the late thaw that puts off the paying (T036). On Ilmen 4 watched Jorra come in from the back room with grey slate dust past the bent little finger and say nothing, filed dusty and clean forearms apart, and went around the space under the racks where whole slate should have stood (T035, T031). On Ilmen 5 watched Alda lay a date where a name should stand, touch the tin once unopened, make the two-finger sign at the birth-flower unaware, say \emph{warm and breathing} exactly and not true, and turn a fourth hidden note face-down toward a floorboard he cannot name (T007, T008, T023). On Ilmen 6 heard a pot set down out of a woman’s shadow answer nearly full --- a third sound, neither flat nor silent --- and filed it as the first earthly answer to the Stone 13 interval, advanced and not paid, while the flat hearings stayed five from four sources (T082, T061); watched Sella touch the widow’s mark before the opening and at no other hour (T079). On Ilmen 7 saw the hairline come up into the open ice of the Ilm and set it beside the missing Fishstairs step and the told bell in three places; watched Berr come back from the river with the red cord under his coat, wipe his thumb twice before touching nothing, keep a number he would not give and go off with the box locked; heard the Singing Sill note early and the well-roof argument end in weather (T083, T085, T041, T077). On Ilmen 8 stood at House Silt three doors down while Dessa coughed worse and still called it weather, got specific over four loaves and nineteen steps, smoothed the sieve-wire scar and did not look into the basket or say the number or the name; Mira passed her without looking and brought no crust; the Slip Brook ran clay-heavy a little high; and the shape of Dessa’s hand on the wicker reached in past tense, untagged, for a pocket-place and a lit rectangle with a name unlooked-at, the boat nine promises old on cold water (T008, T073, T044, T004). Carried up the yard at dusk under the Vail roof with the two crusts in the fold, no third, the carried fire under blind ash keeping four, four and a gap, his hand outside the wool up an inch toward the warmth and down. Still cracked, mute, unranked, below Thin; no power moved, no experiment, no joining.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 10: Lived Days 38–44, Ilmen 9–15, thirty-eight to forty-four days old, carried everywhere. Held on the bank at the Slip Brook while the yard lifted Dessa Silt out with their hands and no words; heard the small flat knock of a body cracked all the way through, the sixth hearing and second from a person, and filed it beside the five from four sources without joining or counting a seventh. Paid the held thumb-on-wicker detail in past tense, untagged: the grey sleeve, the small cold rectangle with a name not looked at, the boat nine promises old on cold water, the hand coming back with wool, nothing crossing. Watched Alda reach for her slate before the body and lay dates where a wonder should stand, watched the clerk at the Fishstairs set for a measure nobody had called, and filed the order of reaching apart from the other record-first hands. On Day 39 was set in the moot-post’s shade while one in twelve was read twice and the true subtraction went over the basket; kept four ways out of the square and the bell’s four, four and a gap. On Day 40 registered no collector coming for the woman in the brook and nobody naming the omission, kept the clean dark line left where it lay, and watched Tarn send his broom over the road to the Fishstairs without turning. On Day 41 saw Mira’s second cord twisted twice beneath the grey with neither knot counted, and no third crust; on Day 42 saw from the basket’s low angle the pewter tin above Dessa’s empty bed with its pale fold and thumb-rubbed lid, entering it nowhere. On Day 43 filed a green-mouthed woman looking at pots apart from Orra’s name, kept the Weir as a sixth like room with a weak board, and heard the Singing Sill early and called weather. On Day 44 heard Orra tie the forty-first knot and say \emph{forty} low into the basket and watched her watching him; he had no answer, kept the shape and the word on separate trays, and went home at dusk with both crusts still in the fold. Still cracked, mute, unranked, below Thin; no eighth hearing, no seventh pause, no power moved, nothing joined, paid or explained except a sound, a shape and a word.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 11: Days 45–47, Ilmen 16–18, forty-five to forty-seven days old. Carried below the north bridge at dawn and set out of the draught; watched a brine-gull go off upriver with a coal not yet cold and kept the subtraction nobody else kept, while the clerk at the Fishstairs put hand to slate before eye to stalls. Read the shape of Orra’s forty-first knot --- double turn, tail tucked, tied left over right, the weight of a thumb --- without its name; the word forty was not spoken again and Orra watched him watching. Watched Mira’s two cords shown with the knots uncounted and set on a board beside Orra’s without the boards touching. Under the roof watched the house’s arithmetic go on in loaves and glances and the widow’s mark touched once before an opening; watched Tarn’s knife announced and his broom sweep the collector’s road without turning, and Jorra’s bone-coloured forearms lead at the damper. On Day 46 watched Alda reach for the slate before the child, touch the tin unopened, cross the sign and cover it with a date, saying \emph{warm and breathing}, exact and not true. In the afternoon the barley smell stopped: the smoky crust was gone, and he set Sella’s, Alda’s and Mira’s hands on three places on a tray without making a cause. On Day 47 watched frost write on the well-lip, a number pass from fist to mouth to shoulder and arrive nowhere, Berr wipe his thumb twice and take himself out of his own sentence, a weir woman report the weak board, and the Singing Sill give its note early --- all called weather. Carried home at dusk with one crust in the fold and an empty place beside it. Still cracked, mute, unranked, below Thin; no power moved, no seventh hearing, no ending.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 12: Days 48–54, forty-eight to fifty-four days old, carried in the basket with one crust and an empty place in the fold. At the well frost-bloom wrote again on the lip, the oiled paper hung slack in its frame, and the two neighbours who had argued the ice fell silent; he filed the slack frame, the silence and the hairlines stopping short of the edge beside the honeyed ice and called no cause. On Account-day Berr read one in twelve over the basket and the true subtraction went unspoken while the bell went four, four and a gap. Jorra’s grey dust came back from the back room; Tarn’s head did not turn at a vessel’s note on Day 50 or at the nearly-full pot on Day 52, and the two ears kept their silence. Alda wrote a fifth note, touched the tin once unopened and covered the unaware sign with a date. A second pot answered nearly full and he filed it beside the first, advanced and not paid, with no hand to tap either. Mira’s two cords were shown side by side with knots uncounted and her board beside Orra’s not touching. More hairlines stopped short of the edge, the Singing Sill gave its note early, and the weak board at the Weir was said plainly still there and trodden by nobody. He carried the empty place through all seven days unnamed, kept six hearings beside and never among and the three hands on their tray, and his hand outside the wool went up an inch toward the warmth and came down.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 13: Lived Days 55--60, Ilmen 26--30 and Silt 1, fifty-five to sixty days old, two months at the close. At the yard well heard a man come downriver from Greybank tell how a counting room was shut in the last war and the men inside died of the breath with the damper closed, eighteen leagues east; the yard took it as history and nobody joined it to the kiln under his own roof, and he filed the saying on a tray of its own beside the told bell, the heard bell and the four-four-and-a-gap without writing a cause (T065). Carried three doors down to House Silt, saw the pewter tin above the empty bed with its pale fold and thumb-bright lid, and watched Alda lay the birth-slates writing-down before the fold, press it too long, cross the sign at the flower’s red edge unaware and cover it with a date, say \emph{warm and breathing} exactly and not true, touch her tin unopened and write no sixth note (T089, T007, T008). Kept the exact three days to Silt while the house kept them in loaves and glances, and watched the yard prepare a sweeping already done while Sella laid one thumb in the clean dark line and the same thumb in the death-house ridge without fetching a broom (T071, T013). At the last market watched Berr wipe his thumb twice and read one in twelve twice over the basket, the soft-cuffed clerk glimpsed hand-to-slate-before-eyes and silent, Mira answer a question with her own answer, touch her grey cord with the second twisted twice beneath it, show knots uncounted, keep her board beside Orra’s without touching it and bring no crust; a barrow of grey went out toward the Bone Orchard unread (T015, T090, T059, T013). On Silt 1 watched a new hairline of grey gather beside the clean dark line and Sella stand over it with a broom and call it thaw, and set the new grey and the left-in-place line on two places that did not touch (T092). Carried home at dusk with one crust in the fold and the empty place beside it unnamed, the river beginning to move under the ice, the six hearings still six and no seventh, his hand up an inch toward the new grey and down.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 14: Days 61–67. Carried everywhere at sixty-one through sixty-seven days old and kept the count exactly while nobody gave a figure; heard water going over water behind the racks and filed it as a fifth low thing, not a hearing; held six hearings, three near-full answers (a third filed on Silt 6), three intervals, the word, the knot’s shape and the weight of a thumb on separate trays and joined none; watched Sella keep her half-pace and touch the widow’s mark at no hour in seven days, Tarn announce his knife and check the cracked-pot place, Jorra bring dust out of the back room and move the damper ahead of her sentence; in House Silt saw the sixth note written and turned down and the pale stone gone, both unmentioned; heard Mira’s figure and cord and Berr’s twice-wiped thumb at the Fishstairs; on Silt 8 lay with one crust and the empty place, the honeyed ice and the current in veins, and his hand up an inch toward the water and down. Nothing joined, paid, explained or ended.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 15: Days 68–74, Silt 9–15, sixty-eight to seventy-four days old, carried at the half-pace through the flood. Heard the district’s note --- a low turning of many small failures inside one slow certain one, a vessel of enormous capacity with a thin place nobody would name --- under the four low sounds, and filed the coming and the going with no word and no cause. Below the sill read the child’s cold foot as the extremity going before the core, the afterdrop waiting on the far side of a warming he could not perform, and could not put a hand two paces out; the woman called it the cold, the yard called the water weather, and no cause or cure was spoken. On Account-day watched Berr wipe his thumb twice, read one in twelve over the standing water, take himself out of his own sentence and go off with the box locked; the true subtraction went over the basket and the number went from fist to mouth to shoulder and arrived nowhere. Watched the water go around the clean dark line at the Vail corner and the burned line two doors down, and Sella stand over both lines and the new finer grey with a broom and sweep neither while telling the fire it was the thaw. Saw Mira’s second cord twisted twice beneath the grey with neither knot counted, Orra standing at the flood’s edge with her board and cord and no answer, and Alda’s sixth page and the tin above the empty bed stay shut three doors down. Saw Tarn’s knife on its sill with the seventh nearly gone and his head not turning at a vessel’s note; saw Jorra’s grey dust on Silt 14 and his clean bone-coloured forearms on Silt 15, the damper moved ahead of Sella’s sentence and \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed. Kept six hearings, three near-full answers, three intervals, the word, the knot’s shape, the weight of a thumb, four low sounds and a fifth thing that was not a hearing on trays that did not touch; kept one crust in the fold with the empty place unnamed; crossed into Silt 16 with the count unspent. No experiment, no rank change, no recognition, no ending.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 16: Days 75–77, Silt 16–18, seventy-five to seventy-seven days old. Kept the exact count against the house’s bad arithmetic through three days of sweeping around what the flood left; at the well watched a small foundling in cast-offs finish a kiln-hand’s sentence, turn his head toward a pot a half-beat after the boy’s, rub a green sliver and take a warm loaf from a man from Slate Row with no slate between them, and filed the delay, the loaf and the unfinished sentence separately with no cause written. At the Fishstairs saw the steps come back four, four and a landing out of line that nobody made a fall of, the soft-cuffed clerk still set, Mira’s second cord twisted twice with neither knot counted and her board beside Orra’s not touching. Three doors down watched Alda lay her slates down before the fold, cross the sign unknowing, cover it with a date given a woman thirty-nine mornings dead and turn her sixth page toward a floorboard; saw Jorra’s grey dust and his bent finger leading at the damper, and Tarn’s seventh year nearly gone and his head not turning at a vessel’s note. Kept six hearings, three near-full answers, three intervals and the unspoken word on separate trays; one stiff crust and its unnamed empty place, no third. At dusk carried up the yard at the half-pace, set on the bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, fold put right without a look at his face, thread frozen and unwiped, river note through the finger’s-width-open door and the fire’s four-four-and-a-gap through the floor kept apart. Count crossed into Silt 19 unspent. No present-tense break, no tagged memory, no experiment, no rank change, no ending.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 17: Lived Days 78–84, Silt 19–25, seventy-eight to eighty-four days old, carried at the edge of the work through the lean week. Kept the count exactly against a house that kept it badly in loaves, glances and a space nobody named; on Account-day watched Berr read one in twelve over a thinner crowd, wipe his thumb twice, take himself out of his own sentence and go off toward High Kiln with the box locked, a figure read aloud that was not the figure paid. Watched the yard sweep around the clean dark line, the new finer grey and the space under the lowest rack, and the gone board at the Weir and the out-of-line landing walked over without a fall while the honeyed ice, the stopping hairlines and the early Sill note were renamed past tense as the thaw that was. On Silt 25 filed a second telling of the shut counting room from a second Greybank man beside the first, keeping the likeness and the difference and joining neither to the kiln; the payer of the carried fire stayed unnamed and the cold foot stayed the cold to one woman and weather to the yard. Watched Jorra’s dust and damper, Tarn’s six counted and seventh held, Alda’s sign and date over a woman forty mornings dead, Mira’s cords and board beside Orra’s, Ulda’s half-beat at the well, the soft-cuffed clerk still set, and the bell four, four and a gap with nobody crossing. No present-tense break, no tagged memory, no experiment, no rank change, no new scar or possession. At dusk set on the bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, fold put right without a look at his face, thread frozen and unwiped, river note and fire’s gap in two places; one crust and its unnamed empty place; count into Silt 26 unspent.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 18: Lived Days 85–90, Silt 26–30 and Seed 1, eighty-five to ninety days old, three months at the close; a six-day passage carried the exact count across the turn of the month into the planting year while the house kept its days in loaves, glances and a space nobody named. Silt went out on the same mud it came in on and the yard went around the boot-print, the clean dark line, the new finer grey called thaw and the space under the lowest rack with a broom and a glance and no figure spoken. Kept the two tellings of the shut room on their tray with likeness and difference held and no third coming, joined to no kiln; kept the one crust and its unnamed empty place, six hearings, three near-full answers, three intervals, the unspoken word, the shape of the double turn, four low sounds in four places with the river’s note a fifth, the two unswept lines and the loan that can hear uncalled; could reach none of the crust, the breast, the bucket’s rim or his own chin. On Silt 26 heard the story of the shut room over the bucket and saw Tarn’s knife on its sill; on Silt 27 watched Jorra’s grey dust past the bent finger and his damper move ahead of Sella’s sentence; on Silt 28 watched Alda lay her slates before the fold, cross the sign unknowing, cover it with the date she gave a woman more mornings dead than any living person keeps count of, and touch her tin without opening it; on Silt 29 watched Mira’s two cords with neither knot counted, her board beside Orra’s not touching, and the soft-cuffed clerk still set for a measure nobody called; on Silt 30 watched Berr wipe his thumb twice, read one in twelve twice, take himself out of his own sentence and go off toward High Kiln with the box locked, the bell at four, four and a gap with nobody crossing, and a foundling’s head turn half a beat after his toward a pot; on Seed 1 watched the first work of the planting month be sweeping and heard a man say the strips east of town would want hands by the morrow, a direction and not a number. At dusk set on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, fold put right without a look at his face, thread frozen and unwiped, river note and fire’s gap in two places as for ninety days. No present-tense break, no tagged memory, no experiment, no rank change, no new scar or possession. Nothing joined, paid, explained or ended; count into Seed 2 unspent.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 19: Lived Days 91–93, Seed 2–4, ninety-one to ninety-three days old, three months, carried at the edge of the first planting work; kept ninety-one, ninety-two and ninety-three exactly against a house keeping its days badly in loaves, glances and an unnamed space at the row’s end. At dusk on Seed 4 Sella set him on his bed under the roof, put the fold right without looking at his face and left the thread frozen; the river’s note came through the finger’s-width-open door and the fire’s four, four and a gap through the floor in two places, one brown-edged crust stiff in the fold with the empty place unnamed and no third. His hand went up an inch toward the water and came down. Nothing joined, paid, explained or ended.

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 20: Lived Days 94–100, Seed 5–11, ninety-four to one hundred days old (three months and ten days), a passage chapter of seven lived days. Kept the count exactly against a house keeping its days badly in loaves pushed along a shelf, glances at the clay jar and a space at the row’s end nobody calls a number, and wanted his number said by somebody who would know what it counted; nobody said it. \item Ch 21: Days 101–103, Seed 12–14, one hundred and one to one hundred and three days old, three lived days with no recap. On Seed 12 watched a neighbour at the loaf shelf name the shelf’s old gap as a planting and the fold’s gap as a child’s appetite in one breath, her hand to the board before her eyes to him, and filed the two tellings on two places without making her joining his own (T097 planted); watched a woman lift a pot a hand’s breadth too high so something came up to the rim of a note and went back down, and added no seventh. No experiment, no rank change, no recognition, no seventh, no joining, no ending; the count stands at one hundred and three, unspent.

\item Ch 22: Lived Days 104–106, Seed 15–17, one hundred and four to one hundred and six days old, three lived days with no recap. Old life offstage, no seventh hearing, no sixth sighting, no knot counted, no word forty, no tin or box opened, no payment and no ending; count one hundred and six, unspent. The next I don’t count} and say \emph{I owe six}, noted his chest tight with the breath still unspent, and watched his broom go over the collector’s road over and over without once turning along it while the unforged sentence from the frozen ford stayed beside the seventh year (T036/T076, T009). No present-tense break, no tagged memory, no power moved, no experiment, no rank change, no ending.

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 24: Lived Days 110–112, Seed 21–23, one hundred and ten to one hundred and twelve days old, three lived days with no recap, the planting month in its last tend. On Seed 21 watched a neighbour at the loaf shelf reach past the palm’s breadth of bare board before her eyes found him, pause for the half-beat of an absence, close on the loaf beyond and say in one breath that the old space came in with the planting and this one was the price of a wet thing set down wrong, making a cause of two bare boards without seeing the empty place at his ear; set her hand on a place of its own beside the two earlier tellings and the watcher’s late turn, a third shaping of T097 advanced and not paid, with no joining, no name and no third gap (T097, T060/T086). At the going of the light lay on his bed under the roof with the thread frozen, the door a finger’s width open, the river’s note through the gap and the kiln’s four, four and a gap through the floor, the two counts not meeting; his hand went up an inch toward the water and came down. One hundred and twelve stood unspent. Still cracked, mute, unranked, below Thin; no present-tense break, no tagged memory, no power moved, no experiment, no recognition, no ending.

\item Ch 25: Lived Days 113–115, Seed 24–26, one hundred and thirteen, then fourteen, then fifteen days old — three months and twenty-three to twenty-five days — nobody under the roof knowing a number exists. On Seed 24 watched a man bring a number up out of a fist toward the yard well, look at it and put it back in his sleeve so the figure arrived nowhere (T077/T015), and a second neighbour at the loaf shelf call the old space at the row’s end a thing the planting brought in and the empty place at his ear a child’s appetite in one breath, laying two rooms under one cause without seeing it; he kept the shelf’s two gaps, the fold’s one crust and its empty place, and the neighbour’s joining on three places that do not touch, advanced T097 and not paid, no fourth likeness and no third gap (T060/T086). At the going of the light turned out the private file and found it unchanged — six hearings beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced, three intervals plus the unchecking stroke, the word forty unspoken, four low things with the river’s note a fifth, the two shut-room tellings joined to no kiln, the damper’s double bite filed as an object, the held breath from Seed 16 unspent and the loan uncalled — added the day and spent none of it, one crust stiff two inches from his ear and its empty place unnamed, the shelf’s two gaps in the room that does not touch this one, the carried fire missing its fifth breath under blind ash and its payer unnamed for a hundred and fifteen days. He wanted the crust, the breast, the bucket’s lip and his number said aloud by somebody who would know what it counted, and could reach or ask for none of them; his hand outside the wool went up an inch toward the note of water over water and came down with the count at one hundred and fifteen, unspent and spoken by nobody. Still cracked, mute, unranked, below Thin; no power moved, no experiment, no recognition and no ending.

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 26: Days 116–119, Seed 27–30, the planting month going out and Reed coming on in the dark beyond the door. One hundred and sixteen, then seven, eight and nineteen days old — three months and twenty-six through twenty-nine days — and nobody saying so. On Seed 27 he was carried to the very edge of the worked strips and watched the last hands come out, counted in glances and handfuls and never in a figure: a woman lifting two chaffed fingers and shutting them, a man with a barrow shaping the number of backs with his mouth and thinking better of it. One hand that went in on Seed 15 did not come out with the rest; the yard went around the empty place with a look and no number, and he filed it on a place of its own as a chart closed with a neat line over a note nobody had opened (T098 planted, not paid, held for a later body or figure), not laid beside the shelf’s two gaps, the fold’s one crust and its empty place, or the word forty. On Seed 27 and again on Seed 29 neighbours laid two bare boards under one appetite in a single breath without seeing they had joined two rooms; he set each saying beside the earlier tellings and the watcher’s late turn, made no joining of his own, allowed no fourth likeness and no third gap. On Seed 28 he read the damper’s double bite once more as the iron that holds and the iron that takes, saw Jorra’s bent finger lead at it while Tarn’s stroke went on over the flagstones without the half-check and the stones kept the stopped place, and kept two silences unjoined and the loan uncalled; across the market a silent woman’s green at the mouth was filed beside Berr’s and the Silt 30 green, three shapes in three places with no name, no dialogue and no ear. On Seed 29 Mira’s second cord showed twisted twice with neither knot counted, Alda’s sixth page and both tins stayed shut, and the cold foot stayed dark inside three turns of wool below the sill. On Seed 30 Berr read one in twelve over the very absence nobody entered and took himself out of his own sentence with \emph{your house}, the heard bell stayed beside the told bell and the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set at the out-of-line landing. At the going of the light Sella carried him up from the moot-post’s shade at the half-pace, went around the space beneath the lowest rack, set him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without looking at his face and left the thread frozen and unwiped, her hand resting a half-beat longer than the setting needed; she told the fire it was the thaw, turned the coals with the back of a broken pot, said \emph{The house will keep it}, counted under her breath toward no opening, pushed a strand of coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist, the grey streak pale in the dying light, and did not look toward the bed. The river’s note came through the finger’s-width gap and the kiln’s four, four and a gap through the floor, and the two counts did not meet and the three counts did not become one. One hundred and nineteen stood unspent and spoken by nobody, and his hand outside the wool went up an inch toward the note of water over water and came down. Nothing was joined, named, paid or ended; no seventh hearing, no sixth sighting, no knot counted, no word forty, no tin or box opened, no name or body for the missing hand. No new scar, possession or change of voice; the surgeon’s register stayed inside his head and the old life stayed offstage.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 27: Lived Days 120–122, Reed 1–3, Firstday to Thirdday, one hundred and twenty, twenty-one and twenty-two days old — four months through four months and two days — nobody saying so. On Reed 2 read the damper’s double bite again as the object that holds and takes, joined to no kiln; watched Jorra’s grey dust past the bent finger and his finger in the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence (T035/T031/T062), and Tarn take the broom only after its instruction, his seventh year pressed past the planting and held, the breath from Seed 16 unspent, the knife at the edge of its sill and the unchecking stroke kept beside the earlier half-beat with no cause across them, the loan uncalled (T036/T076). Mira worked the eels with slime grey on her sleeves and answered \emph{Ask the river} with her own thumb on the cord (T059/T025); Orra gave a date and got no answer (T024). At the close kept six hearings beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced, word forty and seventh hearing unspoken, the cold foot uncured (T093/T094/T096), one crust and the shelf’s two gaps in rooms that do not touch (T060/T086), T097 advanced and unpaid, and the three counts — river’s note, fire’s four-four-and-a-gap, boards’ four-four-and-a-knot — in three places; his hand went up an inch toward the water and came down, count exact, unspent and spoken by nobody.
