\item Ch 34: Lived Days 141–143, Reed 22–24, Secondday to Fourthday, one hundred and forty-one, forty-two and forty-three days old, four months and twenty-one to twenty-three days, nobody saying so. \textbf{Day 141:} at the Clay Yard and reed beds the last bundles came up judged by the arm that carried them, a cutter told a girl with a creel her arm knew what went into a bundle and that was the whole of it, and a woman asking what the hands would be paid was answered with the weather and the river and shut two fingers out of a fist; the yard went around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the broken birth-slates and the place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number (T098 carried); a reed-cutter’s grey cord went past along the boards straightened and turned where no slate lay, its knots unread (T099 carried). The clerk stayed set; in the afternoon the last bundles stood grey in the ruts uncounted with the third Account-day six days off, the yard going around its two lines, the rack space and the empty place with a look and no number, and Sella, moving her lips along the row with its two unnamed gaps, reached a finger beneath the board without looking or a word (T100 carried). At the going of the light she carried him up around the pan and iced trough, set him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without looking at his face, left the thread frozen, told the fire it was the thaw and said The house will keep it, and in the small hours he turned out his file as a man lays instruments on a towel and found every object in its place and nothing laid across anything else — six hearings beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, seven stoppings on the tray with no payer named to any, the damper’s double bite, the two shut-room tellings with no third, the told bell beside the heard, the fifth green a colour and not a name — one hundred and forty-three exact and unspent and the loan uncalled with the seventh year one tend from its end, wanting the crust two inches from his ear and his number spoken by somebody who would know what a number was and getting neither, his hand going up an inch toward the note of water over water and coming down against the fold. No present-tense break, no tagged memory, no power moved, no rank change and no experiment; nothing joined, paid, named, opened, called, spent or ended. Forward, not closed.

Under the roof, from the basket’s low angle, watched Sella reach a finger BENEATH the loaf shelf where the charcoal tally lies, without looking and without a word, and read nothing of the marks (T100 carried, unread). On Day 148 watched the men unnamed go low into the back room before first grey, Jorra’s fine grey slate dust past the bent finger, the full note known before a High Kiln kiln-master and withheld, and the bent finger in the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence (T035/T031/T062); at the Weir kept the reed-cutter’s cord, Orra’s legible unnamed double turn with the word forty unspoken, Mira’s second twist beneath the grey, the clerk’s inward slate and the child’s dark foot on five places that do not touch (T099, T024/T059/T025, T090/T080, T093/T094/T096). At the going of the light heard Tarn tell the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} and bring the ear-sentence a \textbf{ninth} time — after Reed 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23 and 26 — to the word that would call the loan and stop there with no figure and no name, drawing the breath he did not spend; filed the ninth stopping on the interval tray beside eight as an interval and not a payment, and would not let nine likenesses stand up and call themselves a doctrine, for a doctrine is an account that has found a payer and no payer had been named to any of the nine (T036/T076, T061/T082). On Day 149, the third Account-day and last market of Reed, watched Berr wipe his thumb twice, hold a narrow slate unopened, read \emph{one in twelve, as the notice says}, call the levy and deny it with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, pay two marks short for eels into an uncounted palm and go off up the clay road with the box locked and the true subtraction inside — a figure read aloud that was not the figure paid (T015/T041/T047/T077); the bell went four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, heard beside told (T078), and the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set at the out-of-line landing for a measure nobody called (T090/T080). Filed a \textbf{sixth} green at a silent woman’s mouth at the pot board and a \textbf{sixth} silent glimpse of the foundling at the market’s edge — cast-offs worn like a uniform, silt dried pale in his wrists, a gap where a front tooth had been, a green sliver on a string at his throat, his head a half-beat late toward a set-down pot and stopping in the middle of the turn, no loaf, no slate and no sale — as a colour and a shape on places of their own, never Fenna in the narration and the foundling unnamed and given no dialogue (T050/T051, T033/T034). At the going of the light Sella set him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without looking at his face, left the thread of drool frozen, set the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and went to her own bed; in the small hours his file held six hearings and no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, nine stoppings with no payer named, a sixth colour and a sixth shape, one stiff crust with its empty place, and the loan uncalled as the count crossed into Smoke exact and unspent. Nothing joined, paid, named, opened, called or ended.

\end{itemize}

Garl kept in objects at the very end of the kiln month — salt coat, hollow seat, unswept clean dark line and finer grey called the thaw, proverb gone to the pot, debt against the tiles uncalled and unnamed — no lesson made, no collector called, his name unspoken for two hundred and nine days (T009/T013/T092). Cost-questions to the pot and the weather, nothing priced, refused or entered; the sweet edge of lead glaze on a wrong wind taken as a direction, no cause named and no second edge paid (T077, T064 held). \textbf{The chapter’s one true change, advanced and not paid:} on Day 209 the third and last Account-day and last market of the kiln month was read over the basket: Berr came up short off the clay road with the red cord folded square under his coat and green glaze at one corner of his mouth, wiped his thumb twice before touching nothing, held a narrow slate unopened to his forearm, passed a finger over the figure and read \emph{One in twelve, as the notice says} low into the top of the crowd, the figure going twice over the basket, once for the moot and once for the households that came late; he said \emph{The levy is called. It is not called by me} and \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, and went off toward High Kiln with the box locked and the true subtraction inside, believing he had done a kindness. The district’s arithmetic changed for the third time and cannot be changed back; the printed figure stands unchallenged and a figure read aloud is still not the figure paid, answering nothing for the man carried out on Day 188 (T015/T041/T047/T077). The bell went four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, heard beside told; Hessa took the slate up the road unread, the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set at the out-of-line landing, the sixth green a colour and the foundling a shape with no seventh of either (T078, T080, T090, T050/T051, T033/T034 held). The burned-slate word came a second time, still a direction with no owner, room, hand or reason, no third telling and no cause (T035/T031/T065/T095). Tarn brought the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stopped, nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, the Seed 16 breath unspent; Jorra’s finger held in the cold damper until the sentence reached the pot, a remembered repetition (T036/T076, T062). \textbf{Second advancement, unpaid:} in the small hours of Day 209, with Sella gone to her bed and no breathing number anywhere in the house, the hand went up an inch toward the river’s note and came down at once against the fold — a miss under the very conditions that gave the one-rhythm holding on Day 206, and no failure in the miss. Filed on its sixth place, not a longer reach, hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, held change, key, power or rule, no payer named (T061/T082). He still cannot close two inches, lift the crust or speak a number. The file was exact, complete and worth nothing; Ember went out without a boundary drawn and neither month-name corrected, and the count went forward into Day 210 unspent. No new scar, possession, power or rank; the old life offstage.

\end{itemize}

\item Ch 53: Lived Days 210–212, Grain 1–3, Firstday to Thirdday, two hundred and ten through two hundred and twelve days old — six months and thirty days to six months and thirty-two days — nobody saying so. Cost-questions went to the pot and the weather and arrived nowhere: a neighbour at the door on Days 210 and 212, a rack woman with slip dried pale in her wrists and a man who kept a number shut in his fist at the well on Day 211 (T077). Six hearings beside and never among with the sixth out of a person and no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and unpaid, told bell beside heard, told figure beside paid with Ember’s third reading still locked up the road, nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, three held changes on three places, the loft scrape on a fourth, the pale line on a fifth and the held inch on a sixth; the file laid out as instruments on a towel, exact, complete and worth nothing (T061/T082, T100, T060/T086/T097 held). \textbf{The hand was asked six times across the three days and answered as the body answers:} down before the counted breath finished (210 morning), held for the small intake only (210 small hours), down at once (211 morning), held for the river’s own low interval and down on the river’s next low note (211 small hours, the one-rhythm coordination remembered), held for the small intake only (212 morning), and in the small hours of Day 212 with Sella gone to her own bed and the two rooms not touching, up an inch toward the note of water over water, held through the small intake, the hold and the letting go of one of the breaths Sella counts at her fire and down with the breath — the old two-rhythm coordination remembered, not a change made again — filed on its sixth place beside the others and laid across nothing, no payer named and nothing standing up out of it as a longer reach, stronger hand, hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, held change, key, power or rule (T061/T082, advanced and not paid). He still could not close the two inches to the pot handle, lift his chin the two inches to the crust or speak a number anybody under any roof had been asked to believe. On Days 210, 211 and 212 Tarn told the wood \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count}, brought the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stopped with no figure and no name, drew the breath he should have spent and did not spend it, left nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, the Seed 16 breath unspent, the loan uncalled and no collector on the road (T036/T076). Jorra came through with meal-fine grey slate dust past the bent finger and under the nails, kept dusty and clean forearms on one tray, told a pot \emph{You’ll do}, withheld its note from a man on a wrong wind whose saying about a pot singing early stayed a saying, gave no name to the men who went low into the back room before first grey, kept the burned-slate word a direction arrived nowhere beside the dust and the two shut-room tellings with a hand between, and held his bent finger in the cold damper until Sella’s sentence reached the pot as a remembered repetition; \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed and the promise of the boy’s name stayed ungiven (T035/T031/T062/T065/T095). \item Ch 64: Lived Days 243–245, Smoke 4–6, Fourthday to Sixthday, three dated days in six scenes, two hundred and forty-three through two hundred and forty-five days old — six months and sixty-three days to six months and sixty-five — nobody saying either figure under any roof (T071/T072). He knew the shape of a man going cold and wanted the crust; both were true and the second was louder. Instruction went to the wool, fire, pot, broom, running water and river wind and never to the basket; \emph{the house}, \emph{The house will keep it}, half-pace from every open slate, jar-glance without a touch, hand shut half over nothing, finger on top of the shelf’s front edge so the charcoal stayed unread, pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, lips along the two-gapped row with no figure, cost-questions sent to the pot and the weather with nothing priced, refused or entered (T058/T079, T100, T077). Garl stayed in objects — salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease, hollow wheel-seat with its twenty-year lean, clean dark line and finer grey called the thaw, proverb gone to a pot with no crack, tile debt circling without a name — his name unspoken two hundred and forty-five days, no collector up or down the clay road (T009/T013/T092). The widow’s mark hung where it hung, touched once before the kiln on Smoke 1 and at no shelf, well, rack, road, basket, afternoon or dusk on Smoke 4, 5 or 6, because the hand goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour; the opening stayed behind the household, no lesson made and no payer named (T058/T079). \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, T080 advanced and not paid:} at the yard well on Smoke 5 a woman of the firing work, \textbf{Ilva}, drew a short strip of notched birch bark from her sleeve and passed the nail of a thumb across the notches before her eyes went to the woman who had asked and before her mouth answered \emph{Five to this morning}; the hand went to the record before it went to the person and to the pot not at all. What the notches held was a count of firings, plain as a firing is plain, kept in wood because a slate would want a figure put on it; nothing on the stick waited to be read and no figure came off it that a clerk could enter. He took the order of reaching and filed it as a \textbf{ninth record-first hand-shape} on a place of its own beside the eighth, a finger between every pair and fingers between it and the charcoal, the cords, the knots, the pages, the tins, the missing hand and the pale line. He did not read the stick, ask her about it or let nine likenesses stand up and call themselves a rule, for a rule is an account that has found a payer and none stood to any (T080). At the kindling Tarn’s ear-sentence reached the word that would call the loan and stopped, nine stoppings standing with no tenth and the Seed 16 breath unspent; at the wheel-shed Jorra parted dust from slip, withheld the note he knew three turns ahead, kept the burned slate at four and the shut-room tellings at two, held his bent finger in the damper as a remembered repetition, and kept \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed and the promise ungiven (T036/T076, T035/T031/T062/T065/T095). On Smoke 6 a wrong wind off High Kiln brought the sweet edge of lead glaze over the boards, touched the fold and went out on the wind that brought it — a direction arrived nowhere and not a second edge paid — and one of the three shapings of the pot saying stood again as a saying, no fourth likeness made a cause, no pot lost and no name given to what ailed the man carried out on Day 188 (T064 held). The file turned out as instruments on a towel was exact, complete and worth nothing: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers, three pot sayings, the fourth burned-slate telling, two shut-room tellings, told bell beside heard, told figure beside paid with Grain’s third subtraction locked in Berr’s box, the returning-line place gone around with a look and no number, the question on its seventh place with four askings and no witness standing, and the ninth hand on its own tray (T101 carried, T098 carried). Six answers of the hand across the three days, the sixty-first through the sixty-sixth, each filed on the sixth place with no payer named: down at once; down before the letting-go; held to the river’s own low interval with no count in the house to borrow; one borrowed rhythm crossed with one kept; one rhythm held through the little silence after Sella’s count; and in the small hours of Day 245 two rhythms crossing in the inch across a wall that does not touch, remembered and not a change made again. \textbf{Sixty-six} answers now stand on the sixth place, objects and not powers, not a longer reach, a miss entered, a hearing, a seventh, a tenth stopping, a payment, a held change, a key, a power or a rule. He still cannot close two inches to the pot handle, lift the leathery crust or speak a number. Nothing was joined, named, opened, called, spent or ended, no thread was paid and no new thread opened; the hand lay down against the fold like a tool put away and the count went forward into Smoke 7, unspent and told by nobody.

\item Ch 66: Lived Days 249–251, Smoke 10–12, Tenthday to Secondday, six lived scenes, two hundred and forty-nine through two hundred and fifty-one days old — six months and sixty-nine days to six months and seventy-one — nobody saying either figure under any roof (T071/T072). Smoke went on without a boundary drawn; Smoke 10 was the first Account-day and market of the second firing, Smoke 11 and 12 ordinary tending days with no market, no Cross and no bell, and Smoke 20 (Day 259) stood eight mornings beyond the close and was not brought early. First smell hot clay under tallow, wet wool under that, sour Ash breath of the unswept corner called the thaw; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap, not a bell. Three counts in three places — the carried fire’s four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have stood under the floor, its payer unnamed for 249, 250 and 251 days (T088), the river’s note of water over water through the finger’s-width door, and the boards’ four nails, four and a thumb-width knot — did not become one, for agreeing any two would want a payer and none stood to any (T061/T082). The surgeon took the body’s inventory and entered it nowhere: one stiff leathery brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear, its empty place unnamed and no third, the thread frozen in the dry heat and unwiped, cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rode back, the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house would perform. He knew the face of a man going cold and wanted the crust; both were true and the second was louder. Instruction went to the wool, fire, pot, broom, running water and river wind and never to the basket; \emph{the house}, \emph{The house will keep it}, the half-pace from every open slate, the jar-glance with the hand shut half over nothing, the finger on top of the shelf’s front edge so the charcoal stayed unread, the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, cost-questions sent to the pot and the weather with nothing priced, refused or entered. \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, advanced and not paid:} at the Cross on Smoke 10, with the basket set in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade where no slate lay and Sella standing half a pace off, Berr Clay came up short off the clay road and read \emph{one in twelve, as the notice says} twice over the basket, once for the moot and once for the households that came late; he called the levy, denied it with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}, and went off with the box locked and the true subtraction inside, believing he had done a kindness. The district’s arithmetic changed for the first time in Smoke and cannot be changed back; the printed figure stood unchallenged, the figure read was still not the figure paid, it answered nothing for the man carried out on Day 188 or the hand that went in on Seed 15, and the figure read over the dressed grain lying covered under wool at home did not know what that grain had cost — the space between the two figures had no signature (T015/T041/T047, T077). The bell went four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, the heard bell kept beside the told and its gap not made a seventh of the full note; Hessa carried the slate up unread, the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set at the out-of-line landing for a measure nobody called, and Sella carried him home at the going of the light saying nothing of what had been read over him (T078, T080, T090). Six hand questions were asked and answered honestly: the seventy-third down at once on the river’s next low note; the seventy-fourth held through the gap where the bell’s next stroke did not come and down on the next sound in the square; the seventy-fifth held for the small intake only and down before the letting-go; the seventy-sixth kept to the river’s own interval with no count in the house to borrow; the seventy-seventh one rhythm held across the little silence after Sella’s count without crossing two; the seventy-eighth two rhythms crossed in the inch across a wall that does not touch, remembered at the close. Each was filed on the sixth place with no payer named, none a longer reach, a miss entered as a finding, a hearing, a seventh, a tenth stopping, a payment, a held change, a key, a power or a rule, and the file turned out as instruments on a towel was exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air (T061/T082). The nine record-first hands stayed nine with a finger between every pair, Ilva’s notched birch still in her sleeve unread and Hessa’s carried slate still the eighth (T080 held); the row question stayed at five askings with no witness and no row named (T101 held); the charcoal stayed unread, Garl stayed in objects with his name unspoken two hundred and fifty-one days and no collector on the clay road, the dressed grain stayed covered and unfigured, the widow’s mark hung where it hung with no lesson made of the one opening before Smoke 1, and the seventh year stood at its very end and still ungiven with the nine stoppings at nine and no tenth (T100, T009/T013/T092, T058/T079, T036/T076). At the close the hand laid itself against the fold like a tool put away where the next hand will find it without looking, the fire stopped at four, and 251 stood exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody, going forward into Smoke 13, a day not yet earned. No new scar or possession, no power used, no present-tense break, no tagged memory, no ending.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 67: Lived Days 252–254, Smoke 13–15, Thirdday to Fifthday, six lived scenes, two hundred and fifty-two through two hundred and fifty-four days old — six months and seventy-two days to six months and seventy-four — nobody saying either figure under any roof (T071/T072). Smoke went on without a boundary drawn and neither district month-name was corrected; no market, no Cross and no bell in three days, Smoke 20 (Day 259) five mornings beyond the close and not brought early. First smell hot clay under tallow, wet wool under that, sour Ash breath of the unswept corner called the thaw; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap, not a bell. Three counts in three places — the carried fire’s four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should stand under the floor, its payer unnamed for 252, 253 and 254 days (T088), the river’s note of water over water through the finger’s-width door, and the boards’ four nails, four and a thumb-width knot — did not become one, for agreeing two would want a payer and none stood to any (T061/T082). The surgeon took the body’s inventory and entered it nowhere: one stiff leathery brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear, its empty place unnamed and no third, the thread frozen in the dry heat and unwiped, cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rode back, the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house would perform; he knew the face of a man going cold and wanted the crust, both true and the second louder (T060/T086). Instruction went to the wool, fire, pot, broom, running water and river wind and never to the basket; \emph{the house}, \emph{The house will keep it}, the half-pace from every open slate, the jar-glance with the hand shut half over nothing, the finger on top of the shelf’s front edge so the charcoal stayed unread, the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, cost-questions sent to the pot and the weather with nothing priced, and the dressed grain turned under wool, spread, gathered by the handful and laid flat, changed in state and given no figure (T058/T079, T100, T077). Sella went to the fire before the basket each morning, told it the thaw, turned the coals with the back of a broken pot, pushed coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak showed pale off the coals, and left the thread frozen. Tarn told the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count}, set the knife at the lip of its sill with six checkable and the seventh not, brought the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stopped there with no figure and no name, the Seed 16 breath unspent, nine stoppings with no tenth, the loan uncalled, his chest tight, Ash in the knuckle creases, the pale clip-ring at the left wrist and the warm stone cold and unreconciled in its loft pot (T036/T076, T006). Jorra parted dust from slip, told a pot \emph{You’ll do}, withheld its note three turns ahead, put his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence, kept burned slate at four and shut-room tellings at two, and gave the men in the back room no name (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095, T064). On Smoke 14 a pot set down wrong at the racks gave its high thin note before its time and was swept around; the boy filed it beside the three sayings and made no fourth likeness and no cause, and a wrong wind off High Kiln brought the sweet edge of lead glaze over the boards and took it out again (T064). Ilva was glimpsed at the well on Day 252 with the notched strip unread in her sleeve, answering \emph{I keep the count, not the account}; no figure came off the stick and the ninth hand stayed nine (T080 held). The ownerless question was not asked a sixth time and stood at five askings with no witness and no row named (T101 held). Six hand questions were answered honestly, the seventy-ninth down at once on the river’s note, the eightieth before the letting-go of a borrowed count, the eighty-first held to the river’s own interval, the eighty-second through a little silence, and the eighty-third and eighty-fourth crossing two rhythms across a wall that does not touch, remembered and not made again; eighty-four objects lay on the sixth place, exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, and none was a reach, a hearing, a seventh, a payment, a key, a power or a rule (T061/T082). At the close the file lay open on the towel with every gap left gap and every tray parted from its neighbour, the hand laid against the fold as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking, and the fire stopping at four with the silence where the fifth should stand. Forward, not closed.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 68: Lived Days 255–257, Smoke 16–18, Sixthday to Eighthday, six lived scenes, two hundred and fifty-five through two hundred and fifty-seven days old — six months and seventy-five days to six months and seventy-seven — nobody saying either figure under any roof (T071/T072). Smoke went on without a boundary drawn and neither district month-name was corrected; no market, no Cross and no bell in three days, Smoke 20 (Day 259) two mornings beyond the close and not brought early, and the first firing of Frost (Day 271) far off and unbrought. Three counts in three places — the carried fire’s four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should stand under the floor, its payer unnamed for 255, 256 and 257 days (T088); the river’s note of water over water through the finger’s-width door; the boards’ four nails, four and a thumb-width knot — did not become one, for agreeing two would want a payer and none stood to any (T061/T082). The surgeon took the body’s inventory in its old order: one stiff leathery brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread frozen in the dry heat and unwiped, because nobody under any roof had ever been given an instruction about the thread and a basket set down is a pot set down and left; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rode back, the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house would perform; he knew the face severe cold wears and wanted the crust, both true and the second louder, and entered none of it (T060/T086). He could not lift the crust two inches or wipe his own lip, and took the humiliation as a fact rather than as a punishment. Instruction went to the wool, fire, pot, broom, running water and river wind and never the basket; \emph{the house}, \emph{The house will keep it}, half-pace from every open slate, jar-glance with the hand shut half over nothing, finger on top of the shelf’s front edge so the charcoal stayed unread, pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, cost-questions to the pot and the weather with nothing priced (T058/T079, T100, T077). \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, domestic and held, not paid:} on Smoke 17 the dressed grain was gathered in by the handful for the last time before Smoke’s second reading, covered under wool and set away from the hearth on the cool stone at the rack end, so the arithmetic read over it on Smoke 20 will not know what it cost; no figure, no loaf, no third gap, and no signature on the space between the figure and the price (T077 advanced, not paid; T015/T041/T047 and T060/T086 held). A second texture held and joined to nothing: on Smoke 18 frost-bloom wrote white on the stone lip of the yard well where the Warm had lately gone out, and the bucket knocked it grey and the yard called it weather; he kept the white lip on a place of its own with no cause — not a hearing, not a seventh, not a payer, not the widow’s mark (a well is not an opening) and not the first firing of Frost (T083/T085 carried, T058/T079 held). The hand answered six times, the eighty-fifth down at once on the river’s note, the eighty-sixth down before the letting-go of a borrowed count from the room that does not touch, the eighty-seventh held to the river’s own interval, the eighty-eighth held for the small intake only, the eighty-ninth carrying one rhythm across the little silence after a count that ended in the other room, and the ninetieth holding that empty interval as an object in its own right without filling it to make a fifth stroke or crossing a second count; ninety honest answers stood on the sixth place, each an object and not a power, and the file turned out on the towel in the small hours was exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air (T061/T082 advanced, unpaid). Six hearings stayed six beside and never among with no seventh; three near-full answers, three pot sayings with the premature note from Smoke 14 on its own place, burned slate at four and shut-room tellings at two stayed at their old counts; nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled; Ilva’s strip unread and the ninth hand nine (T080 held); the row question at five askings with no witness and no row named (T101 held). With Sella nothing changed hands: on Smoke 18 she carried him up the clay road at the going of the light, set him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without a look at his face, left the thread frozen, told the fire the thaw, turned the coals, said \emph{The house will keep it} and went to her own bed. With Tarn and Jorra the two silences under the roof stayed side by side and unjoined. No collector came, no witness stood, no new thread opened, none paid, none closed, and no ending.

\end{itemize}
}

He is known in the house by objects rather than by memory. The wheel in the shed has a seat worn hollow on the left side where he sat for twenty years, and Sella will not let anyone fill it. A coat of his hangs on a peg behind the door with the salt stains still in it, and she has never taken it down, though Jorra has twice reached for it in the dark and stopped. He was a big man with clay in the creases of his hands and a laugh that ended in a cough; his left thumb was shaped by the wheel into a permanent hook. People who saw him said he moved slowly and arrived early, which in a kiln-house is the same thing. He smelled of wet clay and banked coals. In the house the absent smell is stronger than the memory: when the kiln is cold and the Ash ridge is thick, the room smells the way the corner of a room smells where something was left too long.

\CRsheetheading{Voice \& Manner}
He is remembered in proverbs, which means his voice has been improved by use and is probably not as good as the versions of it that survive. He never said a hard word in front of the fire — a habit Jorra has inherited without knowing it — and when he was angry he went to the wheel. His sayings are all about repair and none of them are about completion.

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item “If it’s worth mending it’s worth mending twice. The second time is the real one.”

\item “Don’t tell me the pot’s ruined. Tell me what it was before it was ruined.”

\item “Feed the fire before you feed yourself. It’ll still be there in the morning. You won’t.”

\item “A man’s hands know what his head’s still arguing about.”

\item “Leave the crack showing. People trust a thing they can see has been handled.”

\end{itemize}

\CRsheetheading{History}
Fourth generation of Vails, born in the kiln-house and married to Sella, a slip-mixer’s daughter, in Y.H. 796. He kept the wheel for twenty years, threw the tiles that went into the floor of the Cross market, and was offered a price for his measure by a Sere factor in Y.H. 809 which he refused and did not mention for a year. He had two children: Jorra, born Y.H. 796, and Enna, born Y.H. 802, who died at nine months of the second chill and whose death he sat through without being able to do anything that mattered. In Y.H. 810 he began to be what Low Kiln calls walking thin — a vessel leaking faster than a man of his trade should leak — and he said nothing about it, because a kiln-master who admits a flaw loses the wheel.

In the Long Cold of Y.H. 811 the Ilm lay under ice for ninety-four days and no collector could cross from Greybank. Garl’s vessel gave in the first weeks of Stone. He died at home with Sella beside him and no iron tube in the room, and his warmth went where warmth goes when nobody takes it: into the Waste, unbanked, unrecorded, unreturned. In the morning there was grey Ash along the skirting board thicker than anyone had seen in that house. Tarn was sent to find a collector and turned back at the frozen ford. Jorra was thirteen and took the wheel a week later. The Vail household has been cool ever since, in a way that has nothing to do with the weather.

\CRsheetheading{Wounds \& Fears}
He knew he was leaking and kept throwing. That is the wound and it is also the answer to any question about why he is dead. He feared being banked thin and coming back as someone who would stand in his own house and not know the wheel; he feared more than that being spent whole and returned beautiful for somebody else’s benefit, which is what he had seen happen to a man he would not name. His contradiction: a man who mended pots for a living would not let anyone mend him, and called the refusal \emph{not wanting to be a bother}, which is the gentlest lie in the district and the most expensive.

\CRsheetheading{Desires}
He wanted to leave the wheel to Jorra whole, with the seat still worn and the note still true, and to come back as himself one day and teach the boy what a full note feels like under the knuckle. He thinks he wanted a whole return for himself. What he needed was to understand, before he died, that a vessel can be repaired without first being emptied — the thing his son’s household’s foundling will one day prove in the face of every priest in Sarn. He did not live long enough to be wrong about it in an interesting way, which is why his absence still has work to do.

\CRsheetheading{Bonds}
\textbf{Ch 123 (bonds).} Absent 420, 421 and 422 days and kept in objects only through three ordinary tending days: the salt-stiff coat with its left-shoulder crease on the peg behind the door, the hollow wheel-seat nobody filled, the clean dark line at the Vail corner with its finer grey called the thaw thinned in the air off the river and left unswept by anybody who would own it, the twice-mended pot’s hairline showing between old-brass staple and tighter wire, and the unforged collector sentence beside the seventh notch at the kindling with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt. His name was unspoken under the roof on all three days and his tile debt stayed uncalled; no collector came up or went down the clay road and no market, Cross or bell came on any of them. Both proverbs went to the pot and the fire and never to a person, so repair stayed apart from restoration and the hairline was left showing when Sella lifted the pot thumb-first at the wire crossing. At the kindling Tarn’s sentence was found where put on all three days and not made a habit, not a tenth stopping or a rule, and the boy filed it on a place of its own beside the unforged collector sentence, not a calling of the loan and not a payment; with Jorra \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed and the promise neither given nor withdrawn. With Corin his name stayed unspoken the same three days as the carried fire’s fifth unpaid, the two counts standing side by side without becoming one while the boy kept 420, 421 and 422 exact with 415 through 420 honest answers, six on the sixth place and not one a doctrine, and found the wool at the fold where it had been put. Neither the offered figure and its return at the well, the well-asking answered with the weather, the second man’s turned slate and direction, the clerk’s entered figure nor the two readings up the road in Berr’s locked box supplied a figure, payer or payment to either: the figure read was still not the figure paid and an offer taken back into a fist was not an account. No new scar or possession, no change of voice; nothing opened, named, paid or ended.

On Ash 2 at the kiln mouth, before any word and before any instruction went to the basket, she put her hand to the widow’s mark for one breath, lifted the clay lid with the back of a hand and tipped the carried coal under the back of a broken pot; the fire took, still answering four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should have stood, its payer unnamed three hundred and thirty-one days. Six openings in six months are six and not a rule, no seventh was made due, nobody praised the opening or named what it mended, and the mark was not touched again at any other hour on any of the three days; nothing of it came back to this absence as sign, mending, payment or payer. His name has not been spoken under this roof in three hundred and thirty, thirty-one and thirty-two days; no collector came up the clay road or went down it on any of these three days, and six arithmetics of the year stand behind one unsigned figure in Berr’s locked box with one in twelve printed and unchallenged and the figure read still not the figure paid. The nine stoppings stayed nine with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, the loan uncalled, the carried fire’s fifth unpaid three hundred and thirty, thirty-one and thirty-two days with its payer unnamed, and the three coverings called weather entered nowhere. No bond paid, named or spoken, no new scar or possession and no change of voice.

\textbf{Sella Vail} — his wife. She decided he would not be collected; he did not ask her to decide. A promise unkept gathers Ash in Sarn as surely as a debt, and the ridge in their room is the shape of theirs. \emph{Ch 2:} she touches the widow’s mark before the kiln and at no other time; she will not let anyone fill his seat or take his coat down, and the house keeps a private roll in which he is entered and which it does not show to a man from Slate Row. \emph{Ch 3:} the mark she touches only before the kiln was confirmed by the factor at Greybank and entered at the Court as a kindness, and she did not answer Berr when he said it; she went on covering the boy’s ears against the river wind instead.

\textbf{Jorra Vail} — his son, who has his hands and not his patience. Garl never told the boy he was proud of him. The boy has spent three years building a life around the absent sentence. \emph{Ch 2:} Jorra sits in the hollow seat he cannot fill and goes to the wheel when he is angry, which is the habit Garl had and never explained.

\textbf{Corin} — he never met the boy, who now sleeps under his roof and uses a warm stone that was warmed at Garl’s fire. There is a late recognition in this: the dead man’s hearth warmed the child he would take in, and a promise that cannot be settled because it was never made. \emph{Ch 2:} the boy read him as a man-shaped gap --- four, four and a space where the fifth thing should be --- and saw the charred edge of a slate in the kiln ash without knowing whose hand had written on it.

\textbf{Berr Clay, the Thane of Clay} — owed Garl for a consignment of tiles and never entered it. Garl never called it in. The Vail house has been short of coin ever since, and the debt has gathered interest in the Court’s books even though nobody in Low Kiln can read them. \emph{Ch 3:} at the Cross the debt was spoken around and never named, a space in Berr’s sentence with the shape of the hollow seat; his care not to call it was another kindness entered nowhere, for a debt uncalled can never be paid, settled or done with.

\textbf{Enna} — his daughter, who died at nine months and whose second chill he could not stop. He has been uncollected for a year; she has been returned thin or not returned at all, which nobody in the house will say aloud. Both are entered on the house’s private roll.

\textbf{Ch 4.} His coals held under ash all night and the kiln kept its four and four and a gap; the seat stayed hollow, the salt coat kept its shape, the ridge turned the corner unswept and the charred slate lay in the ash unexamined. Sella touched the mark for the kiln and not at the bank, said his sayings to the fire and the pot, and let the debt against the tiles lie uncalled while a measure was called in another house. Jorra came in with slate dust and did not say what the back room held.

\textbf{Ch 5.} The house keeps his shape without needing him in it. On Stone 13 the coals held under their ash and the kiln took its breath in fours and missed one; on Stone 15 the coat kept its salt-stiff shape on the peg, the seat its hollow on the left, and the ridge ran to the corner and turned it without a break, unswept. His proverbs went to the fire and the pot --- \emph{feed the fire before you feed yourself} and \emph{leave the crack showing} --- and never to a person. The debt against the tiles stayed uncalled while another measure was called elsewhere, and he was not asked to settle either.

\textbf{Ch 6.} On Stone 20 his debt against a firing of tiles was spoken around once more at the Cross, a place in Berr’s sentence shaped like the hollow of a wheel-seat, and Berr went around it the way a woman goes around Ash left in a corner; it remains neither paid nor settled nor done with. On Stone 19 Sella measured the ridge with her thumb --- near two thumbs at Vail, a finger more two doors down where the man gave under the tube --- and said leave it, it will be swept on the Last Day. His coat kept its salt shape on the peg, his seat its hollow on the left, the charred slate lay in the kiln ash unexamined, and the proverbs went to the fire and the pot: \emph{leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled.}

\textbf{Ch 7.} On Stone 29 the boy lay at the edge of the floor with the two crusts beside him while Sella laid her thumb into the Vail ridge and then walked two doors down and laid the same thumb into the death-house ridge; both turned their corners without a break and neither would be swept before the Last Day. Garl’s salt-stiff coat kept its shape on the peg, his wheel-seat its hollow on the left, and his proverb went to the pot and the fire and never to the basket: leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled. At the door the uncalled debt against the firing of tiles went around the talk the way a woman goes around a pot left on the floor in the dark --- a careful circle and no word for the thing circled. On Stone 30 Berr went around the debt as carefully as Sella went around Ash, set the printed figure down instead, and the coat, the seat, the ridge and the proverb kept the house in his shape through the year’s last market.

\textbf{Ch 8.} Through the Five he was absent and kept by objects: the salt-stiff coat on its peg, the wheel-seat hollow on the left, the proverb going to the fire and the pot and never to the basket. Under the Vail roof his name was not spoken on the Remembering; Sella went around it as around Ash left in a corner. The Ash ridge turned its corner without a break and was measured twice by one thumb --- near two thumbs at Vail, a finger’s width thicker two doors down --- and left where it lay on the Last Day; on Ilmen 1 it was burned in the morning and called dealt with by a neighbour, and the corner was a clean dark line. His uncalled debt against the tiles was still uncalled through the turn of the year, and the charred slate lay untouched in the kiln ash.

\textbf{Ch 9.} Through Days 31–37 his place in the house is a clean dark line where the Ash ridge had turned its corner for a year and two days, burned on Ilmen 1 and called dealt with by a neighbour with a pail of water while Sella stood over it with a broom and said nothing. The proverb still goes to the pot and the fire and never to the basket: leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled. The crack had been showing all year in a grey line along the wall and now the line is gone and the proverb goes on being said to the pot. The salt coat keeps its shape on the peg, the wheel-seat its hollow on the left, and the debt against the firing of tiles lies where it lay through another turning of the year, neither paid nor settled nor done with.

\textbf{Ch 10.} His place in the house is the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned its corner for a year and two days and was burned and called dealt with on Ilmen 1. On Ilmen 11 Sella laid her thumb in that line and then walked two doors down and laid the same thumb in the death-house ridge, a finger’s width wider, and came back without saying which was which and without fetching a broom for either; the line was left where it lay. His salt-stiff coat kept its shape on the peg behind the door, the wheel-seat its leftward hollow of twenty years, and the proverb went on being said to the pot and the fire and never to the basket: leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled. The carried fire he first kept still lay under blind ash and the back of a broken pot, missing one breath in every four, and the debt against the firing of tiles was neither paid nor settled nor done with when a woman went into the brook uncollected and no collector came for her either.

\textbf{Ch 11.} His place in the house is kept by the same objects on all three days: the salt-stiff coat on its peg behind the door, the wheel-seat hollow on the left that nobody fills, the charred slate in the kiln ash swept around and never picked up, and the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned its corner, which is not swept because a line left where it is is still a line kept. His proverbs go to the fire and the pot --- \emph{feed the fire before you feed yourself} and \emph{leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled} --- and never to the basket, the second still said to the pot after the crack was gone. The uncalled debt against the tiles is neither paid nor settled nor done with. The carried fire he first kept still lies under blind ash and the back of a broken pot, and on Day 45 a brine-gull carried off one of its coals, not yet cold, with no slate the poorer for the loss.

\textbf{Ch 12.} His absence kept the house through seven more days: the salt coat held its broader shape, the wheel-seat its hollow that nobody fills, the charred slate its place in the ash and the clean dark line its place on the wall, unswept because a line left where it is is still a line kept. His sayings went to the fire and the pot and never to the basket. The carried fire he first kept lay under blind ash and the back of a broken pot missing one breath in every four, and the debt against the tiles was neither paid nor settled while another woman lay sixteen mornings uncollected and nobody found a word for it.

\textbf{Ch 13.} His absence keeps the house through the approach to Silt. The salt-stiff coat holds a broader man’s shape on its peg behind the door, the wheel-seat in the shed keeps its twenty-year hollow on the left that nobody fills, the charred slate lies in the kiln ash, and the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned stays unswept because a line left where it is is still a line kept. His proverb goes to the pot and the fire and never to the basket --- \emph{leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled} --- and goes now to a pot with no crack in it, a saying about honest repairs said over a corner where the repair was rubbed out. The carried fire he first kept lies under blind ash and the back of a broken pot, warming the boards by degrees and missing one breath in every four; the coal the brine-gull took on Day 45 is fifteen days gone, entered in no slate and missed in no account. On Ilmen 29 Sella lays one thumb in the clean dark line and the same thumb in the ridge two doors down and fetches no broom; a barrow of grey goes out toward the Bone Orchard at the last market and nobody looks twice. On Silt 1 a new hairline of grey gathers in the corner beside the clean dark line and Sella stands over it with a broom and calls it thaw, and does not sweep. The debt against the firing of tiles is neither paid nor settled nor done with.

\textbf{Ch 14.} His absence keeps the house through seven days in which the river comes up and the yard calls it weather. The salt-stiff coat holds a broader man’s shape on its peg, the wheel-seat in the shed keeps its twenty-year hollow on the left that nobody fills, the charred slate lies in the kiln ash unexamined, and the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned its corner lies as it has always lain. Beside it a new hairline of grey has gathered, finer than the old line, and Sella stands over it with a broom and does not sweep because the house says it is the thaw; the boy sets the two lines in two places and does not let one become the other. His proverb about leaving the crack showing goes to a pot with no crack in it, said over a corner where the repair was rubbed out, and costs more now than it did when he was alive to say it. The carried fire he first kept lies under blind ash and the back of a broken pot, warming the boards by degrees and missing one breath in every four; the coal the gull took on Day 45 is twenty-two days gone, entered in no slate and missed in no account. The debt against the firing of tiles is neither paid nor settled nor done with, and no collector came up the road for the woman twenty-nine mornings dead.

\textbf{Ch 15.} His absence keeps the house through the flood and the going of it. The salt-stiff coat holds a broader man’s shape on its peg, the wheel-seat in the shed keeps its twenty-year hollow on the left that nobody fills, the charred slate lies in the kiln ash unexamined, and the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned its corner lies as it has always lain. The Ilm came up over the Fishstairs in a thin brown sheet and stood a hand’s breadth short of that line and of the burned line two doors down, and when it went off into mud neither line had been swept; the boy set the standing line, the water that went around it and the new finer grey beside it in three places that did not touch. His proverb about leaving the crack showing went to a pot with no crack in it over a corner where the repair had been rubbed out, a saying that has outlived the thing it was true about and costs more now there is nobody to say it in his own voice. The carried fire he first kept lay under blind ash and the back of a broken pot at four, four and a gap, with its payer unnamed and the coal the gull took twenty-nine days gone, entered in no slate. The debt against a firing of tiles lay where it lay, neither paid nor settled nor done with, and no collector came up the road for the woman thirty-six mornings dead.

\textbf{Ch 72 (bonds).} Present in objects only, a keeping and not a story: the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease on its peg, the hollow wheel-seat, the proverb gone to a pot with no crack and said over a corner where the repair was rubbed out, and the debt against a firing of tiles circled without a name, neither paid nor settled nor done with. His name has not been spoken under this roof in two hundred and sixty-nine days and no collector came up the clay road or went down it on Smoke 28, 29 or 30. Tarn kept the unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the very lip of its sill, with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt, and the ear-sentence stopped short of the calling word on all three days as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end. The carried fire he first kept answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand, its payer unnamed for two hundred and sixty-nine days. No bond paid, named or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 73 (bonds).} Present in objects only, a keeping and not a story: the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease on its peg, the hollow wheel-seat, the proverb gone to a pot with no crack and said over a corner where the repair was rubbed out, and the debt against a firing of tiles circled without a name, neither paid nor settled nor done with. His name has not been spoken under this roof in two hundred and seventy-two days and no collector came up the clay road or went down it on Frost 1, 2 or 3. Tarn kept the unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the very lip of its sill, with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt, and the ear-sentence stopped short of the calling word on all three days as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end. The carried fire he first kept answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand at four, four and a gap on Frost 1–3, its payer unnamed for two hundred and seventy-two days; Sella’s opening at the kiln mouth on the 2nd held the widow’s mark one breath and made no payment to any of it and no lesson of four openings in four months. The boy kept the finding that the household’s not-doings and his own kept gaps do not join for want of a payer, and did not lay it across this absence or any other. No bond paid, named or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 74 (bonds).} Present in objects only, a keeping and not a story: the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease on its peg, the hollow wheel-seat no one may fill, the proverb gone to a pot and the fire and never to a person, and the uncalled tile debt circling without a name, neither paid nor settled nor done with and worse for being uncalled. His name has not been spoken under this roof in two hundred and seventy-five days and no collector came up the clay road or went down it on Frost 4, 5 or 6. Tarn kept the unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the very lip of its sill, with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt, and brought the ear-sentence to the calling word on all three days and stopped there as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end. The carried fire he first kept answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand, its payer unnamed two hundred and seventy-three through two hundred and seventy-five days; the first firing of Frost was Sella’s work at the kiln mouth on the 2nd and paid nothing here and made no lesson of four openings in four months. The boy kept the finding that the household’s not-doings and his own kept gaps do not join for want of a payer, and did not lay it across this absence or any other. No bond paid, named or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item \textbf{Ch 78 (bonds).} With Sella the house kept its shape around a man not in it: the coat on its peg, the hollow seat, the unswept line, the proverb said to the pot and the fire, the debt against the tiles neither paid nor settled. Tarn kept the unforged collector sentence with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford, and brought the ear-sentence to the calling word and stopped on all three mornings with no tenth. Jorra gave the men in the back room no name and kept \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed. With the boy nothing was joined: the hundred and fiftieth answer stayed an object and not a doctrine, and the household’s not-doings stayed on a place apart from his own gaps for want of a payer. No bond changed hands, no name spoken, no collector on the clay road.

The carried fire he first kept answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand, its payer unnamed two hundred and ninety-one through two hundred and ninety-three days (T088); Sella’s opening before the kiln on Frost 2 held the mark one breath and paid nothing here and made no lesson of four openings in four months (T058/T079). Frost’s first and second arithmetics stayed locked in Berr’s box up the clay road with the printed one in twelve unchallenged and the figure read still not the figure paid (T015/T041/T047). The Frost 14 saying gained a third shaping on Frost 23 from an ownerless voice over the boards and the well-roof, the slate-runner once carrying a name the district spent and not saying whose; three shapings were filed on a place of its own with a finger between every pair, not a witness, not a cause, not a confession, not a joining and not paid, and not joined to this absence (T080 advanced, not paid). The boy kept the hundred and sixty-second answer as an object and not a doctrine. No bond changed hands, no name spoken, no collector on the clay road, no new scar or possession and no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 85 (bonds).} With Sella the house kept its shape around a man not in it, and on all three days his twice-mended pot stood on the pot board with the handle stapled, the second wire drawn tighter and left longer than it needed, and the hairline of the original crack showing dark between the staples; she put her thumb where the wire crossed the crack before letting the weight come on the handle and said both proverbs — \emph{if it’s worth mending it’s worth mending twice} and \emph{leave the crack showing, people trust a thing they can see has been handled} — to the pot and the fire and never to a person. The tile debt stayed uncalled and worse for being uncalled; no collector came up or went down the clay road on Bone 7, 8 or 9. Tarn kept the unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the edge of its sill and the ear-sentence stopped at the calling word with no tenth, and on Bone 8 his broom checked half a beat behind Jorra’s standing finger before going on toward the road, neither man naming the silence and the loan still uncalled. Jorra gave the men in the back room no name and kept \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed while the burned slate stood at five with a finger between it and the four, which paid nothing here. With the boy nothing was joined: the hundred and ninety-second answer stayed an object and not a doctrine, four held changes stayed four and not a rule, and the household’s not-doings stayed on a place apart from his own kept gaps for want of a payer. No bond changed hands, no name spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 123 (Days 420–422, Ilmen 26–28).} Absent four hundred and twenty, twenty-one and twenty-two days and kept in objects through three ordinary tending days, his name unspoken the same number as the carried fire’s unpaid fifth. The salt-stiff coat, the hollow wheel-seat, the twice-mended pot’s hairline and the uncalled tile debt hold the house in his shape; at the Vail corner the clean dark line and its finer grey called the thaw lay a hair less distinct where the air came off the river and the sour tang thinned, and nobody swept or owned it, the softening being called weather. At the kindling Tarn’s sentence was found where put on all three days and not made a habit, and the boy filed it beside the unforged collector sentence and Jorra’s silence, not a calling of the loan and not a payment. Neither the two readings up the road, the offered figure and its return at the well, the well-asking answered with the weather, the second man’s turned slate and direction, the clerk’s entered figure nor the softening at the river’s skin brought a figure, payer or payment to either count. Forward, not closed.

He is an absence with objects attached, and in Chapter 2 the objects are given a room. The kiln breathes in fours with a gap where the fifth breath should be; the wheel-seat is worn hollow on the left by twenty years of leaning; a salt-stiff coat keeps a broader man’s shape on its peg behind the door; the Ash ridge runs the length of the skirting board and turns the corner without a break, near two thumbs wide, and nobody sweeps it before the Last Day. His sayings have outlived him and improved in the keeping, and the house says them to the pot and the fire and never to a person. In the kiln ash lies the charred edge of a slate with the writing gone off the end, swept around for a year and never picked up. In Chapter 3 the absence leaves the house and goes into the market: the kiln’s breath missed one as the boy was carried out, the uncalled debt against the tiles hangs in the space between Berr and Sella, and a barrow of the same grey Ash goes out through the north gate while nobody looks twice. The reader knows him by what the household and the district do around the hole before anyone says how the hole was made.

On Days 5 and 6 the absence keeps the house. The coals under their ash hold all night and the kiln goes on taking its breath in fours and a gap; the seat stays hollow on the left, the salt coat keeps its broad shape on its peg, and the Ash ridge along the skirting board is not swept. In the kiln ash the charred edge of a slate lies black on one side and eaten into the shape of a strip of bark, with the writing gone off the end, and nobody picks it up. His proverbs are said to the pot and the fire in his improved voice --- \emph{feed the fire before you feed yourself}, \emph{leave the crack showing} --- and never to a person. The debt against the tiles lies uncalled beside a measure that was called and entered, and the boy files the two facts together without joining them.

On Days 7, 8 and 9 the absence keeps the house as exactly as it did on Days 5 and 6: banked coals holding under ash, a breath missed in the fours, the coat, the seat and the unswept ridge, and the sayings improved by twenty years of use said to the clay and the fire. The boy now files the death-house bench and the interval of a note that did not come beside the older objects, and the uncalled debt beside the warmth entered nowhere, joining none of them. Garl stays dead; the house’s debt and the Ash ridge are the shape of the promise he never made and Sella never released.

On Days 10 through 14 the absence keeps the house as exactly as ever and acquires a measure: Sella lays a thumb in the grey and calls it near two thumbs here, a finger more two doors down, and says neither will be swept before the Last Day; Tarn offers to check the width. The coat keeps its salt shape, the seat its hollow, the charred slate lies in the kiln ash unexamined, and the sayings go to the pot and the fire and never to a person. At the Cross on Stone 20 the debt against the tiles is spoken around again, a space in a sentence shaped like the hollow seat, and Berr sets the printed figure down where everyone can see it instead. The boy puts the debt on the tray beside the fourth pause and joins neither to the other. Garl stays dead; the house’s debt and the Ash ridge remain the shape of a promise nobody made and nobody released.

On Days 15 through 24 the absence keeps the house through the last tend of the year and into its last market. The kiln takes its breath in fours and misses one on all ten days; the coat holds its salt shape, the seat its hollow, the ridge its unbroken corner and the charred slate its place in the kiln ash. The debt against the tiles is circled at the door on Stone 29 and gone around at the Cross on Stone 30, neither paid nor settled nor done with. On Stone 29 Sella measures the ridge by thumb against the death-house ridge, near two thumbs here and a finger thicker there, and a woman at the tubs says the grey will be left where it lies until the Last Day and burned the next morning and called dealt with. The boy puts the thumb-measured ridge on the tray beside the charred slate, the barrow of grey, the fourth and fifth pauses and the date said aloud, and does not join any of them. Garl stays dead; the house keeps its shape around a man who is not in it, and the debt goes on living by nobody saying the word for it.

On Days 25 through 30 the absence keeps the house through the Five and crosses the turn of the year. The coat keeps its salt shape on the peg, the seat its hollow on the left and the proverb goes to the fire and the pot and never to the basket; under the Vail roof his name is not spoken on the Remembering and Sella goes around it as around Ash left in a corner. The ridge turns its corner without a break and is measured twice by one thumb, near two thumbs here and a finger’s width thicker two doors down, and left where it lies through the baking; on the morning of Ilmen 1 it is burned and called dealt with by a neighbour, and the boy keeps the left-in-place ridge and the burned-and-called-gone ridge under the same hand. The coat, the hollow seat and the uncalled debt against the tiles survive the burning and the opening of the slates, and the charred slate lies untouched in the kiln ash. Garl stays dead; the house keeps its shape around a man who is not in it.

On Days 31 through 37 the absence keeps the house through the first warm days of the new year. The ridge’s place is a clean dark line and is not swept; the coat, the hollow seat and the charred slate in the kiln ash keep their places; the proverb goes to the fire and the pot and never to the basket, and goes on being said after the thing it was said about has disappeared. The carried fire from Kindling still lies under blind ash and a broken pot, warming the boards by degrees and missing one breath in every four, and the debt against the tiles is neither paid nor settled nor done with. Garl stays dead; the house keeps its shape around a man who is not in it.

On Days 38 through 44 his absence keeps the house as the first left thing the boy can set beside the second. On Ilmen 9, the morning a woman was taken out of the clay-heavy brook and nobody called it anything, his salt-stiff coat kept its shape on the peg behind the door, the wheel-seat its leftward hollow of twenty years, the charred slate its place in the kiln ash, and his proverb went to the pot and not to the basket. On Ilmen 11 Sella laid one thumb in the clean dark line where his Ash ridge had turned its corner and another in the ridge two doors down, and brought the knowledge back without a word and without a broom. The carried fire under blind ash missed one breath in every four; the uncalled debt against the firing of tiles lay where it lay through the Fish Blessing upriver; and the line where the ridge had been was not swept, because a line left where it is is still a line kept. Another woman had now been left where she fell, and the house went around both absences without giving either a name.

On Days 45 through 47 the absence keeps the house as the first left thing set beside a second. On the morning after the blessing a coal goes upriver with a brine-gull out of the fire the house keeps, and one warmth less is abroad with no account showing it; the boy keeps the subtraction and no one else does. Under the roof the coat keeps its broader shape, the seat its twenty-year lean, the charred slate its place in the ash and the clean dark line its place on the wall, unswept. The proverbs go to the pot and the fire and never to the basket, and the debt against the firing of tiles stays neither paid nor settled nor done with. Another woman has now been left where she fell for nine mornings and nobody has found a word for it; the house goes around both absences without giving either a name.

On Days 48 through 54 the absence keeps the house as the first left thing set beside a second. The salt-stiff coat holds a broader man’s shape on its peg, the wheel-seat its twenty-year lean that nobody fills, the charred slate its place in the kiln ash, and the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned its corner is not swept, because a line left where it is is still a line kept. His proverbs go to the fire and the pot and never to the basket. The carried fire he first kept lies under blind ash and the back of a broken pot, warming the boards by degrees and missing one breath in every four, and the coal the brine-gull took on Day 45 is entered in no slate and missed in no account. The uncalled debt against the firing of tiles is neither paid nor settled nor done with, while another woman lies sixteen mornings uncollected and nobody has found a word for it.

On Days 55 through 60 the absence keeps the house as the first left thing set beside a second and a third. The salt-stiff coat holds a broader man’s shape on its peg, the wheel-seat its twenty-year lean that nobody fills, the charred slate its place in the kiln ash and the clean dark line its place on the wall, unswept because a line left where it is is still a line kept. His proverbs go to the pot and the fire and never to the basket, \emph{leave the crack showing} still said over a pot with no crack in it and a corner where the repair has been rubbed out; the joke has outlived the thing it was true about and costs more now that he is not here to say it. The carried fire he first kept lies under blind ash and the back of a broken pot, warming the boards by degrees and missing one breath in every four; the coal the brine-gull took on Day 45 is fifteen days gone and entered in no slate. On Ilmen 29 Sella lays one thumb in the clean dark line and the same thumb in the ridge two doors down and fetches no broom, while the yard prepares a sweeping already done; at the last market a barrow of grey goes out toward the Bone Orchard and nobody looks twice. On Silt 1 a new hairline of grey gathers beside the clean dark line and Sella will not sweep it because it is the thaw. The uncalled debt against the tiles stays neither paid nor settled, while another woman lies twenty-two mornings uncollected and nobody has found a word for it.

On Days 61 through 67 the absence keeps the house as the first left thing set beside a second and a third. The salt coat holds its broader shape on the peg, the hollow seat its twenty-year lean that nobody fills, the charred slate its place in the kiln ash, and the clean dark line its place on the wall, unswept because a line left where it is is still a line kept. A new, finer line of grey gathers beside it on Silt 2 and stays there through the week, unswept because the house says it is the thaw and it will go when it goes; the boy sets the new line and the old one in two places and keeps them apart. His sayings go to the pot and the fire and never to the basket, \emph{leave the crack showing} still said over a corner where the repair has been rubbed out and a pot with no crack in it, a saying that has outlived the thing it was true about. The carried fire he first kept still lies under blind ash and broken pot at four, four and a gap, with its payer unnamed and the coal the gull took twenty-two days gone. The uncalled debt against the tiles is neither paid nor settled, while another woman lies twenty-nine mornings uncollected and nobody has found a word for it. The house keeps its shape around a man who is not in it.

On Days 68 through 74 the absence keeps the house through the flood and the going of it as the first left thing set beside a second and a third. The salt-stiff coat holds a broader man’s shape on its peg, the wheel-seat its twenty-year hollow that nobody fills, the charred slate its place in the kiln ash and the clean dark line its place on the wall, unswept because a line left where it is is still a line kept. The Ilm comes up over the Fishstairs and stands a hand’s breadth short of that line and of the burned line two doors down, and when it goes off into mud neither has been swept; the boy sets the standing line, the water that went around it and the new finer grey beside it in three places that do not touch. His proverb goes to a pot with no crack in it over a corner where the repair was rubbed out, a saying that has outlived the thing it was true about and costs more now there is nobody to say it in his own voice. The carried fire he first kept lies under blind ash and the back of a broken pot at four, four and a gap, its payer unnamed and the coal the gull took twenty-nine days gone; the debt against a firing of tiles lies where it lay, neither paid nor settled nor done with, while another woman lies thirty-six mornings uncollected and nobody has found a word for it.

He stays dead and stays left: the house’s uncollected debt and the flaw in the floor nobody patches. Through Bone 22–24, Days 321–323, his salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease keeps its shape on its peg, the wheel-seat its twenty-year hollow that nobody fills, the clean dark line with its finer grey called the thaw lies unswept, and his twice-mended pot stands on the pot board with the crack showing while Sella puts her thumb first where the wire crosses and both proverbs go to the pot and the fire and never to a person — repair kept apart from restoration. The debt against a firing of tiles circles without a name and is worse for being uncalled; his name is unspoken under the roof three hundred and twenty-one, twenty-two and twenty-three days and no collector comes up or goes down the clay road. The carried fire he first kept still answers four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should have stood, its payer unnamed those three days, and the river’s water over water and the boards’ four nails, four and a thumb-width knot are the other two counts in three places that do not become one. Sella’s handful at the rack end on Bone 22 is one object lifted and let fall back and is not made again on the twenty-third or twenty-fourth; it brings no opening, no name or payer under the roof and is not laid across this absence. Five arithmetics of the year stand behind one printed figure in Berr’s locked box, one in twelve printed and unchallenged, the figure read still not the figure paid and no signature on the space; the finding kept on a place of its own with no payer is not laid across this absence. Sella’s mark is untouched at every hour that is not an opening, Tarn keeps the unforged collector sentence beside the knife and the ear-sentence stopping at the calling word with no tenth, and Jorra keeps \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed while the burned slate stands at five with no witness, no hand at the flame and no payer. The boy’s answers 217 through 222 are objects on the sixth place and neither the staying of Bone 15 nor the early letting-go of Bone 17 pays anything here. No bond paid, named or spoken, no new scar or possession and no change of voice.

The unforged collector sentence lay beside the seventh notch at the kindling with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt; Tarn’s thumb’s resting on the uncut seventh on Bone 26 was checked and found where it had been left and was \textbf{not made again} on Ash 1, 2 or 3, not a tenth stopping, not the seventh year given and not a payment (T036/T076/T006). The nine stoppings stayed nine with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, the loan uncalled, the carried fire’s fifth unpaid three hundred and thirty, thirty-one and thirty-two days with its payer unnamed, and the three coverings called weather entered nowhere with a finger between every pair. Six arithmetics of the year stood behind one printed figure in Berr’s locked box up the road, one in twelve printed and unchallenged, the figure read still not the figure paid and no signature on the space (T015/T041/T047 held).
