\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 1: Does not appear; his name, the stone warmed at his hearth and the house’s silence around him are held for Chapter 2.

\item Ch 2: Present throughout Days 2 and 3 as the shape of the house. The kiln’s breath he kept alive was counted in fours and a gap; his seat stayed hollow, his coat stayed on its peg, his Ash ridge grew, and his proverb \emph{leave the crack showing} was said in the house’s voice to the pot and the fire. The house’s private roll was spoken around: he was entered on it, and the foundling’s name would be entered there in a careful hand. The charred edge of a slate lay in the kiln ash and was not examined. No collector was called.

\item Ch 3: Day 4, Account-day. Present as what is left where it lay. The kiln took one breath behind the boy as he was carried out and missed the next; the lead on Berr’s breath and the red cord folded square came with the confirmation of Sella’s widow’s mark, and the debt Garl left against the tiles went spoken around, neither called nor settled. In the afternoon a barrow of grey Ash went out through the north gate toward the Bone Orchard, the same work that went out every market-day; the boy put it with the ridge under the Vail skirting board and the charred slate in the kiln ash, and nobody explained any of the three.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 4: Days 5 and 6. Present as the shape of the house and its rule. The banked coals held under their ash through the night and the kiln breathed four, four and a gap; the hollow seat stayed unfilled, the salt-stiff coat stayed on its peg, and the Ash ridge ran to the corner and turned it without a break, unswept. The charred edge of the slate lay in the kiln ash and was not examined. His sayings went to the fire and the pot --- \emph{feed the fire before you feed yourself} and \emph{leave the crack showing} --- and nobody said them to the boy. The debt against the tiles lay uncalled while the year’s first measure was called and entered in another house, and the boy kept the two facts side by side.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 5: Days 7--9. Present as the house’s shape and its rule. The coals held under ash through the night and the kiln took its breath in fours and a gap; the salt-stiff coat kept its shape on the peg behind the door, the wheel-seat its hollow on the left, and the Ash ridge ran to the corner and turned it without a break, unswept and not to be swept before the Last Day. His sayings went to the fire and the pot --- \emph{feed the fire before you feed yourself} and \emph{leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled} --- and never to a person. The debt against the tiles stayed uncalled while a number of days to Kindling went around the house as a closed fist.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 6: Days 10--14. Present as the house’s shape and its rule. His coat kept its salt-stiff shape on the peg, his wheel-seat its hollow of twenty years on the left, the charred slate lay in the kiln ash unexamined, and his sayings went to the pot and the fire --- \emph{leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled} --- and never to a person. The kiln took its breath in fours and missed one on all five days. On Stone 19 Sella measured the ridge with her thumb, near two thumbs here and a finger more two doors down, and Tarn offered to check it; she said leave it, it’ll be swept on the Last Day. On Stone 20, Account-day, the debt against the firing of tiles was spoken around at the Cross and never named, a space in Berr’s sentence shaped like the hollow seat, and Berr went around it and set the printed figure down instead. Neither paid nor settled nor done with.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 7: Days 15--24. Present as the house’s shape and its rule on all ten days: the kiln breathing four, four and a gap; the salt-stiff coat on its peg behind the door, the wheel-seat hollow on the left, the Ash ridge running to the corner and turning it without a break and not to be swept before the Last Day, the charred slate lying in the kiln ash unexamined. His proverbs went to the pot and the fire --- \emph{feed the fire before you feed yourself}, \emph{leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled} --- and never to a person. On Stone 29 Sella laid her thumb in the Vail ridge and then in the death-house ridge, a finger thicker, and came back without saying which was which; the uncalled debt against the tiles went around the door talk in a careful circle with no word for the thing circled, and a woman at the tubs said the grey would be left until the Last Day, burned next morning and called dealt with. On Stone 30 Berr went around the debt at the Cross without naming it and set the printed figure down instead. Neither paid nor settled nor done with.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 8: Days 25--30. Present as the house’s shape and its rule on all six days: the salt-stiff coat on its peg behind the door, the wheel-seat hollow on the left, and the proverb going to the fire and the pot and never to the basket. His name was not spoken under the Vail roof on the Remembering and Sella went around it as around Ash in a corner. The ridge turned its corner without a break, was measured by one thumb at Vail and a finger’s width thicker two doors down on the Last Day, and was left where it lay through the baking; on Ilmen 1 it was burned in the morning and called dealt with by a neighbour, and the corner was a clean dark line. The uncalled debt against the tiles stayed uncalled through the turn of the year and the charred slate lay untouched in the kiln ash.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 9: Days 31–37. Present as the shape of the house and its rule. The place where the Ash ridge had turned its corner for a year and two days was a clean dark line, burned on Ilmen 1 and called dealt with by a neighbour with a pail of water while Sella stood over it with a broom and said nothing; it was not swept. His salt-stiff coat kept its shape on the peg behind the door and the wheel-seat its leftward hollow of twenty years and nobody filled it. The proverb went to the pot and the fire and never to the basket --- leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled --- and went on being said after the grey line along the wall was gone. The debt against the firing of tiles lay where it lay through another turning of the year, neither paid nor settled nor done with, and the charred slate lay untouched in the kiln ash. The carried fire under blind ash missed one breath in every four.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 10: Days 38–44. Present as the house’s shape and its first left thing. On Ilmen 9, the day Dessa Silt was lifted out of the brook and no collector came, his salt-stiff coat held its shape on the peg behind the door, the wheel-seat its leftward hollow of twenty years, the charred slate lay untouched in the kiln ash, and the proverb went to the fire and the pot and never to the basket: leave the crack showing; people trust a thing they can see has been handled. On Ilmen 11 Sella measured the clean dark line where his Ash ridge had turned with one thumb and the ridge two doors down with the same thumb, a finger’s width wider, and left both where they lay. The carried fire under blind ash missed one breath in every four, and the debt against the firing of tiles stayed neither paid nor settled nor done with.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 11: Days 45–47. Present as the house’s shape and its first left thing. On Day 45 a brine-gull took a coal not yet cold out of the carried fire he first kept, and one warmth less went out of the world with no slate the poorer; the boy kept the subtraction. The salt-stiff coat held its shape on the peg, the wheel-seat its hollow of twenty years, the charred slate its place in the kiln ash, and the clean dark line where the ridge had turned was not swept, because a line left where it is is still a line kept. The proverbs went to the pot and the fire and never to the basket, \emph{leave the crack showing} still being said after the crack was gone. The uncalled debt against the tiles was neither paid nor settled nor done with while no collector came for the woman the brook took nine mornings ago.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 12: Days 48–54. Present as the house’s shape and its first left thing. On all seven days the salt-stiff coat held a broader man’s shape on its peg, the hollow seat its twenty-year lean, the charred slate its place in the kiln ash and the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned was not swept, because a line left where it is is still a line kept. His proverbs went to the pot and the fire and never to the basket; the carried fire he first kept lay under blind ash and the back of a broken pot, warming the boards by degrees and missing one breath in every four. The uncalled debt against the tiles was neither paid nor settled, the coal the brine-gull took on Day 45 was entered in no slate and missed in no account, and another woman lay sixteen mornings uncollected with no word for it.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 13: Days 55--60. Present as the house’s shape and its first left thing: salt-stiff coat on its peg, the hollow seat nobody fills, the charred slate in the kiln ash, the clean dark line unswept because a line left where it is is still a line kept (T009, T013, T031). His proverb went to the pot and the fire and never to the basket, said over a pot with no crack and a corner where the repair had been rubbed out. The carried fire he first kept lay under blind ash and broken pot at four, four and a gap; the coal the brine-gull took on Day 45 was fifteen days gone, entered in no slate and missed in no account (T088, T065). On Ilmen 29 Sella laid one thumb in his clean dark line and the same thumb in the ridge two doors down and fetched no broom; a barrow of grey went out toward the Bone Orchard at the last market (T013). On Silt 1 a new hairline of grey gathered beside the clean dark line and was called thaw and not swept (T092). The debt against the tiles stayed neither paid nor settled (T009); another woman lay twenty-two mornings uncollected with no word for it.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 14: Days 61–67. Present as the house’s shape and its first left thing: the salt-stiff coat held a broader man’s shape on its peg, the hollow seat its twenty-year lean that nobody fills, the charred slate its place in the kiln ash and the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned its corner unswept because a line left where it is is still a line kept. A new, finer hairline of grey gathered beside it on Silt 2 and lay there all week, unswept and called thaw; the boy set the two lines in two places. His proverb went to a pot with no crack in it over a corner where the repair had been rubbed out. The carried fire under blind ash and broken pot kept four, four and a gap, its payer unnamed and the coal the gull took twenty-two days gone; the debt against the tiles stayed neither paid nor settled while another woman lay twenty-nine mornings uncollected.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 15: Days 68–74, Silt 9–15. Present as the house’s shape and its first left thing through the flood and the going of it: salt-stiff coat on its peg, hollow seat nobody fills, charred slate in the kiln ash and clean dark line unswept because a line left where it is is still a line kept. The Ilm came up over the Fishstairs and stood a hand’s breadth short of that line and of the burned line two doors down, and when it went off into mud neither had been swept; the boy set the standing line, the water that went around it and the new finer grey in three places that did not touch. His proverb went to a pot with no crack over a corner where the repair had been rubbed out. The carried fire under blind ash and broken pot kept four, four and a gap, its payer unnamed and the coal the gull took twenty-nine days gone; the debt against the tiles lay where it lay, neither paid nor settled nor done with, while another woman lay thirty-six mornings uncollected.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 70: Days 261–263, Smoke 22–24. Present in objects only, a keeping and not a story: the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease on its peg, the hollow wheel-seat, the proverb gone to a pot with no crack, and the debt against a firing of tiles circled without a name, neither paid nor settled nor done with. His name has not been spoken under this roof in two hundred and sixty-three days; no collector came up the clay road or went down it on Smoke 22, 23 or 24. Tarn kept Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside the knife at the very lip of its sill, with no name on the man who turned back at the frozen ford and no figure on the debt, and the ear-sentence came to the word that would call the loan and stopped as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven. The carried fire he first kept answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand, its payer unnamed for two hundred and sixty-three days; the boy kept the house’s not-doings --- the uncalled loan among them --- as a finding with no payer, held apart from his own kept gaps with a finger between and joined to no absence (T009/T013/T092, T088, T061/T082). No bond paid, named or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\end{itemize}

Sixteen and built like a gate hinge: tall for a clay boy, narrow, with slip dried to the colour of old bone up both forearms and a permanent bend in his left little finger from a splinter off the wheel when he was eleven. He cuts his hair short so Ash cannot nest in it, which is a thing the district notices and he never explains. His eyes do not finish sentences; they go to the door, to the fire, to the wheel, and come back without reporting. He smells of damp clay, tallow and the sweetish edge of lead glaze carried up from High Kiln on a bad wind. The thing people notice first is his hands, which are the hands of a thrower and have been working since he was nine. The thing they notice last is that he never looks at Sella when she speaks to him, though he obeys her instantly.

\CRsheetheading{Voice \& Manner}
Short, flat, declarative. He asks almost no questions, and when he does it is the tool rather than the clay: \emph{Is it dry? Did you fire it? Who wrote it?} He speaks to the wheel and to the pots as other men speak to animals, and only then to people. When he is angry he gets quieter, the way Sella does, and the household has learned to read the lowering of his voice as a weather signal. He never says \emph{with} or \emph{against} when \emph{I haven’t said} will do.

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item “The wheel doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady.”

\item “You want me to say it. I’m not saying it.”

\item “Sella. Don’t feed him from your own dish. He’s not Vail.”

\item “A slate burns in four minutes. Four. I’ve timed it.”

\item “I didn’t say I was with them. I said I wasn’t against them. That’s different. In this district it isn’t, but it’s what I said.”

\item “He’s not Vail.” --- said in the kiln-house at first light, refused an answer, and sealed by the boy’s arrival.

\item “You’ll do.” --- to the pot on the wheel, in a voice with no welcome in it and no unkindness either.

\item “It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady.” --- to the wheel before anyone, said again on Day 140 of a pot he told \emph{You’ll do} while keeping its full note from a High Kiln kiln-master who said it was singing before its time.

\end{itemize}

\CRsheetheading{History}
He is the son of Garl and Sella Vail, and he took the wheel at thirteen when Garl died in the Long Cold and did not come back and nobody came to draw him. The wheel had been Garl’s for twenty years and the seat was worn hollow; Jorra has spent three years trying to fill that hollow with his own weight. He has thrown pots since he was nine, fired them since eleven, and knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves his hands, though he will not say so in front of the kiln-masters, who would call it early and make something of it. His house has remembered the Ash Rising since Y.H. 668, when children were taken and the rising was put down by a man with a list; the memory is kept not in stories but in the way certain doors are never closed and certain names are never entered. Since he was fourteen men from the Broken Slates have come into the back room of the kiln-house and spoken in low voices. He has listened to all of them and told none of them yes.

He watched Enna, his sister, die of the second chill at four, and has never forgiven the fire for being warm while she cooled. He watched his father die and was sent to find a collector and could not cross the ford, and has never asked whether he was sent too late or whether he was sent at all. When Corin arrived he said one sentence — \emph{He’s not Vail} — and has said nothing about it since, which in that house is a form of argument.

\CRsheetheading{Wounds \& Fears}
A father who went uncollected, a sister who went cold in a warm room, and a wheel he was given before he was ready. He fears Sella will die with something unsaid and leave him holding the house and the lie together. He fears the Broken Slates will decide for him what he is, because he has not decided and the longer he waits the more their decision looks like his own. He fears the boy most of all, because the boy hears things. His contradiction: he is the most careful keeper of the Vail fire in four generations and he is quietly helping the people who want to burn every slate in Sill. He has never once thought these two facts cannot live in the same man.

\CRsheetheading{Desires}
He wants the wheel to stay in the house and the fire to hold and nobody to write the boy down as Vail without asking him first. He thinks he wants Sella to say that he has done well with the wheel. What he needs is to learn that burning a slate does not return a person to you, and that the anger he has been nursing for three years is not his alone — it has been lent to him by men who intend to collect on it.

\CRsheetheading{Bonds}
\textbf{Ch 123 (bonds).} At the wheel-shed edge on the afternoons of Ilmen 26, 27 and 28 the household straightened around his silence without a word from anybody; nothing from the figure offered at the yard well and gone back into its fist, the well-asking answered with the weather, the second man’s turned slate and direction, the clerk’s entered figure, the two readings up the road, Tarn’s sentence found where put or the softening at the river’s skin came under the shed as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer. He came through the finger’s-width door with the day’s meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent little finger and white in a fist-crease where a hand had opened, not the bone-coloured slip of the wheel; kept dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray and parted them as clot from vessel, asked neither which slate had been broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, and gave no name to the men unnamed in the back room or word that the room was cold while the broken ones under the lowest rack stayed entered by nobody. He spoke to the wheel and a pot before any person — \emph{It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady} — told a pot \emph{You’ll do}, knew its full note three turns ahead with air under it and a want in it and withheld the knowing from any High Kiln master who would call it early and sing a pot before its time; his bent finger went into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence, took the cold out of the fingertip, moved the tongue a hair’s breadth and came out without leaving the extra holding of Ash 26 a second time — one piece of iron with two bites, gathered once and not made again, for a second would be a habit and a third a way and both want a payer where none stood. With Corin nothing changed: the boy lay under the roof unwritten, \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed and the promise under the shed was neither given nor withdrawn while the burned slate stood at five, the shut-room tellings at two, the row at five askings with no witness, the offered figure with no reader and the four ownerless directions apart and unspent. Tarn’s sentence found where put and not made a habit was filed by the boy on a place of its own beside his own silence, two quiet men under one roof and not a custom, and neither was laid across the clerk’s figure, the offered figure, the face at the yard’s edge, the burned slate at five or the five shapings of the well-saying, for a doctrine is an account that has found a payer and none stood. No new scar, wound, rank or possession and no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 86 (bonds).} Nothing changed hands with Jorra through Bone 10–12. He kept the wheel and the household’s shape at the shed’s edge, parted dusty forearms from clean as clot from vessel, spoke to the wheel and a pot before any person and withheld the note known three turns ahead from a High Kiln master who would call it early. His bent finger stood in the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence; the men who went low into the back room before first grey got no name and no word that the room was cold. He grew quieter at the fifth burned-slate telling and the household straightened around the quiet without an order, the claim gathering interest against a promise he neither paid nor refused. Sella’s reading went up the road and back without changing anything under the wheel-shed, and Tarn’s stroke went over the bright patch without the half-check while Jorra’s finger stood where it stood. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed and the promise of the boy’s name was neither given nor withdrawn. No name given, no debt paid, no bond paid, sold, named or spoken.

\textbf{Sella Vail} — his mother. He believes she took Corin in to replace Enna and to keep the house’s standing after Garl died. She has never contradicted him. Every obedience he gives her is therefore double: it is love and it is a correction neither of them will make. \emph{Ch 2:} she announced the taking and he answered \emph{he’s not Vail}; she got quieter and gave him no answer at all. He went on working, did not look at her, and shifted the damper before she had finished telling him to.

\textbf{Corin} — the foundling. Jorra was the first in the house to notice that the boy turns his head toward a pot before anyone taps it, and that he does it to hear the note, not the noise. He has told nobody. He resents the boy for being given a bed in the house while the clay-bound hand sleeps in the loft, and he cannot stop watching him. \emph{Ch 2:} the foundling arrived under the roof and nobody wrote him as Vail, which is what Jorra wanted and what he cannot bear. He spoke to the wheel, to the pots and once to Tarn about a rasp out of its place, and never addressed the boy.

\textbf{Alda Reed} — attended Enna’s death and Corin’s birth, and has never met Jorra’s eye for longer than a moment. He knows she wrote something down the night Enna died and has never asked to see it, because asking would make it a thing between them.

\textbf{Tarn} — the Vail’s clay-bound hand. Jorra treats him as a brother when the wheel needs him and as a servant when it does not. Tarn has decided to hate him for it and keeps failing, because Jorra once sat up all night with him through a fever and has never mentioned it. \emph{Ch 2:} Tarn was given the loft while the foundling was given the bed, and said so in one sentence to Sella. Jorra said nothing; he has never defended the household’s arithmetic and never contests it.

\textbf{Berr Clay, the Thane of Clay} — Jorra threw a stone at his door in Y.H. 810 and denied it. The Thane suspects the boy is with the Broken Slates and lets him be, which Jorra finds more frightening than being watched.

\textbf{Ch 4.} Sella’s hand went to the mark before the kiln and not at the bank; he shifted the damper before she had finished and again at dusk, and did not take up her silence about the back room. The boy was at the edge of his notice as a thing that hears: he spoke to the pots and not to him, and came in from the back room with slate dust worked into his forearms --- grey and fine, not slip --- and said \emph{the back room’s cold} to nobody. He wanted the boy outside the name Vail and the hollow seat his, and did not say either.

\textbf{Ch 5.} The wheel took the house into its rhythm again with slip dried to old bone up both forearms and no slate dust on Stone 13 or Stone 15; the boy noticed the absence and could not ask which it meant. He told a pot \emph{you’ll do}, told the wheel it did not care whose hands were on it, and shifted the damper before Sella had finished telling him the fire was low. He did not say the back room was cold. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed as it had been on the hour it was spoken, and the foundling went on being carried under the roof without a Vail name, which is what Jorra wanted and what he could not bear.

\textbf{Ch 6.} On all five days he came in from the shed with bone-coloured slip dried to old bone up both forearms and the bent little finger, and no slate dust; the boy noticed the absence and could not ask what it meant. He told a pot \emph{you’ll do} and \emph{the shoulder’s thick}, told the wheel it did not care whose hands, only if they were steady, and moved the damper before Sella had finished telling him the fire was low, going in with the bent finger ahead of his hand. He did not say the back room was cold and did not look toward the basket or the bed. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed; the foundling went on being carried under the roof unwritten.

\textbf{Ch 7.} On Stone 23, after five mornings of clean bone-coloured slip, he came in from the back room with fine grey slate dust worked into the creases of his forearms past the bend of the little finger and said nothing about where he had been; the boy read the arranged face the way he had once read a resident who kept his eyes on a chart. He told the pot she would want a thinner slip, told the wheel it did not care whose hands, only if they were steady, and went to the damper before Sella had finished, the bent finger going in first. On Stone 25 the forearms were clean again and he kept dusty and clean as two entries; on Stone 29 the sweeping talk made him quieter and the yard straightened around it without an order. He knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel and would not say so in front of a kiln-master, who would call it early and make something of it; the boy knows this about him as he knows the bent finger, and keeps both where questions can last for years. He did not say the back room was cold and did not look toward the bed; \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed through the year’s last market.

On the Last Day the grey in the corners was still where it lay and the baking went on around it, and he went quieter as the sweeping talk went around. On Ilmen 1 he worked the slip toward the thaw and the pits with the same forearms and the same silence, and the foundling went into the new year carried under the roof without a Vail name.

\textbf{Ch 123 (Days 420–422, Ilmen 26–28).} At the wheel-shed edge on all three afternoons the man who is not Vail keeps his silence while the household straightens around it: dusty forearms parted from clean as clot from vessel, the full note known three turns ahead and withheld, the bent finger in the cold damper ahead of an unfinished sentence and out without a second holding. He gives the offered figure at the well, the well-asking, the second man’s turned slate and direction, the clerk’s entered figure and the two readings up the road no meaning under the shed; Tarn’s sentence found where put is filed by the boy beside his own, two quiet men under one roof and not a custom, and neither is laid across the clerk’s figure, the offered figure and its return, the face at the yard’s edge, the burned slate at five or the four ownerless directions, for a doctrine is an account that has found a payer and none stood. The softening at the river’s skin stays a change called weather and is not brought under the shed. \emph{He’s not Vail} stays sealed and the promise neither given nor withdrawn, gathering interest against the burned slate toward the far-off hour when a promise may be called; the withheld full note gathers toward the far-off day a pot is sung before its time and something is paid for it. No new scar, wound, rank or possession and no change of voice, nothing paid, called or ended. Forward, not closed.

He enters at the wheel with his weight in the hollow his father wore and has spent three years failing to fill --- slip dried to the colour of old bone up both forearms, the left little finger bent from a splinter at eleven, a story about a fight he tells because a fight sounds more like him. In Chapter 2 he says one flat sentence about the foundling and is refused an answer, and the sentence is sealed by the boy’s arrival: a child lies under the roof and nobody has written him as Vail. He does not look at his mother while obeying her instantly, speaks to the pots before people, goes quiet when the levy is spoken of, and has given none of the men who come into the back room a word they can carry away. He is the most careful keeper of the Vail fire in four generations and is quietly helping the people who want to burn every slate in Sill, and has never once thought the two facts cannot live in the same man. Through the middle tend of Grain his dust, his wheel and his withheld note kept their old order while the burned-slate word held at four and the pot sayings at three; the wrong-wind voice on Grain 15 let one saying stand without a pot lost, and the promise of the boy’s name stayed ungiven (T035/T031/T065/T095 held, T061/T082).

The broken birth-slates stay under the lowest rack, gone around as wide as a pail of hot water set where a child might knock it and entered by nobody, and he keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray without asking which slate was broken or whether it was a birth-slate. He speaks to the wheel before anyone --- it does not care whose hands, only if they are steady --- tells a pot \emph{You’ll do}, knows its full note before it leaves the wheel and will not say so before a kiln-master from High Kiln. When Sella has not finished telling him the fire is low his bent finger goes into the damper ahead of her sentence, the cold iron taking the cold out of his fingertip, and the end of her instruction arrives at the pot while the household straightens around his silence the way cloth straightens when a weight is lifted. He reads the iron as a bite that holds warmth in and can take the hand off a man, with no Grathic word for both mercies, and keeps the reading to himself, exact and worth nothing. On Seed 11 he is heard at the wheel and not seen, a low note and a word to a pot, with no figure coming out of the shed onto the yard. He does not look toward the bed or the basket; \emph{he’s not Vail} stays sealed and the foundling’s name is neither given to the men who burn slates nor withdrawn. No new scar or possession, no change of voice.

On Days 126 through 128 the wheel goes on and the back room stays shut. The men in the room off the shed remain three or four shapes with no names, and the dust ground small as meal past the bent finger still waits for the question he will not ask. The equality under the roof holds at its moved place, Tarn’s stroke going on without the half-check and neither man naming the other’s silence.

Three or more men unnamed go low into the finger’s-width-open back room before first grey and get no name; the two shut-room tellings stay two with no third, and the burned-slate word comes over the boards a fourth time from Slate Row, a direction arrived nowhere and not a cause. He comes through with meal-fine grey slate dust parted from slip as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray and asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate. A wrong wind brings a third shaping of the pot saying — gone quiet on every row come the thaw — and he lets it stand as a saying, knowing the pot’s full note three turns ahead and withholding it, with no pot lost and no name for what ailed the man carried out on Day 188. He speaks to the wheel before anyone, tells a pot \emph{You’ll do}, and holds the cold damper until Sella’s sentence reaches the pot as a remembered repetition, not a change made again. His quiet goes before him into the shed the way a cold air goes before a door, the household straightening around it without an order; \emph{he’s not Vail} stays sealed and the promise of the boy’s name is neither given nor withdrawn. Forward, not closed.

Through Grain 10–12 the wheel and the back room keep their old shape. He is offstage at the market where the seventh colour and seventh shape are gathered, and at the wheel-shed on the two tending days his meal-fine grey dust goes past the bent finger while men unnamed go low into the finger’s-width-open room before first grey and get no name, the two shut-room tellings still two. The three shapings of the pot saying and the fourth burned-slate telling stay directions arrived nowhere; he knows his pot’s note and withholds it, tells the wheel and the pot their old sentences, and lets his finger wait at the cold damper until Sella’s sentence reaches the pot as a remembered repetition. \emph{He’s not Vail} stays sealed and the promise of the boy’s name stays ungiven.

Through Grain 13–18 the wheel and the back room keep their old shape while the claim of the Broken Slates gathers interest and is not paid. Three or more men unnamed go low into the finger’s-width-open back room before first grey on all three mornings of the dressing and get no name; the two shut-room tellings stay two with no third, and the burned-slate word holds at four tellings out of Slate Row with no fifth, a direction arrived nowhere and joined to no cause. He comes through with meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent finger and under the nails, parts dust from slip as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray and asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate. He speaks to the wheel before anyone, tells a pot \emph{You’ll do}, knows its full note three turns ahead and holds the near-full answer with air under it and a want in it back on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them. Three shapings of the pot saying stand as sayings about a pot: on a wrong wind one goes over the boards with no owner, room, hand at the flame, figure or reason, and the sweet edge of lead glaze touches the fold and goes out on the wind that brought it, a direction and not a second edge paid; no pot is lost, no fourth likeness stands up as a cause and no name is given to what ailed the man carried out on Day 188. When Sella’s sentence goes low his bent finger goes into the cold damper and holds until the sentence reaches the pot, then moves a hair’s breadth and is left standing: a remembered repetition and not a change made again, not paired with the Day 161 fraction, the Day 166 beat beneath the shelf or the Day 171 flagstone half-check. His quiet goes before him into the shed and the household straightens around it without an order. The first grain is dressed and stored under wool without a figure and the returning-line place is gone around with a look and no number; \emph{he’s not Vail} stays sealed and the promise of the boy’s name ungiven. Forward into Grain 19, not closed.

Through Grain 19–21 the burned-slate word holds at four tellings out of Slate Row, a direction arrived nowhere and still not a third telling of the counting room shut in the war, and the three shapings of the pot saying stand as sayings with no fourth likeness made a cause; the Grain 21 question about a row is a different instrument with no owner yet, filed on its own seventh place with a finger between it and the sayings, the slate, the shut room, the hearings and the count. Men unnamed go low into the finger’s-width-open back room before first grey and get no name from him, and the meal-fine grey dust goes past the bent finger and under the nails while clean forearms stay on the other tray. He knows the full note of a Vail pot three turns before it leaves his hands — with air under it and a want in it — and withholds it from men on wrong winds whose sayings stay sayings, with no pot lost and no name given to what ailed the man carried out on Day 188. His bent finger stands in the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence as a remembered repetition, one iron with two bites — the bite that holds a vessel whole and the bite that can take the hand off a man — with no Grathic word for both mercies and no rule stood up out of three held changes. He grows quieter whenever the burned-slate word goes around and the household straightens around the quiet without an order. He is the most careful keeper of the Vail fire in four generations and is quietly helping the people who want to burn every slate in Sill, and has never once thought these two facts cannot live in the same man. \emph{He’s not Vail} stays sealed and the promise of the foundling’s name stays ungiven.

Through Grain 22–24 (Days 231–233) the wheel and the back room keep their old shape while the claim of the Broken Slates gathers interest and is not paid. Three or more men unnamed go low into the finger’s-width-open back room before first grey on all three mornings and get no name from him; the two shut-room tellings stay two with no third, and the burned-slate word holds at four tellings out of Slate Row with no fifth, a direction arrived nowhere and joined to no cause. He comes through with meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent finger and under the nails, white in the creases where a fist had opened, not bone-coloured slip; parts dust from slip as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray and asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate; the broken birth-slates stay under the lowest rack, gone around and entered by nobody. He speaks to the wheel before he speaks to anyone — \emph{It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady} — tells a pot \emph{You’ll do} in a voice with no welcome and no unkindness, knows its full note three turns ahead with air under it and a want in it, and holds the knowing back on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them. When the ownerless question goes over the boards a second time he lets it stand on its own seventh place with a finger between it and his sayings, the slate, the shut room, the hearings and the count; he does not supply a witness, name a row or make a cause of it. His bent finger goes into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence and holds until it reaches the pot, then moves a hair’s breadth and is left standing: a remembered repetition and not a change made again, one iron with two bites and no Grathic word for both mercies, joined to no kiln and paired with no other fraction. His quiet goes before him into the shed and the household straightens around it without an order. The dressed grain stays under wool without a figure and the returning-line place is gone around with a look and no number. He is the most careful keeper of the Vail fire in four generations and is quietly helping the people who want to burn every slate in Sill, and has never once thought the two facts cannot live in the same man. \emph{He’s not Vail} stays sealed and the promise of the foundling’s name stays ungiven.

Through Smoke 1–3 (Days 240–242) the wheel and the back room keep their old shape under a roof in which the first firing of the month has come and gone without a lesson. Three or more men unnamed go low into the finger’s-width-open room before first grey on all three mornings and get no name from him and no third telling; he comes through with meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent little finger and under the nails, white in the creases where a fist has opened, parts dust from slip as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray and asks neither which slate broke nor whether it was a birth-slate. He speaks to the wheel first, tells a pot \emph{You’ll do}, knows its full note three turns ahead with air under it and a want in it and withholds the knowing on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them. The three shapings of the pot saying stand as sayings; on Smoke 3 the sweet edge of lead glaze rides a wrong wind off High Kiln over the boards, touches the fold and goes out on it, and he lets one saying stand again without making a lesson of the green, losing a pot or naming what ailed the man carried out on Day 188. The burned-slate word holds at four from Slate Row, still not a third telling of the shut room; the row question holds four askings with no owner, room, hand at the kiln, cause or witness, and he does not claim it or supply one. When Sella’s sentence goes low his bent finger goes into the cold damper ahead of it, holds until the end arrives at the pot, moves a hair’s breadth and is left standing — a remembered repetition paired with no other fraction, one piece of iron with two bites and no word in Grathic for both. \emph{He’s not Vail} stays sealed and the promise of the boy’s name stays ungiven. No new scar or possession, no bond paid or spoken.

Through Smoke 4–6 (Days 243–245) the wheel and the back room keep their old shape under a roof whose first firing is behind and not looked at again. Men unnamed go low before first grey and get no name; the two shut-room tellings stay two and the burned-slate word stays at four, a direction arrived nowhere. He parts dust from slip, speaks to the wheel before anyone, knows a pot’s full note three turns ahead and withholds it, and holds his bent finger in the damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence as a remembered repetition, one iron with two bites and no word in Grathic for both. On Smoke 6 the sweet edge of lead glaze rides a wrong wind over the boards and goes out on it; he makes no lesson of the green and names no cause for the man carried out on Day 188. \emph{He’s not Vail} stays sealed and the promise of the boy’s name stays ungiven. No new scar or possession, no bond paid or spoken.

Through Smoke 7–9 (Days 246–248) the wheel and the back room keep their old shape under a roof whose first firing is behind and not looked at again. Men unnamed go low before first grey and get no name; the two shut-room tellings stay two and the burned-slate word stays at four, a direction arrived nowhere. He parts dust from slip as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, speaks to the wheel before he speaks to anyone, tells a pot \emph{You’ll do}, knows its full note three turns ahead with air under it and a want in it and withholds the knowing on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them, advanced and not paid. When the ownerless question goes over the boards a fifth time on the afternoon of Smoke 8 he lets it stand on its own seventh place with a finger between each pair of askings and fingers between them and his sayings, the slate, the shut room, the hearings and the count; he supplies no witness, names no row and makes no cause of it, and the sweet edge of lead glaze rides a wrong wind over the boards and goes out on it without becoming a lesson. His bent finger stands in the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence, holds until the end arrives at the pot, moves a hair’s breadth and is left standing — a remembered repetition paired with no other fraction, one iron with two bites and no word in Grathic for both. \emph{He’s not Vail} stays sealed and the promise of the boy’s name stays ungiven. No new scar or possession, no bond paid or spoken.

Through Smoke 10–12 (Days 249–251) he is at the wheel-shed edge, the cold damper, the kiln mouth, the drying racks and the Clay Yard on all three days. He comes through with the day’s meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent little finger and under the nails, white in the creases where a fist had opened, not bone-coloured slip; parts dust from slip as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray and asks neither which slate broke nor whether it was a birth-slate, while the broken birth-slates under the lowest rack are entered by nobody. Three or more men unnamed go low into the finger’s-width-open back room before first grey on all three mornings and get no name from him, and he does not say the room was cold; the two tellings of the room shut in the war stay two with no third. He speaks to the wheel before he speaks to any person (\emph{It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady}), tells a pot \emph{You’ll do} in a voice with no welcome and no unkindness, knows its full note three turns before it leaves his hands with air under it and a want in it, and withholds the knowing on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them, advanced and not paid. The three shapings of the pot saying stay sayings with no fourth likeness made a cause; the burned-slate word holds at four tellings out of Slate Row with no fifth and still not a third telling of the shut room; the row question stays at five askings with no owner, witness, cause or row named. When Sella’s sentence goes low his bent finger goes into the cold damper ahead of it, takes the cold out, holds until the end of it arrives at the pot, moves a hair’s breadth and is left standing — a remembered repetition paired with no other fraction, one piece of iron with two bites and no Grathic word for both mercies, joined to no kiln. Smoke’s first reading goes up the clay road in Berr’s locked box and changes the district’s arithmetic where two hundred people stand, and neither the reading nor the house comes to meet the other; he gives no name to what ailed the man carried out on Day 188 and no lesson to the green. \emph{He’s not Vail} stays sealed and the promise of the boy’s name to the men who burn slates is neither given nor withdrawn. No new scar or possession, no change of voice.

Through Smoke 13–15 (Days 252–254) the wheel and the back room keep their old shape under a roof whose first firing is behind and not looked at again. Men unnamed go low before first grey on all three mornings and get no name; the two shut-room tellings stay two and the burned-slate word stays at four, a direction arrived nowhere. He comes through with meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent little finger, white in the creases where a fist had opened, not bone-coloured slip; parts dust from slip as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, speaks to the wheel before he speaks to anyone (\emph{It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady}), tells a pot \emph{You’ll do}, knows its full note three turns ahead with air under it and a want in it, and withholds the knowing on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them. The three shapings of the pot saying stay sayings with no fourth likeness made a cause; on Smoke 14 a pot set down wrong at the racks gives its high thin note before its time and the woman sweeps around it and says something practical about the slip, so no pot is lost, no lesson is made and no name is given to what ailed the man carried out on Day 188. The sweet edge of lead glaze rides a wrong wind off High Kiln over the boards and goes out on it without becoming a cause. When Sella’s sentence goes low his bent finger goes into the cold damper ahead of it, takes the cold out, holds until the end arrives at the pot, moves a hair’s breadth and is left standing — one piece of iron with two bites and no Grathic word for both, joined to no kiln. The row question is not asked a sixth time and stands at five askings with no witness and no row named. \emph{He’s not Vail} stays sealed and the promise of the boy’s name stays ungiven. No new scar or possession, no bond paid or spoken.

Through Smoke 16–18 the wheel and the back room keep their old shape. He comes through each morning with meal-fine grey slate dust past the bent finger and white in the creases of a fist, parts dusty forearms from clean ones on one tray, gives the men who went into the room no name and does not say the room was cold, and keeps the two tellings of the shut room at two. He speaks to the wheel before anyone, tells a pot it will do, knows its full note three turns ahead and withholds it; the three shapings of the pot saying stand with the premature note from Smoke 14 on its own place and no fourth likeness made a cause, the burned-slate word stands at four and the row question at five askings with no witness. When Sella’s sentence goes low his bent finger goes into the cold damper ahead of the end of it, takes the cold out, holds and is left standing — a remembered repetition joined to no kiln. He does not ask about the ear while Tarn does not ask about the room; \emph{he’s not Vail} stays sealed and the promise of the boy’s name to the men who burn slates is neither given nor withdrawn.

Through Smoke 19–21 he holds the old shape at the wheel and the damper and gives nothing up. Men unnamed go low into the back room before first grey on the 19th and 21st and get no name from him and no word that the room was cold; meal-fine grey slate dust is worked past the bent little finger, white in the creases of a fist, parted from clean slip; he speaks to the wheel before any person and tells a pot \emph{You’ll do}, knows its full note three turns ahead with air under it and a want in it and withholds the knowing on the near-full tray. Three pot sayings stay three with the premature note from Smoke 14 on its own place and no fourth likeness made a cause; the burned-slate word from Slate Row holds at four and the shut-room tellings at two; the ownerless row question stands at five askings with no witness and no row named (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095, T101). Sella’s unfinished sentence still finishes at the pot, \emph{he’s not Vail} is sealed and the promise of the boy’s name to the men who burn slates is neither given nor withdrawn; the equality with Tarn holds at the place it moved to, neither asking about the back room or the ear. Smoke’s second arithmetic goes up the road in Berr’s locked box on the 20th and makes no change under the wheel-shed (T015/T041/T047).

Through Smoke 22–24 he holds the old shape at the wheel and the damper and gives nothing up. Men unnamed go low into the finger’s-width-open back room before first grey on all three days and get no name from him and no word that the room was cold; he comes through with meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent little finger and white in the creases of a fist that had opened, parts dusty forearms from clean as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, asks neither which slate broke nor whether it was a birth-slate. He speaks to the wheel before any person --- \emph{It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady} --- tells a pot \emph{You’ll do}, knows its full note three turns ahead with air under it and a want in it and withholds the knowing on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them (T061/T082). The three shapings of the pot saying stand with the premature note from Smoke 14 on its own place and no fourth likeness made a cause; the burned-slate word from Slate Row holds at four and the shut-room tellings at two; the ownerless row question stands at five askings with no witness and no row named (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095, T101). When Sella’s sentence goes low (\emph{The fire’s low. It wants---}) his bent finger goes into the cold damper ahead of it, takes the cold out of the fingertip and holds until the end arrives at the pot --- one piece of iron with two bites, mercy and mutilation in one, with no Grathic word for both, joined to no kiln (T062). \emph{He’s not Vail} stays sealed and the promise of the boy’s name to the men who burn slates is neither given nor withdrawn; the equality with Tarn holds at the place it moved to, neither asking about the back room or the ear. Smoke’s second arithmetic stays behind and unread up the road and makes no change under the wheel-shed (T015/T041/T047). No new scar or possession, no change of voice.

Through Smoke 25–27, Days 264–266, he keeps the wheel and the household’s shape at the shed’s edge: meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent little finger, dusty forearms parted from clean ones, the wheel told it does not care whose hands, only if they are steady, a pot told \emph{You’ll do} and its full note known three turns ahead and withheld on the near-full tray beside the hearings. Three or more men go low into the finger’s-width-open back room before first grey on all three mornings and get no name from him and no word that the room was cold; his bent finger goes into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence, one piece of iron with two bites and no Grathic word for both. The burned-slate word holds at four, the shut-room tellings at two and the three pot sayings at three with the premature Smoke 14 note apart; the row question takes one further shaping over the boards, a report of an asking, and stands at five askings with no witness and no row named. His promise of the boy’s name to the men who burn slates is neither given nor withdrawn and \emph{he’s not Vail} stays sealed as a lid nobody has tried to lift in three years. Nothing is paid, named or settled and the count goes into Smoke 28 unspent.

The fifth telling stands at five with a finger between the fifth and the four, no witness standing, no hand named at the flame and no sixth due on a day that has not earned one, and the seed waits on the far-off calling-in of his promise — not a confession and not a payment. The shut-room tellings stay at two, the pot sayings at three with the Smoke 14 note apart, and the row at five askings with one shaping and no witness. Bone’s first reading goes up the road in Berr’s box and changes nothing under the wheel-shed; \emph{he’s not Vail} stays sealed and the promise stays ungiven. Nothing is joined, named, opened, called, paid or ended.

Through Bone 22–24, Days 321–323, he keeps the wheel-shed edge and the household straightens around his silence. Each day he came through the finger’s-width door with meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent little finger and under the nails, white in the creases where a fist had opened, not bone-coloured slip; kept dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray parted as clot from vessel, asked neither which slate had been broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, spoke to the wheel before anyone and told a pot \emph{You’ll do} with no welcome and no unkindness. He knew the full note a pot would give three turns ahead, with air under it and a want in it, and withheld it on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them from a High Kiln master who would have called it early. Three or more men went low into the back room before first grey and got no name from him and no word that the room was cold. His bent finger went into the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence on Bone 22 and 24 and the household straightened around the waiting; he read one piece of iron with two bites, the holding and the taking, with no Grathic word for both mercies and no slate entered. He grew quieter as the burned-slate saying went around and the household straightened around the quiet without an order; the fifth telling stood at five with a finger between the fifth and the four, no witness standing and no sixth due on a day that had not earned one, and the claim went on gathering interest against his promise to the men who burn slates, the promise neither given nor withdrawn. The shut-room tellings stood at two, the pot sayings at three with the Smoke 14 note apart, the row at five askings with no witness and the Frost 14 saying at three shapings beside Hessa Rale’s eighth hand. Sella’s handful at the rack end brought no word under the wheel-shed and was not joined to his dust, his damper or his promise; the finding that five readings are five and not one account stayed on a place of its own with no payer. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed. No bond paid or spoken, no new scar, possession or change of voice.

\item Ch 1: Does not appear; the wheel, the hollow seat and his objecting are held for Chapter 2.

\item Ch 2: At first light stood at the wheel with slip-coloured forearms and the bent finger, told the pot the slip was too thick and it would crack at the shoulder, and went quiet when the levy was spoken of. When Sella said the boy would come under the roof he said \emph{he’s not Vail}, did not look at her, and was not answered. On the third day sat in the hollow seat as the boy was carried in, obeyed Sella’s instruction about the damper before she had finished, told a pot \emph{you’ll do}, spoke once to Tarn about a rasp, and never addressed the child. Nobody wrote the foundling as Vail.

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 4: Days 5 and 6. At the wheel with slip dried to old bone on both forearms and the bent little finger, speaking to the pots and not to the boy, obeying Sella before she had finished and shifting the damper before she had finished again. At dusk came in from the back room with slate dust worked into the forearms --- grey and fine, not slip --- and said \emph{the back room’s cold} to nobody, answering no question about where he had been and giving Sella nothing to take further. Garl’s coat kept its salt shape on its peg and his hollow seat stayed unfilled; he did not look at the basket.

Shifted the damper before Sella had finished telling him the fire was low and went quieter when the levy was spoken around. Did not say the back room was cold, did not take up Sella’s silence, and kept \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed while the foundling went on being carried under the roof unwritten.

Told a pot \emph{you’ll do} and \emph{the shoulder’s thick; I’ll thin it}, and told the wheel it did not care whose hands, only if they were steady. Shifted the damper before Sella had finished telling him the fire was low and left the end of her sentence where it was, the bent finger going in ahead of his hand. Did not say the back room was cold, did not look toward the basket or the bed, and went quieter when the levy, the uncalled debt and the reading were spoken around. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed as it had been on the hour it was spoken.

On Stone 22 worked at the wheel turning a pot nobody would look at twice. On Stone 23, after five clean mornings, came in with fine grey slate dust worked into the creases of his forearms past the bend of the little finger, said nothing about where he had been, told the pot \emph{she’ll want a thinner slip} and the wheel \emph{it doesn’t care whose hands; it cares if they’re steady}, and took the damper ahead of Sella’s instruction; a pot set down on the bench gave nothing and he did not look toward the bed. On Stone 25 the forearms were clean of dust again and he said the shoulder was thick and he would thin it. On Stone 27 spoke to a pot and the damper and let the thaw argument go over him. On Stone 28 told a pot it would do and moved the damper ahead of Sella. On Stone 29 the sweeping talk made him quieter and the yard straightened; he moved the damper before she had finished, did not say the back room was cold, and did not look toward the bed, and the boy knew he could hear the full note of a Vail pot before it left the wheel and would not say so before a kiln-master. On Stone 30 he had moved the damper and not said the back room was cold. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed all ten days.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

On Ilmen 1 worked the slip toward the thaw and the slip pits with the same forearms and the same silence. It cares if they’re steady}), told a pot \emph{You’ll do} in a voice with no welcome in it and no unkindness, and when Sella’s voice went low and unfinished at the hearth his bent finger went into the cold damper ahead of her hand and held until the sentence reached \emph{feeding} and the end was given to the pot, then moved the tongue a hair’s breadth and was left standing — a remembered repetition, not a change made again, not stood up with the Day 161, 166 or 171 changes into a rule (T062). The iron stayed one piece with two bites, the holding and the taking, with no word in Grathic for both mercies, joined to no kiln and entered in no slate. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed as tightly as on the hour it was spoken, and the promise of the boy’s name to the men who burn slates was neither given nor withdrawn; the claim gathered interest in the rooms he went into and he did not pay it and did not refuse it, which in this district is a way of keeping a thing alive. He did not ask about the ear and Tarn did not ask about the room; the two silences stayed unjoined. No new scar, possession or change of voice. Forward, not closed.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 64: Days 243, 244 and 245, Smoke 4–6, Fourthday to Sixthday, on stage at the wheel-shed edge, the cold damper, the kiln mouth, the drying racks and the Clay Yard on all three days. Came through with the day’s meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent little finger and under the nails, white in the creases where a fist had opened, not bone-coloured slip; parted dust from slip as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, kept dusty and clean forearms on one tray and asked neither which slate had been broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, while the broken birth-slates under the lowest rack were entered by nobody (T009/T013/T092). Three or more men unnamed went low into the finger’s-width-open back room before first grey on all three mornings and got no name from him, and he did not say the room was cold; the two tellings of the room shut in the war stayed two with no third (T035/T031, T065/T095). Spoke to the wheel before he spoke to any person — \emph{It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady} — told a pot \emph{You’ll do} in a voice with no welcome in it and no unkindness either, knew its full note three turns before it left his hands with air under it and a want in it, and withheld the knowing on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them, advanced and not paid (T061/T082). The three shapings of the pot saying stood as sayings — sings itself out early, not heard from since, gone quiet on every row come the thaw — and on Smoke 6 a wrong wind off High Kiln brought the sweet edge of lead glaze over the boards, touched the fold and went out on the wind that brought it; he let one of the sayings stand again as a saying, made no lesson of the green, lost no pot and gave no name to what ailed the man carried out on Day 188 (T064 held, T077). The burned-slate word held at four tellings out of Slate Row, still a direction arrived nowhere and still not a third telling of the counting room shut in the war; the row question stood on its seventh place with four askings, no owner, room, hand at the kiln, cause, witness or row named, and he did not claim it, supply a witness or make a cause of it (T101 carried). When Sella’s sentence went low and unfinished at the hearth his bent finger went into the cold iron of the damper ahead of it, took the cold out of the fingertip, held until the end of the sentence arrived at the pot, moved a hair’s breadth and was left standing — a remembered repetition and not a change made again, paired with no other fraction. The iron stayed one piece with two bites, the holding and the taking, with no word in Grathic for both mercies, joined to no kiln and entered in no slate (T062). He did not ask about the ear while Tarn did not ask about the room, and the two silences stayed unjoined. \emph{He’s not Vail} stayed sealed as tightly as on the hour it was spoken, and the promise of the boy’s name to the men who burn slates was neither given nor withdrawn. The dressed grain stayed covered under wool with no figure and the returning-line place went around with a look and no number; the ninth record-first hand seen at the well stayed on its own tray in the boy’s file and was joined to nothing here. No new scar, possession or change of voice, no bond paid or spoken.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

The three shapings of the pot saying stood as sayings — sings itself out early, not heard from since, gone quiet on every row come the thaw — and on Smoke 8 a wrong wind off High Kiln brought the sweet edge of lead glaze over the boards, touched the fold and went out on the wind that brought it; he let one of the sayings stand again as a saying, made no lesson of the green, lost no pot and gave no name to what ailed the man carried out on Day 188 (T064 held). \textbf{The fourth Grain asking became a fifth on Smoke 8:} a voice with no owner, room, hand at the kiln or cause asked over the boards which row the pot went quiet on; the weather answered first, the price of barley after it, the voice went off up the terrace and the row stood where it stood with nobody leaning in to take the answer down. set him on his bed under the roof, left the thread frozen and unwiped, and went to her own bed before the small hours; no new scar, possession or change of voice}\CRfield{First seen}{Chapter 1}}{\CRsheetheading{Appearance}
A broad woman of thirty-three with forearms the colour of dried slip and a burn across the back of her left hand shaped like a little door --- two straight sides, a lintel and a threshold, the skin inside it puckered and pale --- which she keeps half-closed when she carries a cup, and which closes on nothing when her hand has nothing to hold. She is not tall and she does not make herself tall; she takes up room by being impossible to move. Her hair is coal-black with one grey streak at the temple that she says came from the winter Garl died and will not discuss further. She smells of woodsmoke, wet wool, and under it the faint sour mineral tang of the Ash ridge along the skirting board, which she has not swept in two years and does not intend to sweep. Her hands are never still. When they have nothing to do they count: spoons, nails, the breaths of a sleeping child. She wears her widow’s mark on a cord at her throat, a thumb-length of lead-glazed clay with the Vail kiln scratched into it, and she touches it before she opens the kiln and never at any other time. People notice the burn first and the mark last, which is the order she prefers.

\CRsheetheading{Voice \& Manner}
Grathic proverbs and half-sentences, practical instruction addressed to the pot or the fire before it is addressed to a person. She says \emph{the house} where another woman would say \emph{I}, and \emph{the boy} where another would say \emph{my son}. She never finishes a sentence that would require her to say what she feels, and she is not unaware of this; she has simply decided that a thing said aloud becomes a thing the Court can enter. Her humour is dry and costs her something. When she is angry she gets quieter, and the quieter she gets the more the household straightens up.

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item “The fire doesn’t know you’re sorry. Feed it.” --- said to the fire on Ilmen 25, Y.H. 814, at the going of the light; never to the basket, never as a rebuke and never with a name under it.

\item “Don’t set that near the door. You’ll pay for it in the thaw.”

\item “He’s a boy. He’s warm. That’s the whole of what I know.”

\item “You can ask me what you like. I won’t answer it. Ask the pot instead; it’s more use.”

\item “A slate-name with no house is a coat anybody can wear. I’ve seen it before.”

\item “The boy comes under the roof on the morrow. The house will keep him.” --- the taking announced without an \emph{I} in it, and never explained.

\item “Don’t set that near the door. You’ll pay for it in the thaw.” --- instruction to the pot, not to a person, given with the kiln already open.

\item “The house will keep it.” --- said to the fire at the going of the light on Reed 18 where another woman would have said \emph{I}; the instruction always goes to the wool, the pot, the broom and the fire and never to the basket.

\end{itemize}

\CRsheetheading{History}
She was born in Low Kiln to slip-mixers, married Garl Vail at seventeen, and kept the Vail fire ever since in the way a widow keeps a wound clean: daily, without comment, with a hand that knows exactly how much pressure the thing will bear. She bore two children. Jorra, who lived, and Enna, who died at nine months of the second chill in Y.H. 804, after Alda Reed had warmed the stone and done everything the craft knew. Sella sat up with that child for three nights and learned what the midwives already knew: that a vessel can cool while everybody is being kind to it. In Y.H. 811, in the Long Cold, Garl died with the river iced and no collector able to cross, and his warmth went where unkept warmth goes. The Ash in the Vail corner is thicker than in any other house in the district. Sella has never swept it and has never said why.

On Stone 7, Y.H. 812, a woman in the district bore a child with a branching red flower across his ribs, and Sella took him in on the third day. She gave as her reason the one she has given ever since: a foundling with no house-name can be used by anyone, and a boy entered under a roof is a boy nobody can take for a levy without answering to that roof. This is true. It is not the whole of it. Alda Reed, who delivered him, crossed herself at the birth-flower and told nobody what she had seen, and Sella, who saw the same look on the midwife’s face, asked her nothing at all. She has kept the boy close for three years and has never once asked where his memory came from. She is waiting to see what he will become.

\CRsheetheading{Wounds \& Fears}
Enna’s second chill; Garl going uncollected; the Ash ridge that has grown an inch since. She fears another Long Cold, and fears more than that the day somebody from Slate Row notices that one child in her house listens to the fire before he looks at it. She fears Jorra, who has begun to disappear into the back rooms with men whose names are not spoken, and she fears that she has already lost the wheel to him while he still stands at it. Her contradiction is the whole of her: the woman who feeds every hungry child in the yard has never once said she loves one. She would sooner swallow the widow’s mark.

\CRsheetheading{Desires}
She wants the fire to hold, the wheel to stay in the house, and a Vail name written on the birth-slate of every child born under her roof. She thinks she wants a whole return for Garl, so that he might come back as himself and sit where he used to sit and say nothing in his own voice. What she needs is to admit that she did not take Corin in for the house at all. She took him because he was the only warm thing in a room full of people pretending not to be cold, and because she had already lost one child to the second chill and could not bear to lose another to an explanation.

\CRsheetheading{Bonds}
\textbf{Ch 123 (bonds).} With Corin nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road across Ilmen 26, 27 and 28 as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and the figure offered at the well was not brought under the roof as a teaching or told a second time on a day that had earned only its twenty-seventh or twenty-eighth. She came to the hearth before the basket at both ends of every day, told the coals it was the thaw in the voice another woman would use for a child who could not hear her, turned them with the back of a broken pot, gave the small intake, the hold and the letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, kept her finger above the unread charcoal, lips on a two-gapped row, one glance at the clay jar standing cold under lead glaze beyond the pot board with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn on the back of her left hand closing on air. She lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the tighter wire crossed the crack, left the hairline showing between old-brass staple and wire, gave both proverbs to the pot and the fire and never to a person, kept repair apart from restoration, turned the dressed grain under wool with a touch lighter than a woman would use on a sleeping child and with no figure or handful, and set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up the nineteen steps at the half-pace, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind, the pot, the fire and the banked fire and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places once and not twice, widest at the returning-line place, set him under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and added no second fold; the keeping at the fold was found where put and stayed a finding. \textbf{The widow’s mark hung where it hangs on all three days} — a morning, a hearth, a shelf, a pot, a yard, a well, a basket and a going of the light are not openings, seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule and no eighth came due. She did not make the offered figure a price, a reader, a witness or a payment, and did not join it to the asking that came up at the well on the twenty-third or to the softening under the river’s skin. With Tarn six stood where the house could check and the seventh at the lip with \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} found where put and not made a habit; with Jorra her unfinished sentence still arrived at the pot through the bent finger in the cold damper, taken out without the extra holding of Ash 26 a second time, and \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed. Garl stayed in objects with his name unspoken 420, 421 and 422 days and his tile debt uncalled, his coat on the peg, his hollow seat and the twice-mended pot’s hairline keeping the house in his shape. No bond changed hands, no new scar or possession and no change of voice.

She said nothing of the figure gone twice over a basket, of the man whose slate had gone down the road with the writing turned away, of the asking that came up at the well on the twenty-third or of the softening nobody owned; the well gave back the weather and she gave it no teaching. On Ilmen 25 she said \emph{The fire doesn’t know you’re sorry. Feed it} to the fire and to no basket, with no name and no payer standing under it. With Tarn six stood where the house could check and the seventh at the lip beside Garl’s unforged collector sentence, his hand over blade and sill and away; the sentence was found where put and not made a habit, the loan uncalled in an ended term. With Jorra her unfinished sentence still reached the pot through the bent finger in the cold damper and came out without the extra holding of Ash 26. Garl stayed in the hairline of the pot and the hollow wheel-seat, his name unspoken 417, 418 and 419 days while the fire’s fifth went unpaid the same number. No new scar or possession, no change of voice, nothing paid, forgiven, named or ended; forward, not closed.

Before first grey on Ilmen 6 three or more men unnamed went low into the room off the wheel-shed; she gave them no name and did not say the room was cold, and when a man from Slate Row whose name was on no roll stood at the yard’s edge with his hands loose she carried him down at the half-pace and went wide around the seven places and said no word to him, no loaf passing and no slate shown (T035/T031/T080 advanced, not paid). With Tarn the sixth piece at the kindling stood where the house could check and the seventh at the lip beside the unforged collector sentence, \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count}, the loan uncalled at the end of a term already ended and the head not turned toward the landing; with Jorra her unfinished sentence arrived at the pot through the bent finger standing in the cold damper, and the promise under the shed was neither given nor withdrawn. Garl stayed in his objects with his name unspoken 399, 400 and 401 days, the fire’s fifth unpaid the same number. No new scar or possession and no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 115 (bonds).} With Corin nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road across Ilmen 2, 3 and 4 as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer: the household went back to its grammar as though nothing had turned and the new year’s first arithmetic waited for Ilmen 10, unbrought. She came to the hearth before the basket at both ends of every day, told the coals it was the thaw in the voice another woman would use for a child who could not hear her, turned them with the back of a broken pot, gave a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, kept her finger along the top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal tally stayed unread, moved her lips on a two-gapped row unfigured, glanced once at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the tighter wire crossed the crack with the hairline showing between old-brass staple and new binding and said both proverbs to the pot and the fire and never to a person, kept repair apart from restoration as a surgeon keeps a graft apart from a cure, turned the dressed grain under wool with a touch lighter than a woman would use on a sleeping child and with no figure or handful, and set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up the nineteen steps at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind, the pot, the fire and the banked fire and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places once and not twice, widest around the returning-line place, and set him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and added no second fold. \textbf{The keeping, advanced and NOT paid (T097/T060/T086):} the wool was found folded where put on the three mornings and at the three goings of the light, no third crust, name, gift, payment or payer.
