Garl is kept to the very last day in objects and not in a story — salt coat holding a broader man’s shape, hollow seat with its leftward lean, clean dark line and finer grey unswept, proverb gone to the pot, debt against the tiles uncalled and worse for being uncalled — no lesson made, no collector called, his name unspoken for two hundred and nine days. On Day 209 she carries him down to the Cross, sets the basket in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade where no slate lay, stands half a pace off through Berr’s third reading and the bell’s four, four and a gap, gives no instruction or reason to the basket and carries him home at the going of the light saying nothing of what was read over him. The fire answers four low pulls with the fifth missing and its payer unnamed for two hundred and seven, eight and nine days while the river keeps its note through the door and the boards keep their knot — three counts in three places that do not become one. Her unfinished sentence at the hearth is allowed to finish at the pot behind Jorra’s bent finger as a remembered repetition; the two silences stay unjoined and Ember goes out without a boundary drawn.

\textbf{Ch 53.} Through Days 210–212, Grain 1–3, the house keeps the turning of the month the way it keeps the fire: without a boundary drawn, without a figure spoken and without correcting either of the district’s two names for the months. Ember thins into the ordinary tending of a year begun and the yard goes around its left places — the clean dark line and the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space under the lowest rack with its broken birth-slates, the pan’s gone round ring, the bare trough whose water is called weather, the field’s empty place and the place the carriers crossed — with a look and a wide step and no number. Garl is kept in objects and not in a story: the salt coat holds a broader man’s shape, the seat its hollow and leftward lean, the proverb has gone to the pot and the debt against the tiles is circled without a name, worse for being uncalled, with no lesson made and no collector called and his name unspoken for two hundred and twelve days. Sella gives the instruction to everything but the basket, says \emph{the house}, keeps the half-pace and the two inches, moves her lips along a row standing with two unnamed gaps and gives nobody a figure, keeps her finger on top of the shelf’s front edge so the charcoal stays unread, glances once at the cold clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing without a touch, tells the fire it is the thaw and says \emph{The house will keep it}, and does not look toward the bed at the setting. The widow’s mark hangs where it hung at a shelf, a well, a yard, a basket and a dusk, because none is an opening and there has been no opening since before the kiln on Ember 1. Cost-questions go to the pot and the weather and arrive nowhere; a number in a fist goes back into a coat with nothing paid. The fire answers four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for two hundred and ten, eleven and twelve days. Forward, not closed.

\textbf{Ch 54.} Through Days 213–215, Grain 4–6, the house keeps the first working week of Grain the way it keeps the fire: without an entry, without correcting either of the district’s two month-names, and with no market and no Account-day until Grain 10 (Day 219). She comes to the fire before the basket on all three mornings, gives every instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom, the running water and the river wind and never to the basket, says \emph{the house} and \emph{The house will keep it}, keeps her half-pace from every open slate, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze and shuts her hand half over nothing without a touch, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, moves her lips along a row standing with two gaps and gives nobody a figure, keeps her finger on top of the shelf’s front edge so the charcoal stays unread, tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot and stands counting under her breath toward no opening (small intake, hold, letting go). The pot rim goes out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and her hand rests a half-beat longer at the setting; on the last day she does not look toward the bed. The fire answers four low pulls with the fifth missing under the floor, its payer unnamed for two hundred and thirteen, fourteen and fifteen days, while the river’s note comes through the finger’s-width door and the boards keep their knot: three counts in three places that do not become one. The widow’s mark hangs where it hung, touched once before the kiln on Ember 1 and at no hour since — no opening in thirty-five days — and the private roll stays unshown while Dessa’s cost stays unentered. Cost-questions at the door and the well go to the pot and the weather and away level, nothing priced, refused or entered; a number in a fist goes nowhere and pays nothing. Garl is kept to every day in objects and not in a story: the salt-stiff coat with its crease at the left shoulder, the seat’s twenty-year hollow and leftward lean, the clean dark line and the finer grey called the thaw unswept, the proverb gone to a pot with no crack, and the debt against the tiles neither paid, settled nor named, worse for being uncalled, with no lesson made and no collector. When the burned-slate word goes around the boards a third time she makes nothing of it; when Jorra grows quieter the household straightens around the quiet without an order from her, and her unfinished sentence at the hearth still finishes at the pot behind his remembered finger (T058/T079, T100, T077, T009/T013/T092/T098, T035/T031/T062, T065/T095, T088). Forward, not closed.

\textbf{Ch 55.} Through Days 216–218, Grain 7–9, the house keeps the second working week the way it keeps the fire: without an entry, with no market until Grain 10, and with the same grammar of instruction to the wool, fire, pot, broom, running water and river wind and never to the basket. She comes to the fire before the basket, says \emph{the house} and \emph{The house will keep it}, keeps her half-pace and her two inches, holds her finger on top of the shelf’s front edge so the charcoal stays unread, and leaves the widow’s mark untouched for thirty-six, thirty-seven and thirty-eight days. The fire misses its fifth with its payer unnamed for two hundred and sixteen, seventeen and eighteen days; the river’s note and the boards’ knot keep three counts in three places that do not become one. A pot saying takes a third shaping and the burned-slate word a fourth telling, both directions arrived nowhere, and she joins neither to the house. Jorra’s quiet goes before him into the shed and the household straightens around it without an order; her unfinished sentence still finishes at the pot behind his remembered finger. Tarn’s ninth stopping stands with no tenth and no collector; Garl stays in objects with the tile debt uncalled. The boy is carried home at the half-pace each dusk, set on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, with the fold put right without a look at his face and the thread left frozen; the two rooms do not touch. Forward, not closed.

Through Grain 10–12 she keeps the house the way she keeps the fire: the boy carried up and down the clay road at the half-pace, set in the moot-post’s thin shade where no slate lay at Grain’s first market, and set on his bed and not in the Debt Loft each night with the fold put right without a look at his face and the thread left frozen. She gives every instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom, the running water and the river wind and never to the basket, says \emph{the house} and \emph{The house will keep it}, keeps her finger on top of the shelf’s front edge so the charcoal stays unread, moves her lips along the two-gapped row without a figure, and leaves the widow’s mark hanging where it hung through thirty-nine, forty and forty-one days without an opening. The seventh green and the seventh shape come and go across the square without reaching under her roof; nothing is explained, entered, paid or named.

Through Grain 13–18 she brings the year’s harvest under the roof in two steps and keeps both by covering: the first cut grain comes in off the strips and is set near the hearth under wool, then across Grain 16–18 it is taken out, beaten with a flail on the flagstones, winnowed on the river wind, spread thin to finish drying and poured back under the fold --- dressed and stored, counted in glances and handfuls and by the carrying arm’s weight, with no slate opened and no figure given. Every cost-question goes to the pot and the weather and arrives nowhere; a number comes up out of a fist and goes back into its sleeve. She goes around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the pan’s gone ring, the bare trough, the field’s empty place and the place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, each with a look and a wide step and no number. Her pot handle stands two inches beyond the reaching hand, her hand resting a half-beat longer at the setting and never looking toward the bed; her finger lies on top of the shelf’s front edge while her lips move along a row with two gaps, and the charcoal is not read. The widow’s mark is untouched since before the kiln on Ember 1, no opening in forty-two through forty-seven days; her private roll stays unshown, Dessa’s cost unentered, and Garl kept in objects with the tile debt uncalled. She carries him home at each going of the light without looking at his face, sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, and leaves the thread frozen. Forward into Grain 19, not closed.

Through Grain 19–21 she keeps the house in the same grammar with one more tend behind her and Grain’s second Account-day read over the basket on Day 229: she changes nothing under the roof in answer to the figure, sends cost-questions to the pot and the weather, goes wide around the yard’s places with a look and no number, and carries him home at the going of the light saying nothing of what was read over him. The dressed grain stays dressed and covered with no figure, and the returning-line place stays gone around with a look and no number; T098 advances and is not paid. The widow’s mark has now gone fifty days untouched since the opening before the kiln on Ember 1, and the rule still holds that the hand goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour. On Grain 21 she goes to her own bed before the small hours and leaves the coals to keep themselves; in the room that does not touch his her breaths go small intake, hold, letting go — a count kept toward no opening and never offered to any ear under this roof — and the wall stands between that count and his ear. She has taken in a foundling, kept a fire, held a wheel in the house through a son’s silence and a husband’s uncollected debt, and has never once said what any of it cost or asked where the boy’s memory came from. Nothing joined, named, opened, spent or ended.

Through Grain 22–24 (Days 231–233) she keeps the last tend of the harvest the way she keeps the fire: by instruction given to the tool and never to the basket, by a figure sent to the pot and the weather, and by a wide step around every place the yard has left where it lies. She turns the dressed grain for damp, spreads it thin and gathers it back under the fold, counted in glances, handfuls and the carrying arm’s weight, entered on no slate and given no figure. The second ownerless asking goes over the boards in the afternoon of Day 232 and is answered with the pot and the weather as the first was, the weather first and the price of barley after it, and the row stands where it stood. She goes around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the pan’s gone ring, the bare trough, the field’s empty place and the returning-line place, each with a look and a wide step and no number. She sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, goes to her own bed before the small hours and leaves the coals to keep themselves; in the room that does not touch his her breaths go small intake, hold, letting go, a count kept toward no opening and never offered to any ear under this roof. She has taken in a foundling, kept a fire, held a wheel in the house through a son’s silence and a husband’s uncollected debt, and has never once said what any of it cost or asked where the boy’s memory came from. Nothing joined, named, opened, spent or ended.

She goes around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, goes to her own bed before the small hours of Day 236 and leaves the coals to keep themselves; in the room that does not touch his her breaths go small intake, hold, letting go, a count kept toward no opening and never offered to any ear under this roof. She has taken in a foundling, kept a fire, held a wheel in the house through a son’s silence and a husband’s uncollected debt, and has never once said what any of it cost or asked where the boy’s memory came from. Nothing joined, named, opened, spent or ended.

Through Smoke 1–3 (Days 240–242) she keeps the house the way she keeps the fire: instruction to the wool, fire, pot, broom, running water and river wind and never to the basket, \emph{the house} and \emph{The house will keep it}, the half-pace from every open slate, the jar-glance without a touch, the hand shut half over nothing, the burn-wrist pushing coal-black hair back so the grey streak shows pale, the finger on top of the shelf’s front edge so the charcoal stays unread, the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, lips along the two-gapped row with no figure, cost-questions to the pot and the weather. \textbf{The one change in these days was hers:} before the first firing of Smoke she went to the kiln mouth, put her hand to the widow’s mark, held it one breath, let go, lifted the clay lid with the back of a hand and tipped the carried coal under a broken pot; the fire took with its fifth still missing and no payer named, nobody praised what it mended and nobody saw it, and she put it behind the household without a word. She did not touch the mark again at any shelf, well, rack, road, basket, afternoon or dusk in three days, because the hand goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour, as on Tallow 1 and Ember 1. The dressed grain was turned under wool for damp, spread thin and gathered back by the handful, changed in state and given no figure, entered on no slate and laid across none of the absences. A wrong wind off High Kiln on Smoke 3 brought the sweet edge of glaze over the boards, touched the fold and went out on it, and she let one of the three sayings stand as a saying with no fourth likeness made a cause. She carried him home each evening around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, set him on his bed under the roof, left the thread frozen and went to her own bed before the small hours. No new scar or possession, no bond changed hands, and the private roll stayed unshown.

Through Smoke 4–6 (Days 243–245) she keeps the house the way she keeps the fire: instruction to the tool and never to the basket, \emph{the house}, the half-pace, the jar-glance, the hand shut half over nothing, the unread charcoal under the shelf’s front edge, the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, and cost-questions sent to the pot and the weather. Through Smoke 13–15 (Days 252–254) she keeps the house the way she keeps the fire: instruction to the wool, fire, pot, broom, running water and river wind and never to the basket, \emph{the house} and \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say \emph{I}, the half-pace from every open slate, the jar-glance with the hand shut half over nothing, the finger on top of the shelf’s front edge so the charcoal stays unread, the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and cost-questions sent to the pot and the weather with nothing priced. On Smoke 14 a pot set down wrong at the racks gives its high thin note before its time and a woman sweeps around it with a practical word about the slip, making no cause of the sound; a wrong wind off High Kiln brings the sweet edge of lead glaze over the boards and takes it out again. The fire answers four low pulls with a missing fifth, its payer unnamed for two hundred and fifty-two, fifty-three and fifty-four days. No new scar or possession, no bond changed hands, no opening made after the first.

Through Smoke 16–18, Days 255–257, the keeping goes on in the same grammar and makes one small domestic change she does not name. She comes to the fire before the basket on all three mornings, gives every instruction to the wool, fire, pot, broom, running water and river wind and never to the basket, says \emph{the house} and \emph{The house will keep it}, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, counts under her breath toward no opening, and keeps her finger on top of the shelf’s front edge so the charcoal stays unread. On Smoke 18 she gives the instruction to the bucket and the fire and never the basket, goes around the trough with a look and a wide step, and lets the yard call the white frost on the well lip weather, because a well is not an opening. The widow’s mark hangs where it hung, touched once before the kiln on Smoke 1 and at no hour since; the one opening stays behind the household with no lesson and no payer, and the next real opening is the first firing of Frost, far off and unbrought. At the going of the light on Smoke 18 she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face, leaves the thread frozen and goes to her own bed. The wall has acquired no door.

Through Smoke 19–21 she keeps the house the way she keeps the fire: to the fire before the basket on all three mornings, instruction to the wool, fire, pot, broom and river wind and never to the basket, \emph{the house} where another woman would say \emph{I}, the half-pace from every open slate, the jar-glance with the hand shut half over nothing, coal-black hair pushed back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, her finger on top of the shelf’s front edge so the charcoal stays unread, the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. Through Smoke 22–24, Days 261–263, she keeps the house the way she keeps the fire, and the keeping is made as much of what she leaves undone as of what she does. She comes to the fire before the basket on all three mornings, tells the coals it is the thaw, turns them with the back of a broken pot, says \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say \emph{I}, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, keeps her finger on top of the shelf’s front edge so the charcoal stays unread, moves her lips along a two-gapped row without giving either gap a figure, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing, and sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She lifts a corner of the wool over the dressed grain for damp on the 22nd and 23rd and turns it under the wool on the 24th, each with no figure, so the arithmetic on Smoke 30 will not know what it cost. Through Smoke 25–27, Days 264–266, she keeps the house through the third working week’s going out: fire before basket, the thaw told to the coals, the back of a broken pot, \emph{The house will keep it}, the count under her breath toward no opening, the finger on top of the shelf’s front edge with the charcoal unread, the two-gapped row without a figure, the glance at the clay jar and the hand shut half over nothing, the pot handle two inches out with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carries him at the half-pace, goes wide around the seven places, sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face and leaves the thread frozen. Through Frost 1–3, Days 270–272, she keeps the house the way she keeps the fire, and in the first light of Frost 2 she performs the month’s one real opening. On the other mornings she tells the coals it was the thaw, turns them with the back of a broken pot, says \emph{The house will keep it}, counts under her breath toward no opening, keeps her finger above the charcoal, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, turns the dressed grain beneath the wool for damp with a progressively lighter touch and gives it no figure, carries him at the half-pace, goes wide around the seven places and sets him on his bed under the roof with the thread frozen. Through Frost 4–6, Days 273–275, she keeps the house through the week of going around, and in the middle of it makes the chapter’s one change without a word. She comes to the fire before the basket each morning, tells the coals it was the thaw, turns them with the back of a broken pot, says \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say \emph{I}, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, keeps her finger on top of the shelf’s front edge, moves her lips along a two-gapped row without giving either gap a figure, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing, and sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, a half-beat at the setting and no look toward the bed. On Frost 5 her finger goes beneath the shelf’s front edge and stays for two counted breaths where on Day 166 it stayed for one, and comes away without a look, a word or a going back — a change a house can make and say nothing about (T100 advanced, not paid). She turns the dressed grain under wool for damp on all three mornings with a progressively lighter touch and gives it no figure; she goes wide around the seven walked-around places and sets him on his bed under the roof with the thread frozen. The widow’s mark hangs where it hangs, touched once before the kiln on Frost 2 and at no shelf, well, rack, road, basket, yard, morning, hearth, afternoon, dusk or going of the light on Frost 4, 5 or 6; the first firing of Frost stays behind the household with no lesson or payer and four openings remain four. Nothing is settled by the week’s going out and the count goes into Frost 7 unspent.

Through Frost 7–9, Days 276–278, she keeps the house through the week’s going out, and on the last morning makes the chapter’s one change as maintenance and gives nobody a figure. She comes to the fire before the basket each morning, tells the coals it was the thaw, turns them with the back of a broken pot, says \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say \emph{I}, counts under her breath toward no opening, keeps her finger on top of the shelf’s front edge with the charcoal unread, moves her lips along a two-gapped row without giving either gap a figure, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing, and sets the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. The white the frost wrote on the well lip on Frost 8 does not go with the sun as it went on Frost 4, and stays past noon, past the going of the light and onto Frost 9; the rope stiffens, the trough takes a skin and she banks the coals an hour earlier at the going of the light, and the yard calls all of it weather. On Frost 9 she goes to the trough with the back of the broken pot, presses the skin until it gives with a thin dry sound, lifts a plate of ice clouded with silt, sets it on a flat stone out of the path of feet and draws what the yard calls weather, telling the weather where to stand and giving nobody a figure (T083/T085 advanced, not paid). She turns the dressed grain a second time that morning because the stone has gone cold, lifts the wool with a lighter touch and gives no figure, so the arithmetic that will read over it tomorrow will not know what it cost (T077). She goes wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, sets him on his bed under the roof each dusk and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face and leaves the thread frozen. The widow’s mark hangs where it hangs, touched once before the kiln on Frost 2 and at no shelf, well, rack, road, basket, yard, morning, hearth, afternoon, dusk or going of the light on Frost 7, 8 or 9, because none is an opening; the first firing of Frost stays behind the household with no lesson or payer and four openings remain four. Nothing is settled by the week’s going out and the count goes into Frost 10 unspent.

Through Frost 10–12, Days 279–281, she keeps the house the way she keeps the fire, and the month’s first reading passes the roof without leaving a figure behind. On Frost 10 she carries him to the Cross, sets the basket in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade where no slate lay and stands half a pace off through the reading and the bell, giving no instruction or reason to the basket, and carries him home at the going of the light saying nothing. The arithmetic changed for the month up the road in Berr’s locked box and cannot be changed back, while the printed one in twelve stands unchallenged and the figure read is still not the figure paid; nothing of it comes back under the roof as a lesson, a mending, a figure or a payment. On Frost 11 and 12 she turns the dressed grain under wool for damp with a lighter touch and gives it no figure, so the number that read over it does not know what it cost, and the space between figure and price stays unsigned (T077). The grammar holds exactly — fire before basket, instruction to the tools and never the basket, \emph{the house}, \emph{The house will keep it}, half-pace, pot rim two inches out, fold righted without a look, finger above the charcoal, lips along a two-gapped row, one glance at the clay jar and the hand shut half over nothing, the widow’s mark untouched because no hour among these days is an opening. The stayed frost, the plate of ice and the week’s small goings-around are called weather and entered nowhere (T083/T085 held), the fire’s fifth stays unsupplied with its payer unnamed for three more days (T088), and Frost 20 stands eight mornings ahead and unbrought. Nothing is opened, named, called, paid or ended.

Through Frost 13–15, Days 282–284, she keeps the house the way she keeps the fire, and the second working week settles nothing. She comes to the hearth before the basket each morning, tells the coals it was the thaw, turns them with the back of a broken pot, says \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say \emph{I}, keeps her finger above the charcoal so the tally beneath stays unread, moves her lips along a two-gapped row without a figure, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing, and sets the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She goes wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, turns the dressed grain under wool for damp and gives it no figure, carries him at the half-pace and sets him on his bed under the roof with the fold righted and the thread frozen. The widow’s mark hangs where it hangs at every morning, afternoon and going of the light, because none is an opening; the first firing of Frost stays behind the household with no lesson or payer and four openings remain four. The stayed frost, the skinned trough and the plate of ice are called weather and entered nowhere, and the fire’s fifth stays unsupplied with its payer unnamed for two hundred and eighty-four days. Frost 20 stands five mornings ahead and unbrought, and nothing is opened, named, called, paid or ended.

Through Bone 10–12, Days 309–311, she keeps the house the way she keeps the fire, and the month’s first reading passes the roof without leaving a figure behind. On the tenth she carries him to the Cross, sets the basket in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade where no slate lay and stands half a pace off through the twice-read figure and the bell, and carries him home at the going of the light saying nothing. The arithmetic changed for the month up the road in Berr’s locked box and cannot be changed back, while the printed one in twelve stands unchallenged, the figure read is still not the figure paid, four readings are four and not one account, and a rule made from them would want a payer where none stood. Through the eleventh and twelfth her grammar holds exactly: fire before basket, instruction to the wool, the wind, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, the charcoal unread, the two gaps unfigured, the twice-mended pot lifted with the thumb on the wire and the crack showing, the pot rim two inches out, the dressed grain turned under wool with a lighter touch and no figure, and the widow’s mark touched at no hour. Five openings in five months are five and not a rule; the seven walked-around places go around with a look and no number, and the skinned trough and silt-clouded plate stay weather entered nowhere. The carried fire’s fifth is unpaid three hundred and eleven days with its payer unnamed. Bone 20 stands five mornings ahead and is not brought early. Nothing is joined, named, opened, called, paid or ended, and no lesson is made of the reading.

Through Bone 22–24, Days 321–323, she keeps the house the way she keeps the fire, and the chapter’s one movement is a domestic testing that says nothing and is not repeated. She comes to the hearth before the basket at both ends of every day, tells the coals it was the thaw, turns them with the back of a broken pot, says \emph{The house will keep it}, counts small intake, hold and letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, keeps her finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stays unread, moves her lips along a two-gapped row with neither gap figured, glances once at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with her hand half over nothing, lifts the twice-mended pot with the thumb first where the wire crosses the crack and both proverbs to the pot and the fire with the crack showing, turns the dressed grain under wool with a lighter touch and no figure, sets the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, righted the fold without looking at his face and leaves the thread. On Bone 22 at the rack end she lifts the wool from the dressed grain, takes a small handful and lets it fall back through her fingers onto the heap instead of spreading it — a hand testing dryness — with no word, no figure and no repetition; on Bone 23 and 24 her fingers go in and come out without closing and she makes no show of not repeating it. She carries him down and up at the half-pace from every open slate, gives the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket, and goes wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number. The three coverings stay weather entered nowhere, the month’s hunts and repairs stay directions judged by the carrying arm and the weather, and the widow’s mark hangs where it hangs at every morning, rack, well, yard, hearth and bed, because none is an opening and five openings in five months are five and not a rule. With Tarn the exact account of six and the seventh goes unremarked and his stroke over the bright patch without the half-check asks no question from her; with Jorra the men unnamed before first grey, the dust and the bent finger standing in the cold damper ahead of her unfinished sentence go unasked about. Ilva at the well on Bone 23 keeps her count in wood and answers the question put; nothing comes from that well under the roof as lesson, figure, mending, cause or payment. Garl’s name is unspoken three hundred and twenty-three days and his tile debt uncalled. Nothing is opened, joined, named, called, paid or ended.

\item Ch 123: Through Ilmen 26, 27 and 28 nothing crossed under the roof, out of the yard or up the clay road as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and the offer made at the well was not made a teaching under the roof, repeated on a day that had earned only its twenty-seventh or twenty-eighth or told a second time. She came to the hearth before the basket at both ends of every day, told the coals it was the thaw in the voice another woman would use for a child who could not hear her, turned them with the back of a broken pot, gave the small intake, the hold and the letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, kept her finger above the unread charcoal, lips on a two-gapped row, one glance at the clay jar standing cold under lead glaze beyond the pot board with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn on the back of her left hand closing on air. She lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the tighter wire crossed the crack, left the hairline showing between old-brass staple and wire, gave both proverbs to the pot and the fire and never to a person, kept repair apart from restoration, turned the dressed grain under wool with a touch lighter than a woman would use on a sleeping child and with no figure or handful, and set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up the nineteen steps at the half-pace, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind, the pot, the fire and the banked fire and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places once and not twice, widest at the returning-line place, set him under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and added no second fold. \textbf{The widow’s mark hung where it hangs on all three days} — a morning, a hearth, a shelf, a pot, a yard, a well, a basket and a going of the light are not openings, seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule and no eighth came due. At the yard well on Ilmen 26 a woman waiting her turn offered a figure to Ilva’s strip and took it back into her sleeve; Sella was not there to see it and no figure came under this roof, no reader was made of the count in wood and nothing was paid, priced or joined. She said nothing of it at either end of any day, and nothing of the softening under the river’s skin that the yard called weather. With Tarn six stood where the house could check and the seventh at the lip, \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} found where put on all three days and not a custom; with Jorra her unfinished sentence still arrived at the pot through the bent finger in the cold damper, taken out without the extra holding of Ash 26 a second time, and \emph{he’s not Vail} stayed sealed with the promise neither given nor withdrawn. Garl stayed in objects with his name unspoken 420, 421 and 422 days and his tile debt uncalled. No new scar or possession, no change of voice; forward, not closed.

\end{itemize}

\item Ch 114: Days 393, 394 and 395 — the Remembering and the Last Day, Y.H. 813, and Ilmen 1, Y.H. 814, Firstday — the last two of the Five and the turn of a year that opened with nothing signed. Fire before basket at both ends of every day; coals told the thaw and turned with the back of a broken pot; \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say I; a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured; finger on top of the loaf shelf with the charcoal unread; lips on a two-gapped row unfigured; one glance at the clay jar under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air; the twice-mended pot lifted thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack with the hairline showing between old-brass staple and tighter wire and both proverbs to pot and fire and never to a person; dressed grain turned under wool with no figure and no handful; the pot rim set two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up the nineteen steps at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind and the fire and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places once and not twice, and at each going of the light set him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and added no second fold. On the Remembering she carried him to House Silt on an errand, set the basket just inside the finger’s-width door away from every open slate, took what she came for and went without opening the tin above the empty bed or naming the woman. On the Last Day she baked bread and left the grey in the corners; a neighbour called it dealt with because it would be burnt in the morning and she did not say it. The empty place beside the crust was left on the thirteenth, the fourteenth and the morning of the fifteenth exactly as it had been, no hand at it, no third, no name, so that the evening’s keeping would be a change and not a habit. \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, advanced and NOT paid (T097/T060/T086):} at the going of the light on the fifteenth she carried him up the nineteen steps under the Vail kiln-house roof and never into the Debt Loft, set him on the bed at the low angle of the loaf shelf, put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face, righting the wool where the cold had ridden it back — and her hand tucked the wool into the empty place beside the crust. The wool went in as a hand goes in where a thing used to be and is not, not to fill the place, which kept its shape and its emptiness both, but to leave the warmth of a hand where the cold had been. It was a small keeping: no word with it, no third crust put there, no name spoken over the place, no look toward his face, no instruction to the basket; the little-door burn on the back of her left hand closed on nothing, her hand rested the half-beat longer than the setting needed before it went away, and the thread of drool at his mouth was left frozen in the dry kiln heat and unwiped where it lay. She said nothing of where they had been. The boy took the interval apart by what was there and by what was not and filed the keeping on a place of its own beside the crust’s gap, the shelf’s two gaps, the gone pan’s round ring and the field’s empty place, expressly not a joining of rooms, not a third crust, not a gift, not a payment, no payer, not a sixth held object, not a habit or a rule, gathered once and not made again, gathering interest toward the far-off finger that is not his. \textbf{The widow’s mark was not touched on Stone 13, 14 or 15} — a morning, a hearth, a shelf, a well, a yard, a road, a going of the light and a bed are no openings — and seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule with no eighth made due. With Tarn the exact account held at six counted and the seventh at the lip beside Garl’s unforged sentence, the Ash 14 breath and Bone 26 thumb’s resting found where put and not made again, the loan uncalled; with Jorra her unfinished sentence still arrived at the pot through his bent finger in the cold damper, one iron with two bites, and the extra holding of Ash 26 was not left a second time. Ilva stood once at the well on the thirteenth with her strip unread and her ninth hand nine; Hessa came down the clay road on the fourteenth with the writing turned to her sleeve and gave no figure; Garl stayed in his objects with his name unspoken 372, 373 and 374 days and the carried fire’s fifth unpaid the same. Grey streak at the temple pale, coal-black hair pushed back with the burn-wrist. No new scar or possession, no change of voice, no bond paid. Forward, not closed.

Sella said nothing of the room, the tube, the child or the cup on the carry home, and that was not a refusal to tell him, for nobody under any roof tells a basket what a keeping is worth. \textbf{The widow’s mark was not touched on any of the three days} — a market, a well, a yard, a Drawing, a hearth and a bed are not openings, seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule and no eighth is made due. The river’s winter skin was found where put and not spent on the reading or the Drawing; the three coverings stayed weather entered nowhere with a finger between every pair; the fire’s fifth stayed unpaid and Garl’s name unspoken 369, 370 and 371 days; the four rooms with the same gap stayed apart with a finger between every pair and the Drawing’s flat knock stayed on its own place outside the six hearings. Tarn kept six in the worn thumb-mark and the seventh at the lip, found the Ash 14 breath and Bone 26 thumb’s resting where put and not made again, brought the ear-sentence to the calling word and stopped as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth, Seed 16 breath unspent and loan uncalled; Jorra parted dusty forearms from clean as clot from vessel, spoke to the wheel before any person, withheld the full note three turns ahead and put his bent finger into the cold damper with its two bites without leaving Ash 26’s extra holding a second time, \emph{he’s not Vail} sealed and the promise under the wheel-shed neither given nor withdrawn. No new scar or possession, no change of voice, no bond paid or spoken, no lesson, payment or ending. Forward, not closed.

She came to the hearth before the basket at both ends of every day, told the coals it was the thaw and \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say I, turned them with the back of a broken pot, counted a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, kept her finger on top of the loaf shelf with the charcoal unread, moved her lips along a two-gapped row unfigured, glanced once at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack with both proverbs to pot and fire and the hairline left showing, turned the dressed grain under wool with a touch lighter than a woman would use on a sleeping child and no figure or handful, and set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed. She carried him down and up at the half-pace, gave the instruction to the wool, the river wind and the fire she would bank against their coming back and never to the basket, went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number and widest around the returning-line place, and at each going of the light set him on his bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, righted the fold without a look at his face, let her hand rest the half-beat longer than the setting needed and left the thread frozen and unwiped. \textbf{The widow’s mark was not touched on Stone 1, 2 or 3}, six openings in six months being six and not a rule and no seventh made due; the kiln stood cold and its first firing on Stone 5 stood two mornings ahead as a date named to nobody. \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 93: Days 330, 331 and 332, Ash 1–3, Firstday to Thirdday, keeper of the Vail fire, on stage under the roof and in the Clay Yard on all three days and at the kiln mouth on the second. Came to the hearth before the basket at both ends of every day, told the coals it was the thaw and \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say \emph{I}, turned them with the back of a broken pot, counted a small intake, a hold and a letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, kept her finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stayed unread, moved her lips along a two-gapped row unfigured, glanced once at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, lifted the twice-mended pot with the thumb first where the wire crossed the crack and said both proverbs to the pot and the fire and never to a person, leaving the crack showing, turned the dressed grain under wool with a lighter touch and no figure and lifted no handful, set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, righted the fold at ear and chin without a look at his face and left the thread frozen and unwiped. \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, advanced and not paid (T058/T079, T088):} on Ash 2, with the kilns brought up for the dark month’s first firing, she carried the basket to the kiln mouth, set it level on the flagstones out of the draught where the heat came sideways, and before any instruction went to the basket and before any word stood over him a moment with her hands still, put her left hand to the widow’s mark at her throat — a thumb-length of lead-glazed clay with the Vail kiln scratched into it, the cord oiled where a working thumb had touched it ten thousand times, the little-door burn on the back of her left hand half-closing on the cord — held it one breath and let go, lifted the clay lid with the back of a hand and tipped the carried coal under the back of a broken pot. The fire took, answering four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should have stood, its payer unnamed three hundred and thirty-one days; nobody praised the opening, named what it mended, entered a slate or made a lesson, sign, mending, cause or payer of it, the five behind were not looked at again as signs or payments, and no seventh was made due. She did not touch the mark again at shelf, well, rack, road, basket, yard, morning, afternoon, dusk or going of the light on any of the three days, because the hand goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour. The grey streak at her temple showed pale and she pushed coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist without looking toward the bed. On all three days her fingers at the rack end went in and came out and did not close on the grain; the handful of Bone 22 stayed one object and was not made again. She carried him down and up at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot and the river wind and never to the basket, and went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number — the clean dark line and its finer grey called the thaw, the space beneath the lowest rack with its broken birth-slates, the gone pan’s round ring, the trough’s skin of ice, the field’s empty place and the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out. The three coverings — the frost gone off the well’s north lip on Bone 3, the skin on the trough breaking and closing under a pail’s knock, the silt-clouded plate of ice on the flat stone out of the path of feet — stayed weather entered nowhere with a finger between every pair and no fourth likeness made a cause. The month’s hunts and repairs stayed directions judged by the carrying arm and the weather: the Cold Acre hare answered with the weather and gone toward the clay road with nobody weighing it or opening a slate, the cracked jar in a rope sling sent to the pot, and the pot said nothing. On Ash 2 at the well Ilva drew with the pail against her knee and answered a woman’s question about the firings with \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account}, her strip unread and her ninth hand nine; nothing from that well crossed under the roof as sign, lesson, mending, cause or payment. With Tarn the exact account of six and the seventh went unremarked; with Jorra the men unnamed before first grey, the dust and the bent finger in the cold damper went unasked about and he gave the house no name for the men. On Ash 3 at the going of the light she carried him up at the half-pace, went wide around the seven places, set him on the bed under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, put the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face, let her hand rest the half-beat longer than the setting needed before it went away, left the thread where it lay and said nothing of where they had been; the small dry scrape of the loft came from above and behind earlier, with no interior entered. Garl’s name was unspoken three hundred and thirty, thirty-one and thirty-two days, his tile debt uncalled, his twice-mended pot’s crack showing and repair kept apart from restoration. Six arithmetics of the year stood behind one printed figure in Berr’s locked box, one in twelve printed and unchallenged and the figure read still not the figure paid. She wants the house kept as it is kept, with no figure spoken over what it does. No bond changed hands, no new scar or possession and no change of voice.

\end{itemize}

She carried him down and up at the half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket, and went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number — the clean dark line and its finer grey called the thaw, the space beneath the lowest rack with its broken birth-slates, the gone pan’s round ring, the trough, the field’s empty place and the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out; the stayed frost gone off the north lip, the skinned trough and the silt-clouded plate on its flat stone stayed weather entered nowhere with a finger between every pair. The month’s hunts and repairs stayed directions judged by the carrying arm and the weather: a Cold Acre hare was answered with the weather, a cracked jar in a rope sling was sent to the pot, and the pot said nothing. On Bone 30, the month’s third and last Account-day and market, she set the basket in the moot-post’s finger’s width of shade where no slate lay and stood half a pace off through Berr Clay’s twice-read figure and the bell, and carried him home at the going of the light saying nothing. In the small hours she set him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, righted the fold at his ear without a look at his face, let her hand rest the half-beat longer than the setting needed before it went away, and left the thread where it lay; a small scrape of a foot on the loft stair came from above and behind earlier, with no interior entered. She said nothing of where they had been or what had been read over the basket. No bond changed hands, no new scar or possession and no change of voice.

\end{itemize}

No new scar or possession, no change of voice, no bond changed hands.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 78: Days 285, 286 and 287, Frost 16–18, Sixthday to Eighthday, keeper of the Vail fire, on stage under the roof and in the Clay Yard on all three days. Came to the fire before the basket each morning, told the coals it was the thaw and \emph{You’ll go when you go}, turned them with the back of a broken pot, said \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say \emph{I}, counted under her breath toward no opening, pushed coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak showed pale, kept her finger on top of the loaf shelf’s front edge so the charcoal beneath stayed unread, moved her lips along a row standing with two gaps without giving either gap a figure, glanced once at the clay jar standing cold under its lead glaze and shut her hand half over nothing, and set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed (T058/T079, T100). Every instruction went to the fire, the wool, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket; she carried him at the half-pace from every open slate, went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number — the two unswept lines called thaw, the space beneath the lowest rack with its broken birth-slates, the pan’s gone ring, the skinned trough, the field’s empty place and the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out — and set him on his bed under the roof, never in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without a look at his face and left the thread frozen where it lay (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). The dressed grain lay covered and unfigured under wool at the rack end, turned for damp on the three mornings with a progressively lighter touch and given no figure, so the arithmetic that had read over it on the tenth still did not know what it cost (T077). The stayed frost lay white on the well lip past the going of the light, the trough kept its skin and the plate of ice stood clouded with silt on the flat stone out of the path of feet; she told the fire it was the thaw and gave nobody a figure (T083/T085 held, not paid). The widow’s mark hung where it hung, touched once before the kiln on Frost 2 and at no shelf, well, rack, road, basket, yard, morning, hearth, afternoon, dusk or going of the light on Frost 16, 17 or 18, because none of these was an opening; four openings in four months stayed four and not a rule, and nothing of the Frost 14 saying came under the roof as lesson, figure, mending, cause or payment (T058/T079). She heard Tarn bring the ear-sentence to the calling word and stop there on all three mornings and gave the end of her instruction to the pot, asking nothing; she did not ask Jorra about the men or his dust, and neither man named the other’s silence. Frost’s first arithmetic stayed locked in Berr’s box up the clay road with the printed one in twelve unchallenged and the figure read still not the figure paid; Frost 20 (Day 289), the second Account-day, stood two mornings beyond the close and was not brought into a day that had not earned it. No new scar or possession, no bond changed hands, no change of voice.

\end{itemize}

On the afternoon of Frost 14 she carried him down at the half-pace and up again at the going of the light while the yard well went about its small commerce; she heard nothing that made an opening and gave no instruction at any hour to the basket, and the saying that passed between two women at the well was not brought under the roof as a lesson, a joining, a cause or a figure (T080 advanced, not paid). No new scar or possession, no change of voice, no bond changed hands, no opening made and nothing paid.

Instruction went to the fire, the wool, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket; she carried at the half-pace from every open slate, went wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, set him on the bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without a look at his face and left the thread frozen. \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, advanced and not paid:} on Frost 8 the white fronds frost had written on the well lip did not go when the sun was up as they had gone on Frost 4, and stayed past noon, past the going of the light and onto Frost 9; the rope stiffened in the hand, the trough took a skin at its edges and she banked the coals an hour earlier at the going of the light, and the yard called all of it weather with nobody giving a figure (T083/T085 advanced, not paid). On Frost 9 she went to the trough with the back of the broken pot she turns the coals with, set the flat of it against the edge and pressed; the skin gave with a thin dry sound and a hairline ran out from under the pot, and she lifted a plate of ice clear at the rim and clouded where silt had risen into it, held it a moment with the water draining back in strings, and set it on a flat stone beside the well where no foot went, standing it where it would not be trodden. She drew what the yard calls weather with the pail against her knee, told the weather where to stand, gave nobody a figure and said nothing to the basket. She turned the dressed grain a second time that morning because the stone it lay on had gone cold under two days of stayed frost, lifted the wool with a lighter touch than the morning before, laid it back and gave no figure; Smoke’s third arithmetic stayed unread up the clay road in Berr’s locked box and the printed one in twelve stood unchallenged (T015/T041/T047, T077). The widow’s mark hung where it hung on its cord at her throat and her hand did not go to it at a morning, a hearth, a rack, an afternoon, a basket or a going of the light, because none was an opening and the hand goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour (T058/T079); the first firing of Frost stood behind the household with no lesson, sign, mending or payer made of it, four openings remained four and the next stood in a later month’s first firing, far off. With Tarn the loan stayed uncalled and his seventh year at its very end gave nothing; with Jorra the men went unnamed into the back room and his finger led at the damper; with Ilva no figure came off the stick and the ninth hand stayed nine; Garl’s debt stayed uncalled, Dessa dead and unnamed, Alda’s writing unasked about and Berr’s box locked. No bond paid or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

With Tarn the loan stayed uncalled and the seventh year at its very end gave nothing; with Jorra the men went unnamed into the back room and his bent finger led at the damper; with Ilva no figure came off the stick and the ninth hand stayed nine; Garl’s debt stayed uncalled, Dessa dead and unnamed, Alda’s writing unasked about and Berr’s box locked. \item Ch 63: Days 240, 241 and 242, Smoke 1–3, Firstday to Thirdday, on stage on all three days at the kiln mouth, the hearth, the loaf shelf, the bed, the drying racks, the yard well, the trough, the boards and the terrace, carrying him home each evening at the half-pace from every open slate and going wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number. Came to the fire before the basket on all three mornings; gave every instruction to the wool, fire, pot, broom, running water and river wind and never to the basket; said \emph{the house} and \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would say \emph{I}; told the fire the thaw, turned the coals with the back of a broken pot, stood counting under her breath toward no opening (small intake, hold, letting go), pushed coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak showed pale off the coals, moved her lips along the two-gapped row without giving a figure, kept her finger on top of the shelf’s front edge so the charcoal stayed unread, glanced once at the clay jar cold under its glaze and shut her hand half over nothing, set the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and set him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without a look at his face, left the thread frozen and unwiped and went to her own bed before the small hours, leaving the coals to keep themselves (T058/T079, T100). \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change, advanced and not paid:} on the morning of Smoke 1, before the basket and before any instruction, she went first to the kiln mouth; the widow’s mark hung at her throat, a thumb-length of lead-glazed clay with the Vail kiln scratched into it, and she put her hand to it, held it one breath, let go, lifted the clay lid with the back of a hand and tipped the carried coal under the back of a broken pot. The fire took, still answering four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for two hundred and forty, forty-one and forty-two days. Nobody praised what it mended and nobody saw it; no slate was entered, no lesson made, no bond changed hands and no payer named, and she put the opening behind the household without a word. She did not touch the mark again at a shelf, well, rack, road, basket, afternoon or dusk on any of the three days, because the hand goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour, as on Tallow 1 and Ember 1 (T058/T079, T088). The dressed grain was turned under wool for damp on Smoke 2 and 3, spread thin to finish and gathered back by the handful, fold set flat; it changed state and gained no figure, counted in glances, handfuls and the carrying arm’s weight that knows weight and not cost, entered on no slate and laid across none of the absences (T077). To the neighbour at the threshold with a pot on Smoke 2 and again on Smoke 3 she sent the cost-question to the pot and the weather with \emph{Ask the pot... The weather knows the rest}, nothing priced, refused or entered; a man come down the clay road with a number in his fist toward the yard well looked at it and put it back into his sleeve, so the figure arrived nowhere (T015/T041/T047 held). On Smoke 3 a wrong wind off High Kiln brought the sweet edge of lead glaze over the boards, touched the fold and went out on the wind that brought it — a direction arrived nowhere and not a second edge paid — and one of the three shapings of the pot saying stood again as a saying, no fourth likeness made a cause, no pot lost and no name given to what ailed the man carried out on Day 188 (T064 held). Her unfinished sentence at the hearth still finished at the pot behind Jorra’s remembered finger; with Tarn the two silences stayed unjoined and no collector came on the clay road; Garl was kept in objects with his name unspoken two hundred and forty, forty-one and forty-two days. No new scar, possession or change of voice; the private roll stayed unshown and Dessa’s cost unentered.

\end{itemize}

The fire answered four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for two hundred and thirty-seven, thirty-eight and thirty-nine days, while the river’s note through the finger’s-width door and the boards’ four nails, four and a thumb-width knot kept three counts in three places that do not become one (T088, T061/T082). \textbf{The dressed grain:} turned under its wool for damp on Grain 28, spread thin to finish and gathered back by the handful on Grain 29, and lay covered and unfigured near the hearth on Grain 30, counted in glances, handfuls and the carrying arm’s weight that knows weight and not cost, entered on no slate and laid across none of the absences; to the neighbour at the threshold and the woman who asked at the well she sent the question to the pot and the weather, and a man come down the clay road with a number in a fist looked at it and put it back into his sleeve, so the figure arrived nowhere (T077). Her widow’s mark hung untouched where it hung — touched once before the kiln on Ember 1 and at no hour since, no opening in fifty-seven, fifty-eight and fifty-nine days — because a shelf, a strip, a rack, a yard, a basket, a pot, an afternoon and a reading are not openings (T058/T079, T100). \textbf{On Grain 30, the third and last Account-day and market of Grain,} she carried him down at the half-pace from every open slate, set the basket in the moot-post’s thin shade where no slate lay, stood half a pace off and gave no instruction or reason to the basket, gave the wool and the river wind their words and never the basket, and carried him home at the going of the light saying nothing of what had been read over him in the square, going wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, setting him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, putting the fold right without a look at his face and leaving the thread frozen (T015/T041/T047, T058/T079). A wrong wind off High Kiln brought the sweet edge of lead glaze over the boards on Grain 29, touched the fold and went out on the wind that brought it — a direction and not a second edge paid (T064 held). Through all three days Garl stayed in objects, his name unspoken two hundred and thirty-nine days, and no collector came up or went down the clay road on Grain 28, 29 or 30 (T009/T013/T092). No new scar or possession, no change of voice, no bond changed hands; the private roll stayed unshown and the count crossed into Smoke 1 unspent.

At the going of the light each day she carried him home at the half-pace, woodsmoke before her in long low bars and river wind behind with the taste of water over water, set him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without looking at his face, left the thread frozen and unwiped, went to her own bed before the small hours and left the coals to keep themselves. No bond paid, no new scar or possession.

On Grain 21 she left the thread at his mouth frozen and unwiped, set him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, then went to her own bed before the small hours and left the coals to keep themselves; in the room that does not touch his her breaths went small intake, hold, letting go at her fire, a count kept toward no opening and never offered to any ear under this roof, and the wall stood between that count and his ear. No new scar or possession, no change of voice, no bond changed hands; she has still not said whose child he is.

With Jorra her unfinished sentence still finished at the pot behind his remembered finger and the household straightened around his quiet without an order; with Tarn the exact account held and she asked about neither his seventh year nor his ear, and no collector came on Grain 16, 17 or 18.
